361	On a TTY, wizard fields are real inline editors: arrows, Home/End,
362	Backspace and Delete edit typed text rather than inserting escape sequences.
363	Esc or Ctrl-C cancels; piped input remains line-oriented.
364	
365	The create/setup wizard asks one customization-gate question after preset
366	selection. Declining uses resolved defaults and skips detailed template,
367	README/gitignore/license/agent/skill questions; explicit customization flags or
368	a required input without a default make yes the suggested answer.
369	
370	Global recipes live in `scaffolds.toml`. Repositories may commit the allowlisted
371	`.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`, but executable project
372	configuration in those files must be trusted by its exact content hash before
373	it runs. Legacy `.dev.toml` retains its compatibility behavior.
374	
375	## Dashboard and forge inventory
376	
377	Bare `dev` / `dev tui` is the seven-view dashboard described here. It is separate
378	from the plan-first `dev flow [repo]` repository lifecycle preview above.
379	
380	The dashboard has TASKS, REPOS, FLEET, TRY, REMOTE, SKILLS and MCP views, switched
381	with tab or vim-style h/l. Wide TASKS tables show `REPO`; compact layouts keep it
382	in detail. TRY `n` creates an experiment; `space` opens metadata/lifecycle actions;
383	`a` includes retained history. Archive is a reversible same-filesystem move,
384	not deletion or disk reclamation. `?` opens the full key map.
385	
386	The initial view never waits for runtime/project-root resolution, cache decoding,
387	or shell tool probes. TASKS/REPOS/TRY publish independently from one shared local
388	cycle; optional tabs remain lazy. Refreshes are generation-scoped: late results
389	are ignored, failed refreshes keep usable rows, warning-only capability results
390	stay fresh, visible tabs resume after REPOS recovery, and valid empty results
391	clear obsolete rows. For a one-run diagnostic, set `DEV_TUI_TRACE` to an absolute new
392	file. The private bounded trace is written after TUI teardown with relative
393	startup/view timings and aggregate row counts only; it excludes names, paths,
394	commands, key values, URLs, handles and raw errors, and never enters `stats.db`
395	or a network sink. SKILLS and MCP are startup-context-first: inside Git they
396	scan only the exact current checkout plus global/user sources; outside Git they
397	reuse every accepted REPOS target and the ordinary startup directory. Skill listing uses the native versioned
398	77-agent path registry and never runs Node/`npx`; `c` hashes remote Git objects
399	without checkout filters, while mutations require a trusted direct provider and
400	are serialized. MCP inventories only sanitized static declarations for Claude
401	Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and OpenCode; only Claude's documented project
402	approvals are resolved. It never starts or health-checks a server and never
403	exposes secret-bearing values. Full detail:
404	`references/agent-capabilities.md`.
405	
406	REMOTE queries authenticated `gh` and `glab` plus configured Azure DevOps
407	organization/project targets lazily and fully paginates every repository the
408	account can access. A private cache is decoded after the first view; stale rows
409	stay searchable while refresh runs. Malformed/oversized payloads and caches
410	fingerprinted for another configured GH/GL host or Azure target are ignored.
411	GitLab uses explicit `GITLAB_HOST`/`GLAB_HOST` (default `gitlab.com`) instead of
412	cwd inference; a successful empty refresh clears obsolete rows. `/` filters
413	provider, owner/name, visibility and description, with `vis:private` for an exact
414	visibility match. Enter opens an existing local clone. For an absent remote, `c`
415	confirms; `enter` clones and stays in the dashboard, while `o` clones and opens
416	after a spinner-backed, local-only REPOS refresh. A `project_root` outside the
417	configured REPOS discovery roots/depth is rejected before mutation. `q`/Ctrl-C
418	requests cancellation without abandoning the in-flight result. Once accepted,
419	REMOTE shows `repo` and REPOS can search the clone immediately. If Git leaves a
420	destination after failure, REMOTE marks the exact path `inspect` and does not
421	delete it automatically. Use `dev repo remote [query] --json` for the non-interactive form; `--cached` avoids
422	a network query and `--refresh` forces a complete synchronization.
423	
424	`dev journal` derives calendar-day reports from Git rather than storing a
425	second history database. The default current-user report adds existing
426	session/WakaTime observations, matching task intent and recent dirty-worktree
427	snapshots, clearly separated from committed history. `auto` expands at most 100
428	commit details while retaining complete aggregates; `--max-commits 0` is
429	unlimited. Use `--author <email>` or `--all-authors` for commit-only team views,
430	and `--json` for a stable structured report. dev generates the context only; it
431	does not launch the receiving agent.
432	
433	`dev summary` is the complementary current-state view across this machine. It
434	combines durable repositories and present active/deprecated Tries with live Git,
435	worktree, task, runtime, recovery and catalog facts. The default `auto` Markdown
436	expands active work and leaves quiet projects in a compact index; `--attention`
437	selects both active work and recovery hazards, while `--json` always emits the
438	complete selected snapshot. Use journal for time ranges and `repo context` for
439	one repository.
440	
441	Azure DevOps inventory is opt-in and cloud-only:
442	
443	```toml
444	[[forge.azure_devops]]
445	organization = "https://dev.azure.com/acme"
446	project = "Platform"
447	```
448	
449	Install Azure CLI's `azure-devops` extension separately. `dev` never installs
450	the extension, logs in, changes Azure defaults, or stores a PAT.
451	
452	FLEET merges user-authored primary `remotes.toml` with strict dev-owned sibling
453	`remotes.d/ssh-<alias>.toml` fragments, then reuses the accepted REPOS snapshot
454	for the local host and calls each configured host's own `dev` over SSH. Generated
455	entries are owned by explicit `dev ssh setup/remove --fleet`; FLEET `e` and
456	`fleet config edit` open only the primary file, while `fleet config show` marks
457	generated origins. `remote_os` selects POSIX shell or allowlisted encoded
458	PowerShell transport and participates in endpoint cache identity with the SSH
459	port and optional `machine_id` pin. If REPOS is still loading, FLEET waits while keeping cached rows instead
460	of rescanning. The TUI hides this machine by default because REPOS is richer;
461	`a` includes local rows. `dev fleet list` remains local plus remote. Enter
462	prefers Herdr remote navigation and falls back to an SSH login shell.
463	`dev fleet sync` is explicit and strict: it only fast-forwards a clean checkout
464	of the same behind-only branch; dirty/ahead/diverged clones are never rewritten.
465	
466	`dev fleet files [repo-or-path] --to <host>` is a separate one-shot channel for
467	explicitly exported ignored files. It is report-only unless `--apply` is passed;
468	`--yes` never implies `--replace`. Both clones must already match by fetch
469	identity, attached branch and exact commit, and each exact path must be untracked
470	and ignored on both sides. Only bounded regular files are accepted. Apply also
471	requires a `machine_id` pin obtained with the read-only `dev fleet machine-id
472	<host>` command and verified independently. The operation never clones, switches
473	branches, runs provisioning, transfers task/catalog/note state, deletes source
474	files, or evicts a repository; native Windows payloads are disabled.
475	
476	REPOS has LIVE, LATEST and asynchronous SIZE. SIZE is logical
477	checkout+private-Git bytes; shared Git is separate and marked `+S`. Detail also
478	shows no-remote/local-only/multi-upstream recovery topology. Press space to
479	expand linked worktrees; children
480	show their own Git/session/task state and mark harness-owned or untracked
481	checkouts `(ephemeral)` / `(external)`. Press `y` followed by `y/p/b/s/w` to
482	copy contextual Markdown, path, branch, runtime/agent sessions, or every
483	worktree path. `dev repo context [repo]` prints the full Markdown without a TUI.
484	`[tui.repos]` chooses columns and default sort; `O` cycles sort and `R` reverses
485	it.
486	
487	`H` opens the selected repo's heatmap. On an empty panel, `b` backfills only
488	that repo and redraws; `r` rereads existing stats. Stats live in
489	`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and are durable observations, not cache — use
490	`dev stats clear` with an explicit scope. `dev cache clear` only removes
491	regenerable forge/size/gitignore/note-FTS data under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev`.
492	
493	`e` edits config and returning live-reloads data/tool bindings; `r` reloads
494	explicitly. Runtime
495	backend changes require restarting the TUI.
496	
497	External tools are explicit `[[tui.tools]]` config. Run `dev tui tools` before
498	recommending a binding; it shows the exact command and whether it is available.
499	Commands run through `$SHELL` in the selected checkout. For an alias/function
500	that exists only in shell rc, set `interactive = true`; dev uses `$SHELL -lic`
501	and evaluates the command after rc loading. Prefer an executable on PATH when
502	the binding should be portable across machines.
503	
504	## Repository quick notes
505	
506	Read `references/notes.md` before adding/searching/editing/deleting notes or
507	when deciding whether content belongs in dev vs td/beads.
508	
509	Quick notes are multiple timestamped Markdown files under configured
510	`paths.state_dir/notes/<catalog-id>/` (default `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`); the
511	catalog ID attaches them to the canonical clone across worktrees, symlinks and
512	moves. `dev` does not synchronize notes or catalog state, so cross-host
513	attachment requires syncing both. SQLite FTS at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db`
514	is disposable: clearing it removes no thoughts and the next search rebuilds it.
515	
516	TUI context keys: `n` quick-adds on TASKS/REPOS; `N` browses with `/` search,
517	Enter expand, `a` add, `e` editor, and confirmed `d` delete. In TRY, `n` remains
518	“new Try.” REMOTE needs a local clone.
519	
520	## Editing configuration
521	
522	Use `dev edit` (or `dev config edit`) rather than guessing the XDG path. It
523	opens the file selected by `--config`, generating the machine-detected starter
524	when absent, and resolves `--editor` → `$VISUAL` → `$EDITOR` → nvim/vim/vi.
```

```text
1	# Agent skill and MCP inventory
2	
3	Use these inventories to answer two different questions:
4	
5	- `dev skill list`: which reusable instruction packages are present, and whether
6	  an explicit upstream source check reports newer lock-recorded content.
7	- `dev mcp list`: which external MCP capabilities are declared in supported
8	  static agent configuration files.
9	
10	Do not treat an MCP declaration as a skill, a live connection, or permission to
11	invoke tools.
12	
13	## Skill inventory
14	
15	```bash
16	dev skill list
17	dev skill list --repo <repo-or-checkout> --project
18	dev skill list --all
19	dev skill list --all --check --json
20	```
21	
22	Reads use a versioned snapshot of all 77 agent paths from `skills@1.5.23` plus
23	project/global locks. They never execute `skills`, Node, npm, `npx`, agent
24	detectors, or project code. `--all` scans canonical repositories. The TUI is
25	context-first: inside Git it scans only the exact startup checkout plus global
26	paths; outside Git it scans all accepted REPOS targets plus the ordinary startup
27	directory.
28	
29	Keep status dimensions separate:
30	
31	- presence: local directory present or lock-only/missing;
32	- integrity: only embedded `dev-cli` files can be verified against the binary; additional user files are ignored;
33	- update: lock-recorded upstream content is unchecked/current/changed/missing or
34	  unverifiable.
35	
36	`--check` is the explicit network action. It groups equal Git source/ref pairs
37	and hashes Git object bytes without populating a checkout, so filters/autocrlf do
38	not run or alter results. Non-ASCII provider folder hashes remain unverifiable
39	when locale ordering cannot be reproduced. `skill add` and `skill update` are
40	explicit, serialized mutations and require a directly installed `skills`
41	executable; `dev` skips repository-local npm bins and rejects source-less locks.
42	
43	## MCP inventory
44	
45	```bash
46	dev mcp list
47	dev mcp list --repo <repo-or-checkout>
48	dev mcp list --all --json
49	dev mcp list --agent claude-code,codex --scope project
50	```
51	
52	Adapters cover Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. Rows remain
53	scope-qualified declarations; local Claude rows retain the exact project key and
54	an absolute `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` relocates user sources. `dev` resolves only
55	Claude's documented user/project/local/managed project approvals; it does not
56	guess a generally effective configuration. `configured`, `enabled`, and
57	`disabled` are declaration/approval facts, not health.
58	
59	The TUI applies the same context-first target policy as SKILLS: the exact startup
60	checkout inside Git, or the cross-repository REPOS inventory outside Git.
61	
62	The scanner never runs agent MCP commands, configured commands/helpers, servers,
63	or URLs. It never expands environment variables, reads OAuth/token stores, or
64	loads OpenCode `{file:…}` content. Normalized output retains only safe command
65	basenames, endpoint scheme/host, argument counts, credential reference names,
66	policy counts, and redaction markers.
67	
68	Omitted sources include plugin caches, hosted connectors, remote organization
69	configuration, inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and command-line-only inputs.
70	Treat the coverage metadata as part of the result.
71
```

docs/claude/extensions-agent-sdk.md:11:Claude Code extension mechanisms solve different problems. Put reusable instructions in skills, deterministic lifecycle reactions in hooks, external capabilities behind MCP, distributable components in plugins, and a programmatic agent loop in the Agent SDK.

776	Install Azure CLI's `azure-devops` extension and authenticate with Azure CLI.

785	pressing `r`, reparses config and reloads data/tool bindings without restarting
786	the TUI; a runtime-backend change is reported as requiring restart.
787	
788	REPOS includes `LATEST`, defined as the newest dirty-file mtime, commit time, or
789	task update, plus asynchronous `SIZE`. Size is portable logical bytes:
790	
791	- `checkout_bytes` excludes only the checkout root's `.git` entry.
792	- `private_git_bytes` belongs only to this checkout and is included in
793	  `owned_bytes`, the table value.
794	- `shared_git_bytes` is shown separately and never charged to every linked
795	  worktree. `+S` means shared Git storage exists but is not reclaimable with
796	  that row.

798	Measurements stream in after the first frame, use a 10-minute private XDG cache,
799	and can be forced with `r`; unreadable subtrees display a lower bound (`≥`).

808	
809	In REPOS and TRY, `O` cycles sort and `R` reverses it. Structured filters include

812	parallelism, and the alternate screen appears before they finish.

1440	`dev` ships the agent skill that documents it, embedded in the binary — the
1441	same pattern `herdr --skill` uses. A skill vendored separately drifts from the
1442	tool it describes, and an agent reading a stale command list is worse than one
1443	reading none.
1444	
1445	```bash
1446	dev skill list                 # current checkout + global native inventory
1447	dev skill list --all --check --json
1448	dev skill list --repo api --project
1449	dev skill add                  # interactive wizard for daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
1450	dev skill update project-knowledge-harness --global --yes
1451	dev skill install              # → ~/.agents/skills/dev-cli, symlinked into ~/.claude/skills
1452	dev mcp list --all --json      # sanitized static declarations; never health probes
1453	dev --skill                    # print it, for a dotfiles installer to sync
1454	dev skill sync                 # regenerate the command reference from the command tree
1455	dev skill sync --check         # fail if it has drifted — wire into CI
1456	```
1457	
1458	`dev skill add [package]` is only a shortcut into the upstream interactive
1459	wizard. It never selects all skills or agents. Listing is native and never runs
1460	`skills`, npm, `npx`, or project code. Add/update are explicit actions, require
1461	a directly installed `skills` executable, and may access the network; `dev` skips
1462	repository-local `node_modules` candidates, rejects source-less update locks, and
1463	serializes provider processes. `--all` scans each configured canonical checkout
1464	once, while the TUI also includes its exact startup linked worktree when distinct
1465	and reads global paths once. Freshness hashes Git object bytes without checkout
1466	filters or autocrlf transforms; locale-dependent non-ASCII folder hashes stay
1467	unverifiable. Lock hashes describe upstream freshness, not installed-file integrity;
1468	only the embedded `dev-cli` skill can verify that every bundled file matches
1469	(additional user files are ignored).
1470	
1471	`dev mcp list` inventories declarations from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini
1472	CLI, and OpenCode files. It keeps scopes separate, honors absolute
1473	`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, retains exact Claude local project keys, and resolves only
1474	Claude's documented user/project/local/managed project approvals. It deliberately
1475	omits runtime health, a generally effective merged configuration, plugin caches,
1476	hosted connectors, remote organization config, and command-line-only config.
1477	Environment/header/OAuth values, raw arguments, URL credentials, and indirect file
1478	contents never enter normalized output; only safe reference names and finite
1479	policy/count facts remain.
1480	
1481	The skill defers to the companion `git-workflow` skill for commit conventions,
1482	SemVer and branch naming rather than restating them. It owns what is new: the
1483	worktree ownership rule, the task lifecycle, and how `dev` and herdr divide
1484	responsibility.
```

1	# Example: TUI / interactive terminal app
2	
3	Interactive terminal apps (text editors, REPLs, curses-based UIs) can't
4	be driven directly by an agent's bash tool - they take over the terminal.
5	The skill must show how to wrap them in `tmux` so the agent can send
6	input, capture output, and take screenshots.
7	
8	## The tmux pattern
9	
10	This is the standard approach:
11	
12	1. Start the TUI inside a detached tmux session
13	2. Send keystrokes with `tmux send-keys`
14	3. Read screen contents with `tmux capture-pane`
15	4. Clean up with `tmux kill-session`
16	
17	The skill's `SKILL.md` should present this as the primary way to drive
18	the app. A small `driver.sh` that wraps the launch+attach sequence can
19	live in the skill directory, but for most TUIs the raw tmux commands in
20	the skill body are enough.
21	
22	## Example snippet
23	
24	> ## Run (interactive, for agents)
25	>
26	> Start the TUI inside tmux:
27	>
28	> ```bash
29	> tmux new-session -d -s app -x 120 -y 40 './myapp'
30	> ```
31	>
32	> Poll until the ready marker appears (faster + more reliable than a fixed sleep -
33	> returns the instant the app is up, fails loudly if it isn't):
34	>
35	> ```bash
36	> timeout 10 bash -c 'until tmux capture-pane -t app -p | grep -q "Ready"; do sleep 0.2; done'
37	> tmux capture-pane -t app -p
38	> ```
39	>
40	> Send input (this example navigates to the Settings screen and toggles
41	> an option):
42	>
43	> ```bash
44	> tmux send-keys -t app 's'
45	> timeout 5 bash -c 'until tmux capture-pane -t app -p | grep -q "Settings"; do sleep 0.2; done'
46	> tmux send-keys -t app 'Down' 'Down' 'Space'  # navigate + toggle
47	> timeout 5 bash -c 'until tmux capture-pane -t app -p | grep -qF "[x]"; do sleep 0.2; done'
48	> tmux capture-pane -t app -p
49	> ```
50	>
51	> If you find yourself writing more than a couple of these poll lines, pull
52	> them into a `wait_for()` helper in a `driver.sh` next to the skill.
53	>
54	> Quit:
55	>
56	> ```bash
57	> tmux send-keys -t app 'q'
58	> tmux kill-session -t app 2>/dev/null || true
59	> ```
60	>
61	> ### Key reference
62	>
63	> | Key | Action |
64	> |---|---|
65	> | `j` / `k` or `Down` / `Up` | Navigate list |
66	> | `Enter` | Select |
67	> | `s` | Settings |
68	> | `q` | Quit |
69	
70	## Details worth documenting
71	
72	- **Terminal size.** Some TUIs break or hide content at small widths.
73	  Specify a known-good size in the `tmux new-session -x -y` args.
74	- **Startup time.** Poll for a ready marker (`until tmux capture-pane | grep -q X`)
75	  rather than a fixed `sleep N` - returns the instant the app is up, and fails
76	  usefully when it never does. Say what string means ready.
77	- **Keybinding reference.** A table of the main keys. This is the "API"
78	  of a TUI - an agent needs it to drive the app.
79	- **Exit cleanly.** Show the quit keystroke *and* `tmux kill-session` as
80	  a fallback.
81	- **Color/unicode quirks.** If `capture-pane` output is hard to read,
82	  note flags that help (`-e` for escape sequences, `-J` to join wrapped
83	  lines).
84	
85	## Also document the direct invocation
86	
87	For a human running the app interactively, tmux is overkill. Include
88	the one-liner too:
89	
90	> ## Run (direct, for humans)
91	>
92	> ```bash
93	> ./myapp
94	> ```

96	> Press `q` to quit.

_**Agent - sidechain (2026-09-04 04:51:44Z)**_

`high effort → 3+5 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`. If the Agent tool is not available in your current tool set, do not error — perform each angle (and each verification) yourself, sequentially, in this context.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

7	## Toolchain and commands
8

16	go test -race ./...                # CI test command
17	go test ./internal/gitx -run '^TestAddWorktreeUsesExplicitBase$'  # one test

21	make e2e                           # real CLI lifecycle in an isolated temporary HOME
22	make skill-sync                    # regenerate command docs, then rebuild embedded skill
23	make skill-check                   # fail when command tree and generated skill reference drift
24	make install                       # binary under PREFIX; skill in user agent directories
25	```

31	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source
32	uv run mkdocs build --strict
33	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --site site
34	```

36	If generated `docs/llms*.txt` files drift, regenerate them with `uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source --generate-llms` and then rerun the documentation checks.
37	
38	## Architecture
39	
40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:
41	
42	```text
43	cmd/dev/main.go
44	  -> cli.Execute()
45	  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
46	  -> App.Load()
47	  -> Cobra command handler
48	  -> domain package(s)
49	```
50	
51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:
52	
53	- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints. Lifecycle callers use exact-record revisions and locked compare-and-update/delete transactions rather than treating a previously read task as current.
56	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
57	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
58	- `taskflow` is the UI-agnostic lifecycle authority: it separates recorded intent, typed live observations, immutable guarded plans, approvals, and partial result ledgers. Apply locks and reloads task/Git/worktree/runtime/artifact/remote identity, then rejects stale authority before mutation.
59	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, all registered worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and UI projections consume this joined view.
60	- `flowtui` is an independent Bubble Tea model for the preview `dev flow` repository state-machine UI. It receives repository reads and taskflow Plan/Apply callbacks; do not embed it in or add a mode to the dashboard's `tui` model.
61	- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
62	- `note` stores multiple repository thoughts as durable Markdown keyed by catalog ID and maintains a rebuildable SQLite FTS index. It is distinct from task context and the catalog's single metadata summary.
63	- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.
64	- `stats` is durable SQLite data; `diskusage`, note FTS, and forge/gitignore data are regenerable caches. Do not treat stats as cache.
65	- `forge` wraps optional `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI integrations and must degrade to local Git behavior when they are unavailable.
66	- `sshhost` owns bounded static discovery of the active user OpenSSH Include closure, canonical files under `~/.ssh/dev.d`, public-key selection/generation/bootstrap, fresh authentication proofs, and the explicit handoff into dev fleet. OpenSSH and plain `ssh -G` remain semantic authority; dev reads foreign host definitions but never rewrites them, copies private keys, weakens host-key policy, or treats every alias as a fleet member.
67	- `fleet` merges the user-authored primary `remotes.toml` with strict dev-owned `remotes.d/ssh-<alias>.toml` registrations. Remote `dev` state remains host-local. `remote_os` selects target semantics: POSIX uses the shell launcher, while Windows uses an encoded PowerShell launcher that accepts only hidden fleet helpers, preserves sync stdin, and never applies controller path rules to remote paths.
68	
69	The principal task start flow spans `internal/cli/start.go`, `start_flow.go`, `gitx`/`wt`, `runtime`, and `task`: resolve the canonical repository and explicit base, create or select the checkout, provision/open it, then persist and annotate the task. Task-backed park/resume/completion/retirement and exact unmanaged Adopt/Remove policy belong in `taskflow`; CLI commands, the dashboard, `sweep`, and `flowtui` are adapters. Preserve report-before-apply and no-data-loss ordering, including the isolated compatibility paths that have not migrated to taskflow.
70	
71	State is split intentionally:
72	
73	- Git remotes/branches are durable code truth.
74	- Worktrees are disposable local checkouts.
75	- Runtime sessions are per-host and re-derivable.
76	- Task TOML and catalog assets hold only intent/identity that Git cannot answer.
77	- Repository quick-note Markdown is durable sidecar data; `notes.db` is only its disposable search index.
78	- `stats.db` is durable observation data; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/*` is disposable.
79	- The user's OpenSSH configuration is durable connection truth. Dev owns only its exact top-level `Include ~/.ssh/dev.d/*.conf` and structurally valid fragments in `~/.ssh/dev.d`; key bootstrap sends public material only and has no private-key transfer or remote-key revocation lifecycle.
80	- Fleet intent is the merged primary `remotes.toml` plus generated sibling `remotes.d` fragments. A generated fragment exists only after explicit `dev ssh setup --fleet` and a fresh ordinary alias login; controller caches and each remote machine's paths/tasks/runtime remain re-derivable or host-local.
81	
82	## Behavioral contracts
83	
84	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
85	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
86	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
87	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
88	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
89	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
90	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
91	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
92	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
93	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
94	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
95	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
96	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output.
97	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
98	- SSH initialization is report-before-apply; managed host changes are confined to canonical dev-owned fragments. Full bootstrap requires an explicit existing key or explicit generation, registers fleet only behind `--fleet`, and reports interrupted remote installation as unknown rather than pretending to roll it back.
99	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.
100	
101	## Versioning and changelog
102	
103	The current published baseline is `v0.2.4` (2026-09-01). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
104	
105	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
106	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
107	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
108	
109	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
110	
111	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
112	
113	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
114	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
115	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
116	
117	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
118	
119	For a release:
120	
121	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
122	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
123	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
124	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
125	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
126	
127	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
128	
129	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
130	
131	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
132	
133	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
134	
135	| Change | Required synchronization |
136	|---|---|

140	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
141	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
142	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
143	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
144	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
145	
146	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.

18		}

22	func (m Model) capabilityFilePath() (string, error) {

24			return skillFilePath(row)
25		}

27			if strings.TrimSpace(row.ConfigPath) == "" {

29			}

41		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "checkout", row.Checkout)
42		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "path", row.Path)
43		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "agents", strings.Join(row.Agents, ", "))
44		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "managed", string(row.ManagedBy))
45		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "presence", string(row.Presence))
46		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "integrity", string(row.Integrity))
47		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source", row.Source)
48		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source_url", row.SourceURL)
49		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "update", string(row.UpdateStatus))

7	func (m Model) updateMouse(message tea.MouseMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
8		event := tea.MouseEvent(message)
9		if event.Shift || event.Alt || event.Ctrl {
10			return m, nil
11		}
12		if m.overlay.kind == overlayActionMenu {
13			return m.updateActionMenuMouse(event)
14		}

16			return m, nil
17		}
18	
19		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
20			if !m.mouseOverList(event.X, event.Y) {
21				return m, nil
22			}
23			delta := mouseWheelRows
24			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
25				delta = -delta
26			}
27			m.setAt(m.at() + delta)
28			return m, nil
29		}
30		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress {
31			return m, nil
32		}
33	
34		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonLeft && event.Y == 0 {
35			for _, hit := range m.buildHeaderLayout().tabs {
36				if event.X < hit.from || event.X >= hit.to {
37					continue
38				}
39				if m.view == hit.view {
40					return m, nil
41				}
42				m.view = hit.view
43				return m.afterViewSwitch()
44			}
45			return m, nil
46		}
47	
48		row, ok := m.mouseRow(event.X, event.Y)

55		case tea.MouseButtonRight:

64	func (m Model) mouseRow(x, y int) (int, bool) {
65		if x < 0 || x >= m.width {
66			return 0, false
67		}
68		count := m.count()
69		from, to := m.window(count)
70		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
71		if y < first || y >= first+(to-from) {
72			return 0, false
73		}
74		return from + y - first, true
75	}
76	
77	func (m Model) mouseOverList(x, y int) bool {
78		if x < 0 || x >= m.width || m.count() == 0 {
79			return false
80		}
81		from, to := m.window(m.count())
82		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
83		return y >= 2 && y < first+(to-from)
84	}

86	func (m Model) updateActionMenuMouse(event tea.MouseEvent) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
87		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
88			if m.overlay.optionCount == 0 {
89				return m, nil
90			}
91			delta := 1
92			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
93				delta = -1
94			}
95			m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + delta + m.overlay.optionCount) % m.overlay.optionCount
96			return m, nil
97		}
98		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress || event.Button != tea.MouseButtonLeft {
99			return m, nil
100		}
101		first := 4
102		if m.overlay.detail != "" {
103			first++
104		}
105		if event.Y < first || event.Y >= first+m.overlay.optionCount {
106			m.overlay = overlayState{}
107			return m, nil
108		}
109		m.overlay.optionIndex = event.Y - first
110		return m.runOverlayAction()
111	}

+func capabilityFileEditorProcess(path string) (*exec.Cmd, error) {
+	path = config.Expand(path)
+	file, _, err := safefile.OpenRegular(path)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("open capability file %s: %w", config.Contract(path), err)

+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("close capability file %s: %w", config.Contract(path), err)
+	}
+	proc, _, err := editorProcess(path, "")
+	return proc, err

 // configEditorProcess resolves the effective config and editor without running

 // which suspends the alternate screen and redraws after the editor exits.
 func configEditorProcess(app *App, editor string) (*exec.Cmd, string, bool, error) {
 	path := app.configPath
 	if path == "" {
 		path = config.ConfigFile()
 	}
 	path = config.Expand(path)
 	created, err := ensureConfigForEdit(path)
 	if err != nil {
 		return nil, "", false, err
 	}
 	proc, chosen, err := editorProcess(path, editor)
 	return proc, chosen, created, err
 }

+	}

 // ensureConfigForEdit generates a usable config before opening an absent path.
 // Editing an empty file would hide every default the user is trying to change.
 func ensureConfigForEdit(path string) (bool, error) {
 	info, err := os.Stat(path)
 	switch {
 	case err == nil && info.IsDir():
 		return false, fmt.Errorf("%s is a directory, not a config file", config.Contract(path))
 	case err == nil:
 		return false, nil
 	case !os.IsNotExist(err):
 		return false, err
 	}
 	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
 		return false, err
 	}
 	body := renderStarterConfig(config.DetectLayout().Fallbacks())
 	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o644); err != nil {
 		return false, err
 	}
 	return true, nil
 }

 // Tool is one external program bound to a key in the dashboard.
 type Tool struct {
 	// Key launches it. A single character, and not one of the dashboard's own
 	// bindings — dev reports a clash rather than silently shadowing.
 	Key string `toml:"key"`
 	// Name is shown in the footer.
 	Name string `toml:"name"`
 	// Run is a shell command, executed in the selected row's checkout.
 	Run string `toml:"run"`
 	// Interactive runs through $SHELL -lic, loading the user's rc file so a
 	// shell alias or function can be used. Off by default: startup files can
 	// print output and alter environment in ways an ordinary command should
 	// not inherit accidentally.
 	Interactive bool `toml:"interactive"`
 }
 
 // reservedKeys are the dashboard's own bindings. A tool cannot take one,
 // because losing the ability to quit or move is not a trade anyone wants.
 var reservedKeys = map[string]string{
 	"q": "quit", "j": "down", "k": "up", "g": "top", "G": "bottom",
 	"h": "previous view", "l": "next view", "tab": "next view",

 	"O": "cycle repo sort", "R": "reverse repo sort",
 	"m": "edit repo metadata", "y": "copy repo metadata",
 }
 
 // ReservedKey reports the dashboard binding a key would collide with.
 func ReservedKey(key string) (string, bool) {
 	name, ok := reservedKeys[key]
 	return name, ok
 }
 
 // DefaultTools are the programs bound when nothing is configured. They are
 // written out in full by `dev config init` rather than left implicit, so what
 // is bound is visible rather than something to discover by pressing keys.
 func DefaultTools() []Tool {

 func humanSeconds(seconds int) string {

195			}

377	func (m Model) runOverlayAction() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
378		if m.overlay.optionCount == 0 || m.overlay.optionIndex >= m.overlay.optionCount {
379			return m, nil
380		}
381		action := m.overlay.options[m.overlay.optionIndex]
382		token := m.overlay.selection
383		if !m.selectToken(token) {
384			m.overlay = overlayState{}
385			m.err = fmt.Errorf("selected row changed while its action menu was open")
386			return m, nil
387		}
388		m.overlay = overlayState{}
389		return m.runListAction(action)
390	}

459	func (m Model) toggleSelectedRepo() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
460		item, ok := m.currentRepoItem()

1	package tui

3	import tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
4	
5	const mouseWheelRows = 3
6	
7	func (m Model) updateMouse(message tea.MouseMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
8		event := tea.MouseEvent(message)
9		if event.Shift || event.Alt || event.Ctrl {
10			return m, nil
11		}
12		if m.overlay.kind == overlayActionMenu {
13			return m.updateActionMenuMouse(event)
14		}
15		if m.noteMode() || m.overlay.kind != overlayNone || m.mode != modeList {
16			return m, nil
17		}
18	
19		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
20			if !m.mouseOverList(event.X, event.Y) {
21				return m, nil
22			}
23			delta := mouseWheelRows
24			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
25				delta = -delta
26			}
27			m.setAt(m.at() + delta)
28			return m, nil
29		}
30		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress {
31			return m, nil
32		}
33	
34		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonLeft && event.Y == 0 {
35			for _, hit := range m.buildHeaderLayout().tabs {
36				if event.X < hit.from || event.X >= hit.to {
37					continue
38				}
39				if m.view == hit.view {
40					return m, nil
41				}
42				m.view = hit.view
43				return m.afterViewSwitch()
44			}
45			return m, nil
46		}
47	
48		row, ok := m.mouseRow(event.X, event.Y)
49		if !ok {
50			return m, nil
51		}
52		switch event.Button {
53		case tea.MouseButtonLeft:
54			m.setAt(row)
55		case tea.MouseButtonRight:
56			m.setAt(row)
57			if !m.remoteClone.active() {
58				m = m.openActionMenu()
59			}
60		}
61		return m, nil
62	}
63	
64	func (m Model) mouseRow(x, y int) (int, bool) {
65		if x < 0 || x >= m.width {
66			return 0, false
67		}
68		count := m.count()
69		from, to := m.window(count)
70		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
71		if y < first || y >= first+(to-from) {
72			return 0, false
73		}
74		return from + y - first, true
75	}
76	
77	func (m Model) mouseOverList(x, y int) bool {
78		if x < 0 || x >= m.width || m.count() == 0 {
79			return false
80		}
81		from, to := m.window(m.count())
82		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
83		return y >= 2 && y < first+(to-from)
84	}
85	
86	func (m Model) updateActionMenuMouse(event tea.MouseEvent) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
87		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
88			if m.overlay.optionCount == 0 {
89				return m, nil
90			}
91			delta := 1
92			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
93				delta = -1
94			}
95			m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + delta + m.overlay.optionCount) % m.overlay.optionCount
96			return m, nil
97		}
98		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress || event.Button != tea.MouseButtonLeft {
99			return m, nil
100		}
101		first := 4
102		if m.overlay.detail != "" {
103			first++
104		}
105		if event.Y < first || event.Y >= first+m.overlay.optionCount {
106			m.overlay = overlayState{}
107			return m, nil
108		}
109		m.overlay.optionIndex = event.Y - first
110		return m.runOverlayAction()
111	}

32	// View is which list the dashboard is showing.
33	type View int
34	
35	const (
36		// ViewTasks lists recorded change streams — what am I working on.
37		ViewTasks View = iota
38		// ViewRepos lists every repository under the scan roots — what do I have.
39		ViewRepos
40		// ViewFleet lists repository observations across configured machines.
41		ViewFleet
42		// ViewTries lists durable scratch experiments and retained lifecycle history.
43		ViewTries
44		// ViewRemote lists repositories visible through configured forge CLIs.
45		ViewRemote
46		// ViewSkills lists project and global agent skills.
47		ViewSkills
48		// ViewMCP lists static MCP server declarations across agent formats.
49		ViewMCP
50	)
51	
52	// Views is the cycle order.
53	var Views = []View{ViewTasks, ViewRepos, ViewFleet, ViewTries, ViewRemote, ViewSkills, ViewMCP}
54	
55	// CapabilityScope controls which project-local SKILLS and MCP sources are
56	// scanned. Global sources remain part of both scopes and are deduplicated by
57	// the domain collectors.
58	type CapabilityScope uint8
59	
60	const (
61		CapabilityStartupContext CapabilityScope = iota
62		CapabilityAllRepositories
63	)
64	
65	func (s CapabilityScope) String() string {
66		if s == CapabilityAllRepositories {
67			return "all"
68		}
69		return "context"
70	}
71	
72	func (v View) String() string {
73		switch v {
74		case ViewRepos:
75			return "repos"
76		case ViewFleet:
77			return "fleet"
78		case ViewTries:
79			return "try"
80		case ViewRemote:
81			return "remote"
82		case ViewSkills:
83			return "skills"
84		case ViewMCP:
85			return "mcp"
86		default:
87			return "tasks"
88		}
89	}

91	// Actions is everything the dashboard can do. The TUI owns no domain logic:
92	// it calls back into the same code paths the non-interactive commands use, so
93	// behaviour cannot diverge between them.
94	// LoadWarning carries nonfatal inventory diagnostics without making an accepted
95	// snapshot stale or retrying it on every tab visit.
96	type LoadWarning struct{ Message string }
97	
98	func (w LoadWarning) Error() string { return w.Message }
99	
100	func splitLoadWarning(err error) (string, error) {
101		var warning LoadWarning
102		if errors.As(err, &warning) {
103			return warning.Message, nil
104		}
105		return "", err
106	}
107	
108	type Actions struct {
109		// Reload re-reads the task inventory.
110		Reload func(ctx context.Context) ([]inventory.Row, error)
111		// ReloadRepos re-reads the repository list.
112		ReloadRepos func(ctx context.Context) ([]RepoRow, error)
113		// ReloadFleet fans out to configured dev hosts. It is lazy like REMOTE.
114		ReloadFleet          func(ctx context.Context) ([]FleetRow, error)
115		ReloadFleetWithRepos func(ctx context.Context, repos []RepoRow) ([]FleetRow, error)
116		// ReloadRemote queries configured forge CLIs. It is lazy: the network is untouched
117		// until the REMOTE view is opened. Production supplies accepted local rows so
118		// matching does not trigger another repository discovery.
119		ReloadRemote          func(ctx context.Context) ([]RemoteRow, error)
120		ReloadRemoteWithRepos func(ctx context.Context, repos []RepoRow) ([]RemoteRow, error)
121		// ReloadSkills reads local project/global skill state without contacting sources.
122		ReloadSkills          func(ctx context.Context, scope CapabilityScope) ([]agentskill.Skill, error)
123		ReloadSkillsWithRepos func(ctx context.Context, repos []RepoRow, scope CapabilityScope) ([]agentskill.Skill, error)
124		// ReloadMCP reads static declarations only; it never starts or probes servers.
125		ReloadMCP          func(ctx context.Context, scope CapabilityScope) ([]agentmcp.Declaration, error)
126		ReloadMCPWithRepos func(ctx context.Context, repos []RepoRow, scope CapabilityScope) ([]agentmcp.Declaration, error)
127		// Cache seeds are local-only and asynchronous. Live REMOTE/FLEET work remains
128		// lazy until its view is requested.
129		LoadRemoteCache func(ctx context.Context) RemoteCacheResult
130		LoadFleetCache  func(ctx context.Context) FleetCacheResult
131		// AfterFirstView performs optional background work only after the initial
132		// application frame has been computed.
133		AfterFirstView func(ctx context.Context)
134		// CheckSkills performs the explicitly requested read-only network comparison.
135		CheckSkills func(ctx context.Context, rows []agentskill.Skill) []agentskill.Skill
136		// AddSkill and UpdateSkill return locked interactive processes for tea to suspend around.
137		AddSkill    func() (*agentskill.MutationCommand, error)
138		UpdateSkill func(row agentskill.Skill) (*agentskill.MutationCommand, error)
139		// Repos and Tries group asset-specific metadata and lifecycle actions.
140		Repos RepoActions
141		Tries TryActions
142		Notes NoteActions
143		Sizes SizeActions
144		Local LocalActions
145		// Open makes a task live.
146		Open func(ctx context.Context, t *task.Task) (OpenResult, error)
147		// OpenRepo makes a repository live.
148		OpenRepo func(ctx context.Context, r RepoRow) (OpenResult, error)
149		// OpenCheckout makes one linked worktree live.
150		OpenCheckout func(ctx context.Context, r RepoRow, checkout inventory.RepoCheckout) (OpenResult, error)
151		// OpenRemote opens a remote's existing local checkout.
152		OpenRemote func(ctx context.Context, r RemoteRow) (OpenResult, error)
153		// OpenFleet returns an interactive process for a local or remote fleet row.
154		OpenFleet func(ctx context.Context, r FleetRow) (*exec.Cmd, error)
155		// CloneRemote clones a remote that has no local checkout and returns the
156		// new path. Opening is a separate step after local inventory accepts it.
157		CloneRemote func(ctx context.Context, r RemoteRow) (string, error)
158		// Park closes a task's session and records its next action.
159		Park func(ctx context.Context, t *task.Task, next string) (string, error)
160		// SetNext records a task's next action.
161		SetNext func(ctx context.Context, t *task.Task, next string) error
162		// Start creates an isolated worktree task in a repository.
163		Start func(ctx context.Context, r RepoRow, name string) (string, error)
164		// StartDirect tracks the repository's currently checked-out branch without
165		// creating a branch or worktree.
166		StartDirect func(ctx context.Context, r RepoRow, name string) (string, error)
167		// LoadStats builds the selected repository's activity heatmap.
168		LoadStats func(ctx context.Context, repo string) (StatsPanel, error)
169		// BackfillStats derives this repository's history into the activity store.
170		BackfillStats func(ctx context.Context, repo string) error
171		// Copy writes a selected payload to the system clipboard.
172		Copy func(text string) error
173		// ReadFile returns bounded local regular-file contents for an explicit raw
174		// capability copy action. OpenFile hands the same selected file to an editor.
175		ReadFile func(ctx context.Context, path string) (string, error)
176		OpenFile func(path string) (*exec.Cmd, error)
177		// EditConfig returns the editor process; tea suspends around it.
178		EditConfig func() (*exec.Cmd, error)
179		// EditFleetConfig does the same for remotes.toml, which is a separate file
180		// with its own schema — the FLEET view's `e` would otherwise open the
181		// config that has nothing to do with what it is showing.
182		EditFleetConfig func() (*exec.Cmd, error)
183		// ValidateFleetConfig reparses remotes.toml after an edit. It rejects
184		// unknown fields, so a typo has to surface rather than silently drop a host.
185		ValidateFleetConfig func() error
186		// ReloadConfig reparses config and returns live-updatable preferences.
187		// Runtime backend changes need a TUI restart, which status explains.
188		ReloadConfig func(ctx context.Context) (ConfigUpdate, string, error)
189		// RepoColumns and sorting are live-updatable display policy.
190		RepoColumns []string
191		RepoSort    string
192		RepoReverse bool
193		// Tools are external programs the dashboard hands the terminal to.
194		Tools []Tool
195	}

320	// Model is the dashboard state.
321	type Model struct {
322		actions Actions
323		// trace is the one intentional shared pointer in the value-copied model. The
324		// recorder is append-only, bounded and concurrency-safe; it never controls UI
325		// behavior.
326		trace *perftrace.Recorder
327		// runContext bounds read/probe commands to this Bubble Tea program. Mutating
328		// actions deliberately keep their own contexts and completion handling.
329		runContext     context.Context
330		loadContexts   [viewCount]context.Context
331		loadCancels    [viewCount]context.CancelFunc
332		configCancel   context.CancelFunc
333		configContext  context.Context
334		localCancel    context.CancelFunc
335		localContext   context.Context
336		firstViewReady chan struct{}
337		firstViewOnce  *sync.Once
338	
339		view    View
340		rows    []inventory.Row
341		repos   []RepoRow
342		tries   []TryRow
343		remotes []RemoteRow
344		fleet   []FleetRow
345		skills  []agentskill.Skill
346		mcp     []agentmcp.Declaration
347		// Each fixed view owns value-copied request/readiness state. Optional views
348		// stay lazy; no synthetic all-tabs-ready state exists.
349		loads        [viewCount]viewLoadState
350		viewErrors   [viewCount]error
351		viewStatuses [viewCount]string
352		initialLoad  bool
353		// skillsChecking is a separate explicit network operation, not initial tab
354		// readiness.
355		skillsChecking         bool
356		skillsInventoryErr     error
357		skillsInventoryWarning string
358		sizeLoad               diskusage.Load
359		forceSizeReload        bool
360		configGeneration       uint64
361		localGeneration        uint64
362		toolGeneration         uint64
363	
364		remoteCloneSequence uint64
365		remoteClonePrompt   RemoteRow
366		remoteClone         remoteCloneState
367		remoteCloneSpinner  spinner.Model
368		unconfirmedRemotes  []remoteLocalMarker
369	
370		// Cursors are plain fields, one per view, rather than a map: bubbletea
371		// passes the model by value and expects each returned copy to be
372		// independent. A map would be shared between every copy, so a keypress
373		// that produced two candidate models would have them silently agree.
374		taskCursor   int
375		repoCursor   int
376		tryCursor    int
377		remoteCursor int
378		fleetCursor  int
379		skillCursor  int
380		mcpCursor    int
381		// expandedRepos is a slice rather than a map because Bubble Tea copies the
382		// model by value; a map would make candidate models share mutation.
383		expandedRepos []string
384		// filter is the live text query; states narrows the task view.
385		filter string
386		states []task.State
387		// showDone includes finished tasks, which are hidden by default because a
388		// finished task is not work in progress.
389		showDone bool
390		// showAllTries includes deprecated, archived, evicted, and graduated history.
391		showAllTries bool
392		// showLocalFleet includes this machine in FLEET. It is hidden by default
393		// because REPOS already provides the richer local inventory.
394		showLocalFleet  bool
395		capabilityScope CapabilityScope
396		trySort         string
397		tryReverse      bool
398	
399		mode              mode
400		input             textinput.Model
401		skillUpdateTarget agentskill.Skill
402		stats             *StatsPanel
403		overlay           overlayState
404	
405		notes              []*note.Note
406		noteTarget         NoteTarget
407		noteCursor         int
408		noteQuery          string
409		noteExpanded       bool
410		noteLoading        bool
411		noteReturnToBrowse bool
412		noteRequest        uint64
413	
414		status string
415		err    error
416	
417		width, height int
418		quitting      bool
419		chosen        string
420		activate      string
421	}
422	
423	// New builds the dashboard.
424	func New(actions Actions, rows []inventory.Row, repos []RepoRow) Model {
425		in := textinput.New()
426		in.CharLimit = 200
427		cloneSpinner := spinner.MiniDot
428		cloneSpinner.FPS = 200 * time.Millisecond
429	
430		m := Model{
431			actions:            actions,
432			rows:               rows,
433			repos:              repos,
434			input:              in,
435			remoteCloneSpinner: spinner.New(spinner.WithSpinner(cloneSpinner)),
436			width:              100,
437			height:             30,
438			firstViewReady:     make(chan struct{}),
439			firstViewOnce:      &sync.Once{},
440		}
441		if len(actions.Tools) > 0 {
442			m.toolGeneration = 1
443		}
444		if rows != nil {
445			m.seedViewSnapshot(ViewTasks, perftrace.SourceLive, perftrace.FreshnessFresh, true)
446		}
447		if repos != nil {
448			m.seedViewSnapshot(ViewRepos, perftrace.SourceLive, perftrace.FreshnessFresh, true)
449		}
450		return m
451	}
452	
453	// WithTrace observes performance boundaries without controlling model state.
454	func (m Model) WithTrace(trace *perftrace.Recorder) Model {
455		m.trace = trace
456		return m
457	}
458	
459	// WithContext bounds asynchronous read/probe commands to one dashboard run.
460	func (m Model) WithContext(ctx context.Context) Model {
461		m.runContext = ctx
462		return m
463	}
464	
465	// WithRemotes seeds the lazy forge view from a fresh on-disk cache. The first
466	// switch is then instant; r still refreshes explicitly.
467	func (m Model) WithRemotes(rows []RemoteRow) Model {
468		m.replaceRemotes(rows)
469		m.seedViewSnapshot(ViewRemote, perftrace.SourceCache, perftrace.FreshnessFresh, true)
470		return m
471	}
472	
473	// WithFleet seeds cached fleet rows while the first live refresh remains lazy.
474	func (m Model) WithFleet(rows []FleetRow) Model {
475		m.fleet = rows
476		m.seedViewSnapshot(ViewFleet, perftrace.SourceCache, perftrace.FreshnessStale, true)
477		return m
478	}
479	
480	// WithRemotesStale marks seeded rows for background refresh on first visit.
481	func (m Model) WithRemotesStale(stale bool) Model {
482		if stale {
483			m.loads[int(ViewRemote)].freshness = perftrace.FreshnessStale
484		}
485		return m
486	}
487	
488	// WithTries seeds the Try view, primarily for tests and embedded callers. The
489	// production dashboard loads it with the other local inventories in Init.
490	func (m Model) WithTries(rows []TryRow) Model {
491		m.tries = rows
492		m.matchRemoteLocals()
493		m.seedViewSnapshot(ViewTries, perftrace.SourceLive, perftrace.FreshnessFresh, true)
494		return m
495	}
496	
497	// BeginLoading makes Init load task, repository, and Try data asynchronously. This lets
498	// the alternate screen appear immediately instead of blocking on dozens of Git
499	// probes before Bubble Tea starts.
500	func (m Model) BeginLoading() Model {
501		m.initialLoad = true
502		m.beginLocalLoads(loadInitial)
503		return m
504	}
505	
506	// Chosen reports a directory the caller should cd into after the program
507	// exits, or "" when there is none.
508	func (m Model) Chosen() string { return m.chosen }
509	
510	// Activation reports the runtime handle to switch/attach after the dashboard
511	// has restored the terminal, or "" when the user quit normally.
512	func (m Model) Activation() string { return m.activate }
513	
514	// CurrentView reports which list is showing.
515	func (m Model) CurrentView() View { return m.view }
516	
517	// CapabilityScope reports whether SKILLS and MCP are scoped to the startup
518	// context or all accepted repositories.
519	func (m Model) CapabilityScope() CapabilityScope { return m.capabilityScope }
520	
521	// Init implements tea.Model.
522	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
523		commands := []tea.Cmd{textinput.Blink}
524		if m.initialLoad {
525			commands = append(commands, m.reload())
526		}
527		if len(m.actions.Tools) > 0 {
528			commands = append(commands, m.probeTools())
529		}
530		if m.actions.LoadRemoteCache != nil {
531			commands = append(commands, m.loadRemoteCache())
532		}
533		if m.actions.LoadFleetCache != nil {
534			commands = append(commands, m.loadFleetCache())
535		}
536		if m.actions.AfterFirstView != nil {
537			commands = append(commands, m.runAfterFirstView())
538		}
539		return tea.Batch(commands...)
540	}

707	func traceOutcome(err error) perftrace.Outcome {
708		switch {
709		case err == nil:
710			return perftrace.OutcomeSuccess
711		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
712			return perftrace.OutcomeCanceled
713		default:
714			return perftrace.OutcomeFailed
715		}
716	}
717	
718	func snapshotValid[T any](rows []T, err error) bool {
719		return !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) && (err == nil || rows != nil)
720	}

722	func batchCommands(commands ...tea.Cmd) tea.Cmd {
723		filtered := commands[:0]
724		for _, command := range commands {
725			if command != nil {
726				filtered = append(filtered, command)
727			}
728		}
729		switch len(filtered) {
730		case 0:
731			return nil
732		case 1:
733			return filtered[0]
734		default:
735			return tea.Batch(filtered...)
736		}
737	}

781	func (m Model) probeTools() tea.Cmd {
782		generation := m.toolGeneration
783		tools := append([]Tool(nil), m.actions.Tools...)
784		ctx := m.baseContext()
785		return func() tea.Msg {
786			finish := m.trace.Start(perftrace.TUIProducerTools, perftrace.Fields{Generation: generation})
787			jobs := make(chan int, len(tools))
788			for index := range tools {
789				jobs <- index
790			}
791			close(jobs)
792			var workers sync.WaitGroup
793			for range min(2, len(tools)) {
794				workers.Go(func() {
795					for index := range jobs {
796						available := true
797						if tools[index].Probe != nil {
798							available = tools[index].Probe(ctx)
799						}
800						if ctx.Err() != nil {
801							tools[index].Availability = ToolUnknown
802						} else if available {
803							tools[index].Availability = ToolAvailable
804						} else {
805							tools[index].Availability = ToolUnavailable
806						}
807					}
808				})
809			}
810			workers.Wait()
811			finish(traceOutcome(ctx.Err()))
812			return toolsMsg{generation: generation, tools: tools}
813		}
814	}

1024	func (m Model) reloadUpdatedSkill(name, lockName string, scope agentskill.Scope, checkout string) tea.Cmd {
1025		generation := m.viewLoad(ViewSkills).generation
1026		locals := append([]RepoRow(nil), m.repos...)
1027		capabilityScope := m.capabilityScope
1028		return func() tea.Msg {
1029			finish := m.trace.Start(perftrace.TUIProducerSkills, perftrace.Fields{View: perftrace.ViewSkills, Generation: generation})
1030			if m.actions.ReloadSkillsWithRepos == nil && m.actions.ReloadSkills == nil {
1031				finish(perftrace.OutcomeSuccess)
1032				return skillsMsg{
1033					generation: generation, valid: true, loaded: true, status: "updated " + name,
1034					warning: m.skillsInventoryWarning, inventoryErr: m.skillsInventoryErr, err: m.skillsInventoryErr,
1035				}
1036			}
1037			var rows []agentskill.Skill
1038			var err error
1039			if m.actions.ReloadSkillsWithRepos != nil {
1040				rows, err = m.actions.ReloadSkillsWithRepos(m.viewContext(ViewSkills), locals, capabilityScope)
1041			} else {
1042				rows, err = m.actions.ReloadSkills(m.viewContext(ViewSkills), capabilityScope)
1043			}
1044			warning, err := splitLoadWarning(err)
1045			if err != nil && rows == nil {
1046				finish(traceOutcome(err))
1047				return skillsMsg{generation: generation, valid: false, loaded: true, inventoryErr: err, err: err}
1048			}
1049			verified := false
1050			if m.actions.CheckSkills != nil {
1051				for i := range rows {
1052					candidateName := rows[i].Name
1053					if rows[i].Lock != nil {
1054						candidateName = rows[i].Lock.Name
1055					}
1056					if candidateName == lockName && rows[i].Scope == scope && rows[i].Checkout == checkout {
1057						checked := m.actions.CheckSkills(m.viewContext(ViewSkills), []agentskill.Skill{rows[i]})
1058						if len(checked) == 1 {
1059							rows[i] = checked[0]
1060							verified = true
1061						}
1062						break
1063					}
1064				}
1065			}
1066			status := "updated " + name
1067			if m.actions.CheckSkills != nil && !verified {
1068				status += "; matching row was not found for source verification"
1069			}
1070			if warning != "" {
1071				status += "; " + warning
1072			}
1073			outcome := traceOutcome(err)
1074			if warning != "" {
1075				outcome = perftrace.OutcomePartial
1076			}
1077			finish(outcome)
1078			return skillsMsg{
1079				generation: generation, rows: rows, valid: snapshotValid(rows, err), loaded: true,
1080				checked: verified, status: status, warning: warning, inventoryErr: err, err: err,
1081			}
1082		}
1083	}

1144	// visibleTasks applies the state filter and the text query.
1145	func (m Model) visibleTasks() []inventory.Row {
1146		var out []inventory.Row
1147		for _, r := range m.rows {
1148			if len(m.states) > 0 {
1149				if !containsState(m.states, r.Task.State) {
1150					continue
1151				}
1152			} else if r.Task.State == task.Done && !m.showDone {
1153				continue
1154			}
1155			if !matches(taskSearchText(r), m.filter) {
1156				continue
1157			}
1158			out = append(out, r)
1159		}
1160		return out
1161	}
1162	
1163	// visibleRepos applies the text query, and sorts repositories with work in
1164	// flight to the top — that is what someone opening the dashboard is looking
1165	// for, not alphabetical order.
1166	func (m Model) visibleRepos() []RepoRow {
1167		var out []RepoRow
1168		for _, r := range m.repos {
1169			if r.IsTry() || !r.matches(m.filter) {
1170				continue
1171			}
1172			out = append(out, r)
1173		}
1174		sortBy := m.actions.RepoSort
1175		if sortBy == "" {
1176			sortBy = "activity"
1177		}
1178		sort.SliceStable(out, func(i, j int) bool {
1179			cmp := compareRepos(out[i], out[j], sortBy)
1180			if m.actions.RepoReverse {
1181				return cmp > 0
1182			}
1183			return cmp < 0
1184		})
1185		return out
1186	}
1187	
1188	// visibleTries applies structured experiment filters and keeps sorting local to
1189	// the view so repository ordering remains independent.
1190	func (m Model) visibleTries() []TryRow {
1191		out := make([]TryRow, 0, len(m.tries))
1192		for _, row := range m.tries {
1193			if row.matches(m.filter) {
1194				out = append(out, row)
1195			}
1196		}
1197		sortBy := m.trySort
1198		if sortBy == "" {
1199			sortBy = "activity"
1200		}
1201		sortTryRows(out, sortBy, m.tryReverse)
1202		return out
1203	}
1204	
1205	type repoItem struct {
1206		Repo          RepoRow
1207		CheckoutIndex int // -1 is the repository parent; 1+ is a linked worktree
1208	}
1209	
1210	func (i repoItem) child() bool { return i.CheckoutIndex > 0 }
1211	
1212	func (i repoItem) checkout() (inventory.RepoCheckout, bool) {
1213		if i.CheckoutIndex < 0 || i.CheckoutIndex >= len(i.Repo.Context.Checkouts) {
1214			return inventory.RepoCheckout{}, false
1215		}
1216		return i.Repo.Context.Checkouts[i.CheckoutIndex], true
1217	}
1218	
1219	// visibleRepoItems flattens expanded worktrees under their sorted parent.
1220	// Children never participate in repo sorting and therefore cannot drift away
1221	// from the repository they belong to.
1222	func (m Model) visibleRepoItems() []repoItem {
1223		repos := m.visibleRepos()
1224		out := make([]repoItem, 0, len(repos))
1225		for _, r := range repos {
1226			out = append(out, repoItem{Repo: r, CheckoutIndex: -1})
1227			if !m.repoExpanded(r) {
1228				continue
1229			}
1230			for i := 1; i < len(r.Context.Checkouts); i++ {
1231				out = append(out, repoItem{Repo: r, CheckoutIndex: i})
1232			}
1233		}
1234		return out
1235	}
1236	
1237	func repoKey(r RepoRow) string {
1238		if r.Repo.CommonDir != "" {
1239			return r.Repo.CommonDir
1240		}
1241		return r.Repo.Path
1242	}
1243	
1244	func (m Model) repoExpanded(r RepoRow) bool {
1245		key := repoKey(r)
1246		for _, expanded := range m.expandedRepos {
1247			if expanded == key {
1248				return true
1249			}
1250		}
1251		return false
1252	}
1253	
1254	func (m *Model) toggleRepo(r RepoRow) {
1255		key := repoKey(r)
1256		for i, expanded := range m.expandedRepos {
1257			if expanded == key {
1258				m.expandedRepos = append(append([]string(nil), m.expandedRepos[:i]...), m.expandedRepos[i+1:]...)
1259				return
1260			}
1261		}
1262		m.expandedRepos = append(append([]string(nil), m.expandedRepos...), key)
1263	}
1264	
1265	// visibleRemotes filters the combined forge inventory. Local clones sort
1266	// first, then recently updated repositories.
1267	func (m Model) visibleRemotes() []RemoteRow {
1268		var out []RemoteRow
1269		for _, r := range m.remotes {
1270			if r.matches(m.filter) {
1271				out = append(out, r)
1272			}
1273		}
1274		sort.SliceStable(out, func(i, j int) bool {
1275			if out[i].Cloned() != out[j].Cloned() {
1276				return out[i].Cloned()
1277			}
1278			if !out[i].Repo.UpdatedAt.Equal(out[j].Repo.UpdatedAt) {
1279				return out[i].Repo.UpdatedAt.After(out[j].Repo.UpdatedAt)
1280			}
1281			return out[i].Repo.Label() < out[j].Repo.Label()
1282		})
1283		return out
1284	}

1286	func (m Model) visibleFleet() []FleetRow {
1287		var out []FleetRow
1288		for _, row := range m.fleet {
1289			if row.Local && !m.showLocalFleet {
1290				continue
1291			}
1292			if matches(row.searchText(), m.filter) {
1293				out = append(out, row)
1294			}
1295		}
1296		sort.SliceStable(out, func(i, j int) bool {
1297			leftName, rightName := "", ""
1298			if out[i].Repository != nil {
1299				leftName = strings.ToLower(out[i].Repository.Display)
1300			}
1301			if out[j].Repository != nil {
1302				rightName = strings.ToLower(out[j].Repository.Display)
1303			}
1304			if leftName != rightName {
1305				return leftName < rightName
1306			}
1307			return out[i].Host < out[j].Host
1308		})
1309		return out
1310	}
