```text
1	// Package agenttarget resolves the repository checkouts inspected by agent
2	// configuration inventories. It deliberately contains no skill, MCP, or UI
3	// policy so those domains can share one definition of a target.
4	package agenttarget
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/repo"
18	)
19	
20	// Target identifies one concrete checkout of one repository. RepoPath is the
21	// repository's main navigation path (which may be a configured symlink alias),
22	// while CheckoutRoot is the exact worktree to inspect. Linked worktrees share
23	// RepoPath and CommonDir but remain distinct targets through CheckoutRoot.
24	type Target struct {
25		RepoName     string `json:"repo_name"`
26		RepoDisplay  string `json:"repo_display"`
27		RepoPath     string `json:"repo_path"`
28		CheckoutRoot string `json:"checkout_root"`
29		CommonDir    string `json:"common_dir"`
30	}
31	
32	// Key is stable for one checkout of one clone. It is intentionally stricter
33	// than gitx.Repo.Key, which identifies the clone regardless of checkout.
34	func (t Target) Key() string {
35		return comparablePath(t.CommonDir) + "\x00" + comparablePath(t.CheckoutRoot)
36	}
37	
38	// Current resolves the checkout containing cwd. A linked worktree remains the
39	// target checkout; outside Git, the absolute directory remains a useful project
40	// scope for agents that support configuration in ordinary folders.
41	func Current(ctx context.Context, cwd string) (Target, error) {
42		target, err := ResolvePath(ctx, cwd)
43		if err == nil {
44			return target, nil
45		}
46		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
47			return Target{}, ctxErr
48		}
49		if !errors.Is(err, gitx.ErrNotARepo) {
50			return Target{}, err
51		}
52		root, pathErr := absoluteDirectory(cwd)
53		if pathErr != nil {
54			return Target{}, pathErr
55		}
56		name := filepath.Base(root)
57		return Target{
58			RepoName: name, RepoDisplay: name, RepoPath: root,
59			CheckoutRoot: root, CommonDir: root,
60		}, nil
61	}
62	
63	// ResolvePath resolves an explicit path to the checkout containing it.
64	func ResolvePath(ctx context.Context, value string) (Target, error) {
65		absolute, err := absoluteDirectory(value)
66		if err != nil {
67			return Target{}, err
68		}
69		found, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, absolute)
70		if err != nil {
71			return Target{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve target path %q: %w", value, err)
72		}
73		return fromGit(found)
74	}
75	
76	// ResolveRepository resolves an explicit repository reference using repo's
77	// normal name/path rules, then probes the selected path so an explicit linked
78	// worktree path is preserved.
79	func ResolveRepository(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Target, error) {
80		found, _, err := repo.Resolve(ctx, roots, ref)
81		if err != nil {
82			return Target{}, err
83		}
84		target, err := ResolvePath(ctx, found.Path)
85		if err != nil {
86			return Target{}, err
87		}
88		// A named canonical repository contributes its configured alias/category.
89		// An explicit linked-worktree path keeps the main repository identity from
90		// Git, but its checkout root remains the navigation path the caller selected.
91		switch {
92		case comparablePath(found.Path) == comparablePath(target.RepoPath):
93			if found.Name != "" {
94				target.RepoName = found.Name
95			}
96			if display := found.Display(); display != "" {
97				target.RepoDisplay = display
98			}
99			target.RepoPath = navigationPath(found.Path)
100			target.CheckoutRoot = target.RepoPath
101		case comparablePath(found.Path) == comparablePath(target.CheckoutRoot):
102			target.CheckoutRoot = navigationPath(found.Path)
103		}
104		return target, nil
105	}
106	
107	// ResolveRepo is a concise compatibility name for ResolveRepository.
108	func ResolveRepo(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Target, error) {
109		return ResolveRepository(ctx, roots, ref)
110	}
111	
112	// FromRepository converts one canonical repo discovery result without another
113	// filesystem walk or Git process. Bare and non-Git inventory entries have no
114	// checkout to inspect and are skipped.
115	func FromRepository(found repo.Repo) (Target, bool) {
116		if !found.HasGit || found.Bare {
117			return Target{}, false
118		}
119		checkout := firstNonEmpty(found.Path, found.MainRoot, found.RealPath)
120		commonDir := found.CommonDir
121		if checkout == "" || commonDir == "" {
122			return Target{}, false
123		}
124		// Preserve the first discovery root's navigation alias. CommonDir remains
125		// physical identity, so aliases still deduplicate correctly.
126		checkout = navigationPath(checkout)
127		repository := navigationPath(firstNonEmpty(found.Path, found.MainRoot, found.RealPath, checkout))
128		commonDir = canonicalPath(commonDir)
129		name := found.Name
130		if name == "" {
131			name = filepath.Base(repository)
132		}
133		display := found.Display()
134		if display == "" {
135			display = name
136		}
137		return Target{
138			RepoName: name, RepoDisplay: display, RepoPath: repository,
139			CheckoutRoot: checkout, CommonDir: commonDir,
140		}, true
141	}
142	
143	// FromRepo is a concise compatibility name for FromRepository.
144	func FromRepo(found repo.Repo) (Target, bool) { return FromRepository(found) }
145	
146	// FromRepositories converts an already-discovered repository inventory. This is
147	// the --all-style path: callers can reuse repo.Discover output and avoid a
148	// second walk. Bare and non-Git entries are omitted.
149	func FromRepositories(repositories []repo.Repo) []Target {
150		targets := make([]Target, 0, len(repositories))
151		for _, found := range repositories {
152			if target, ok := FromRepository(found); ok {
153				targets = append(targets, target)
154			}
155		}
156		return Dedupe(targets)
157	}
158	
159	// FromRepos is a concise compatibility name for FromRepositories.
160	func FromRepos(repositories []repo.Repo) []Target { return FromRepositories(repositories) }
161	
162	// WithCurrent appends the startup checkout when it is distinct from the
163	// canonical repository inventory, then returns the same deterministic order as
164	// other target builders.
165	func WithCurrent(targets []Target, current Target) []Target {
166		out := append([]Target(nil), targets...)
167		if current.CheckoutRoot != "" {
168			current = ReconcileCurrent(targets, current)
169			out = append(out, current)
170		}
171		return Dedupe(out)
172	}
173	
174	// ReconcileCurrent preserves the exact current checkout while applying the
175	// canonical repository's configured navigation identity when it is known.
176	func ReconcileCurrent(targets []Target, current Target) Target {
177		for _, target := range targets {
178			if comparablePath(target.CommonDir) == comparablePath(current.CommonDir) {
179				current.RepoName = target.RepoName
180				current.RepoDisplay = target.RepoDisplay
181				current.RepoPath = target.RepoPath
182				if comparablePath(target.CheckoutRoot) == comparablePath(current.CheckoutRoot) {
183					current.CheckoutRoot = target.CheckoutRoot
184				}
185				break
186			}
187		}
188		return current
189	}
190	
191	// All discovers configured repository roots once and converts the result to
192	// concrete main-checkout targets.
193	func All(ctx context.Context, roots []string) ([]Target, error) {
194		repositories, err := repo.Discover(ctx, roots, repo.DefaultOptions())
195		if err != nil {
196			return nil, err
197		}
198		return FromRepositories(repositories), nil
199	}
200	
201	// Dedupe returns one deterministic entry per common-directory plus checkout
202	// root. The first value supplies display metadata when aliases collide.
203	func Dedupe(targets []Target) []Target {
204		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(targets))
205		out := make([]Target, 0, len(targets))
206		for _, target := range targets {
207			key := target.Key()
208			if _, ok := seen[key]; ok {
209				continue
210			}
211			seen[key] = struct{}{}
212			out = append(out, target)
213		}
214		Sort(out)
215		return out
216	}
217	
218	// Sort orders targets by display name, repository, checkout, then common dir.
219	func Sort(targets []Target) {
220		sort.SliceStable(targets, func(i, j int) bool {
221			left, right := targets[i], targets[j]
222			leftDisplay, rightDisplay := strings.ToLower(left.RepoDisplay), strings.ToLower(right.RepoDisplay)
223			if leftDisplay != rightDisplay {
224				return leftDisplay < rightDisplay
225			}
226			if left.RepoDisplay != right.RepoDisplay {
227				return left.RepoDisplay < right.RepoDisplay
228			}
229			if left.RepoName != right.RepoName {
230				return left.RepoName < right.RepoName
231			}
232			if left.RepoPath != right.RepoPath {
233				return left.RepoPath < right.RepoPath
234			}
235			if left.CheckoutRoot != right.CheckoutRoot {
236				return left.CheckoutRoot < right.CheckoutRoot
237			}
238			return left.CommonDir < right.CommonDir
239		})
240	}

245		}
```

```text
147	func editorProcess(path, override string) (*exec.Cmd, string, error) {
148		chosen, err := resolveEditor(override)
149		if err != nil {
150			return nil, "", err
151		}
152		command := chosen + " " + shellQuote(path)
153		return exec.Command(shellPath(), "-c", command), chosen, nil
154	}
155	
156	func resolveEditor(override string) (string, error) {
157		for _, candidate := range []string{override, os.Getenv("VISUAL"), os.Getenv("EDITOR")} {
158			if strings.TrimSpace(candidate) != "" {
159				return candidate, nil
160			}
161		}
162		for _, candidate := range []string{"nvim", "vim", "vi"} {
163			if _, err := exec.LookPath(candidate); err == nil {
164				return candidate, nil
165			}
166		}
167		return "", fmt.Errorf("no editor found; set $VISUAL or $EDITOR, or pass --editor")
168	}
```

```text
463	func (s *Scanner) projectSources(target Target) []sourceSpec {
464		base := sourceSpec{
465			scope: ScopeProject, source: SourceDirect, repository: target.RepoDisplay,
466			repositoryPath: target.RepoPath, checkout: target.CheckoutRoot, projectRoot: target.CheckoutRoot,
467		}
468		makeSpec := func(agent Agent, relative string, adapter adapterKind) sourceSpec {
469			spec := base
470			spec.agent = agent
471			spec.path = filepath.Join(target.CheckoutRoot, filepath.FromSlash(relative))
472			spec.adapter = adapter
473			return spec
474		}
475		approvalSpec := func(path string, scope Scope, source DeclarationSource, confined bool) sourceSpec {
476			spec := base
477			spec.agent = AgentClaudeCode
478			spec.scope = scope
479			spec.source = source
480			spec.path = path
481			if !confined {
482				spec.projectRoot = ""
483			}
484			return spec
485		}
486		claude := makeSpec(AgentClaudeCode, ".mcp.json", adapterClaudeProject)
487		addApproval := func(path string, scope Scope, source DeclarationSource, confined bool) {
488			if strings.TrimSpace(path) != "" {
489				claude.approvalSources = append(claude.approvalSources, approvalSpec(path, scope, source, confined))
490			}
491		}
492		addApproval(s.options.ClaudeUserSettingsPath, ScopeUser, SourceDirect, false)
493		addApproval(filepath.Join(target.CheckoutRoot, ".claude", "settings.json"), ScopeProject, SourceDirect, true)
494		addApproval(filepath.Join(target.CheckoutRoot, ".claude", "settings.local.json"), ScopeLocal, SourceDirect, true)
495		for _, path := range s.options.ClaudeManagedSettingsPaths {
496			addApproval(path, ScopeManaged, SourceManaged, false)
497		}
498		return []sourceSpec{
499			claude,
500			makeSpec(AgentCodex, ".codex/config.toml", adapterCodex),
501			makeSpec(AgentCursor, ".cursor/mcp.json", adapterCursor),
502			makeSpec(AgentGeminiCLI, ".gemini/settings.json", adapterGemini),
503			makeSpec(AgentOpenCode, "opencode.json", adapterOpenCode),
504			makeSpec(AgentOpenCode, "opencode.jsonc", adapterOpenCode),
505			makeSpec(AgentOpenCode, ".opencode/opencode.json", adapterOpenCode),
506			makeSpec(AgentOpenCode, ".opencode/opencode.jsonc", adapterOpenCode),
507		}
508	}
509	
510	func (s *Scanner) scanSource(ctx context.Context, spec sourceSpec, targets []Target, readSource func(context.Context, sourceSpec) readResult) ([]Declaration, []Diagnostic) {
511		read := readSource(ctx, spec)
512		if !read.present {
513			if read.code == "" {
514				return nil, nil
515			}
516			diagnostics := []Diagnostic{diagnosticFor(spec, read.code)}
517			if spec.adapter == adapterClaudeUser && len(targets) > 0 {
518				localSpec := spec
519				localSpec.scope = ScopeLocal
520				diagnostics = append(diagnostics, diagnosticFor(localSpec, read.code))
521			}
522			return nil, diagnostics
523		}
524		var rows []Declaration
525		var codes []DiagnosticCode
526		var diagnostics []Diagnostic
527		switch spec.adapter {
528		case adapterClaudeProject:
529			rows, codes = parseClaudeProject(read.data, spec)
530			approvalState := claudeProjectApprovalState{enabled: map[string]bool{}, disabled: map[string]bool{}}
531			for _, approvalSpec := range spec.approvalSources {
532				approval := readSource(ctx, approvalSpec)
533				switch {
534				case approval.code != "":
535					diagnostics = append(diagnostics, diagnosticFor(approvalSpec, approval.code))
536				case approval.present:
537					enabled, disabled, enableAll, code := parseClaudeProjectApproval(approval.data)
538					if code != "" {
539						diagnostics = append(diagnostics, diagnosticFor(approvalSpec, code))
540					} else {
541						approvalState.merge(enabled, disabled, enableAll)
542					}
543				}
544			}
545			applyClaudeProjectApproval(rows, approvalState.enabled, approvalState.disabled, approvalState.enableAll)
546		case adapterClaudeUser:
547			var localDiagnostics []Diagnostic
548			rows, codes, localDiagnostics = parseClaudeUser(read.data, spec, targets)
549			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, localDiagnostics...)
550		case adapterCodex:
551			rows, codes = parseCodex(read.data, spec)
552		case adapterCursor:
553			rows, codes = parseCursor(read.data, spec)
554		case adapterGemini:
555			rows, codes = parseGemini(read.data, spec)
556		case adapterOpenCode:
557			rows, codes = parseOpenCode(read.data, spec)
558		case adapterOpenCodePlist:
559			rows, codes = parseOpenCodePlist(read.data, spec)
560		default:
561			codes = []DiagnosticCode{DiagnosticMalformed}
562		}
563		if diagnostics == nil {
564			diagnostics = make([]Diagnostic, 0, len(codes))
565		}
566		for _, code := range codes {
567			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, diagnosticFor(spec, code))
568		}
569		return rows, diagnostics
570	}
571	
572	func diagnosticFor(spec sourceSpec, code DiagnosticCode) Diagnostic {
573		return Diagnostic{
574			Agent: spec.agent, Scope: spec.scope, Repository: spec.repository,
575			RepositoryPath: spec.repositoryPath, Checkout: spec.checkout,
576			LocalProjectPath: spec.localProjectPath, ConfigPath: spec.path,
577			Code: code, Message: diagnosticMessage(code),
578		}
579	}
580	
581	func finalizeResult(result *Result) {
582		SortDeclarations(result.Declarations)
583		sort.SliceStable(result.Diagnostics, func(i, j int) bool {
584			a, b := result.Diagnostics[i], result.Diagnostics[j]
585			ak := []string{string(a.Agent), scopeSortKey(a.Scope), strings.ToLower(a.Repository), a.RepositoryPath, a.Checkout, a.LocalProjectPath, a.ConfigPath, string(a.Code)}
586			bk := []string{string(b.Agent), scopeSortKey(b.Scope), strings.ToLower(b.Repository), b.RepositoryPath, b.Checkout, b.LocalProjectPath, b.ConfigPath, string(b.Code)}
587			for n := range ak {
588				if ak[n] != bk[n] {
589					return ak[n] < bk[n]
590				}
591			}
592			return false
593		})
594	}
```

```text
1	// Package safefile provides bounded reads that reject non-regular files
2	// without blocking on repository-controlled FIFOs.
3	package safefile
4	
5	import (
6		"bytes"
7		"context"
8		"errors"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	)
12	
13	var (
14		ErrNotRegular = errors.New("file is not regular")
15		ErrTooLarge   = errors.New("file exceeds size limit")
16	)
17	
18	// OpenRegular opens path without blocking on Unix special files and verifies
19	// the opened descriptor rather than trusting a path-level stat.
20	func OpenRegular(path string) (*os.File, os.FileInfo, error) {
21		file, err := openReadOnly(path)
22		if err != nil {
23			return nil, nil, err
24		}
25		info, err := file.Stat()
26		if err != nil {
27			_ = file.Close()
28			return nil, nil, err
29		}
30		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
31			_ = file.Close()
32			return nil, nil, ErrNotRegular
33		}
34		return file, info, nil
35	}
36	
37	// ReadAll reads at most max bytes from an already verified descriptor.
38	func ReadAll(ctx context.Context, file *os.File, max int64) ([]byte, error) {
39		if ctx == nil {
40			ctx = context.Background()
41		}
42		var body bytes.Buffer
43		chunk := make([]byte, 32*1024)
44		for {
45			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
46				return nil, err
47			}
48			n, readErr := file.Read(chunk)
49			if n > 0 {
50				if int64(body.Len()+n) > max {
51					return nil, ErrTooLarge
52				}
53				_, _ = body.Write(chunk[:n])
54			}
55			if readErr != nil {
56				if errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
57					return body.Bytes(), nil
58				}
59				return nil, readErr
60			}
61		}
62	}
63	
64	// ReadRegular opens and reads a regular file under a hard byte bound.
65	func ReadRegular(ctx context.Context, path string, max int64) ([]byte, error) {
66		file, info, err := OpenRegular(path)
67		if err != nil {
68			return nil, err
69		}
70		defer file.Close()
71		if info.Size() > max {
72			return nil, ErrTooLarge
73		}
74		return ReadAll(ctx, file, max)
75	}
```

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Evaluating file path semantics**

I need to think about the file path derivation that should be domain-owned. The skill row Path seems to point to a skill directory, but the comment about Installation.Path being a directory might be accurate. The code build likely uses `Path: chosen.realPath` as its physical directory. Also, the UI appears to assume that SKILL.md is joined. If agentskill changes to report a different path, TUI could break. It looks like the domain should provide `ContentPath()` or `EditablePath()`.  

I'm noticing that the missing skill uses a lock file, but when I try to "open skill file," it actually opens the provider lock for the missing row, which is a bit misleading, but maybe it’s intentional since the skill might not have a local version. Hmm, it feels like there could be deeper capability issues in resource locating. 

The MCP ConfigPath is identified as the scanner source path, and it makes me wonder if editing the managed/system config is really appropriate? However, the feature does allow for it. It’s curious that both Open and Raw files utilize the same capability path, yet raw MCP config could expose sensitive information. 

**Analyzing summary formatting**

I’m exploring how the new `formatSkillSummary` and `formatMCPSummary` might duplicate domain/CLI output sanitization. The `formatMCPSummary` creates a "safe summary" from specific fields, deciding what's sensitive versus safe, while the `agentmcp` domain manages redaction. If I add a sensitive field to the Declaration, the UI formatter might accidentally include it; however, it only lists explicit fields, so that might keep it safer. But any change in safe fields would require updates across all renderers. 

It's interesting to consider how `formatMCPSummary` sanitizes the `Endpoint`, ensuring redactions through the scanner, which might help. But the summary seems to differ from the detail, suggesting maybe there's no general summary formatter in the domain, so generalization for safe presentation could be beneficial.

Meanwhile, methods like `ReadFile` and `OpenFile` introduced generic Actions callbacks, but only in a capability-specific way; it feels like there could be potential for deeper file service, though not fragile enough yet. 

**Exploring MCP width calculations**

I'm considering the new MCP width helper, `mcpServerWidth(minimum, available)`, which loops over `m.mcp` instead of `visibleMCP()`. This means hidden rows will influence the width calculation, potentially causing hidden servers to shrink other content without affecting abstraction-depth. The maximum calculation seems to be `max(minimum, min(32, available))`, so if the available width is negative, it may lead to issues like table overflow. 

I'm also thinking that we could implement a one-off responsive column algorithm specific for MCP, rather than a general table layout, even though each skill and repo has unique thresholds and widths. If we add a long server, that could get tricky!

```text
72	func (m *Model) prepareRepoDependentForReload(view View, enabled bool) {
73		if !enabled {
74			return
75		}
76		state := m.viewLoad(view)
77		switch {
78		case state.loading || m.view == view:
79			m.beginViewLoad(view, loadRefresh)
80			m.setViewStatus(view, "waiting for local repositories…")
81		case state.hasSnapshot:
82			m.invalidateView(view)
83		}
84	}

86	func (m *Model) beginViewLoad(view View, cause loadCause) uint64 {
87		if view == ViewRepos {
88			m.prepareRepoDependentsForReload()
89		}
90		index := int(view)
91		if cancel := m.loadCancels[index]; cancel != nil {
92			cancel()
93		}
94		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(m.baseContext())
95		m.loadContexts[index] = ctx
96		m.loadCancels[index] = cancel
97		if view == ViewRepos && m.remoteClone.phase == remoteCloneRefreshing {
98			// A newer REPOS generation may supersede the clone-triggered refresh.
99			// Cancellation must always follow the generation that can complete it.
100			m.remoteClone.cancel = cancel
101		}
102		state := &m.loads[index]
103		state.generation++
104		state.cause = cause
105		state.requested = true
106		state.loading = true
107		state.outcome = ""
108		m.viewErrors[int(view)] = nil
109		m.viewStatuses[int(view)] = ""
110		m.trace.Mark(perftrace.TUIViewLoadRequested, perftrace.Fields{
111			View: view.traceView(), Stage: perftrace.StageRequested, Generation: state.generation,
112		})
113		return state.generation
114	}

116	func (m *Model) beginLocalLoads(cause loadCause) (tasks, repos, tries uint64) {
117		if m.localCancel != nil {
118			m.localCancel()
119		}
120		m.localContext, m.localCancel = context.WithCancel(m.baseContext())
121		m.localGeneration++
122		tasks = m.beginViewLoad(ViewTasks, cause)
123		repos = m.beginViewLoad(ViewRepos, cause)
124		tries = m.beginViewLoad(ViewTries, cause)
125		if m.remoteClone.phase == remoteCloneRefreshing {
126			// Production's shared loader reads localContext rather than the per-view
127			// context created above, so cancellation follows the actual producer.
128			m.remoteClone.cancel = m.localCancel
129		}
130		return tasks, repos, tries
131	}

134		if m.localContext != nil {

143			m.localCancel, m.localContext = nil, nil

145	}

147	func (m *Model) invalidateView(view View) {
148		index := int(view)
149		if cancel := m.loadCancels[index]; cancel != nil {
150			cancel()
151		}
152		m.loadCancels[index], m.loadContexts[index] = nil, nil
153		state := &m.loads[index]
154		state.generation++
155		state.requested = false
156		state.loading = false
157		state.outcome = ""
158		if state.hasSnapshot {
159			state.freshness = perftrace.FreshnessStale
160		}
161		m.viewErrors[index] = nil
162		m.viewStatuses[index] = ""
163	}

166		m.beginViewLoad(ViewTries, cause)

169		}

172	func (m *Model) seedViewSnapshot(view View, source perftrace.Source, freshness perftrace.Freshness, actionable bool) {
173		state := &m.loads[int(view)]

176		state.freshness = freshness
177		state.outcome = perftrace.OutcomeSuccess

186				Generation: generation, Outcome: perftrace.OutcomeSuperseded,
187			})
```

```text
2	// without blocking on repository-controlled FIFOs.
3	package safefile
4	
5	import (
6		"bytes"
7		"context"
8		"errors"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	)
12	
13	var (
14		ErrNotRegular = errors.New("file is not regular")
15		ErrTooLarge   = errors.New("file exceeds size limit")
16	)
17	
18	// OpenRegular opens path without blocking on Unix special files and verifies
19	// the opened descriptor rather than trusting a path-level stat.
20	func OpenRegular(path string) (*os.File, os.FileInfo, error) {
21		file, err := openReadOnly(path)
22		if err != nil {
23			return nil, nil, err
24		}
25		info, err := file.Stat()
26		if err != nil {
27			_ = file.Close()
28			return nil, nil, err
29		}
30		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
31			_ = file.Close()
32			return nil, nil, ErrNotRegular
33		}
34		return file, info, nil
35	}
36	
37	// ReadAll reads at most max bytes from an already verified descriptor.
38	func ReadAll(ctx context.Context, file *os.File, max int64) ([]byte, error) {
39		if ctx == nil {
40			ctx = context.Background()
41		}
42		var body bytes.Buffer
43		chunk := make([]byte, 32*1024)
44		for {
45			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
46				return nil, err
47			}
48			n, readErr := file.Read(chunk)
49			if n > 0 {
50				if int64(body.Len()+n) > max {
51					return nil, ErrTooLarge
52				}
53				_, _ = body.Write(chunk[:n])
54			}
55			if readErr != nil {
56				if errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
57					return body.Bytes(), nil
58				}
59				return nil, readErr
60			}
61		}
62	}
63	
64	// ReadRegular opens and reads a regular file under a hard byte bound.
65	func ReadRegular(ctx context.Context, path string, max int64) ([]byte, error) {
66		file, info, err := OpenRegular(path)
67		if err != nil {
68			return nil, err
69		}
70		defer file.Close()
71		if info.Size() > max {
72			return nil, ErrTooLarge
73		}
74		return ReadAll(ctx, file, max)
75	}
76
```

```text
17	func (s *Scanner) readSourceFromDisk(ctx context.Context, spec sourceSpec) readResult {
18		if ctx.Err() != nil {
19			return readResult{}
20		}
21		resolved, err := resolveBoundedSymlinks(spec.path, s.options.MaxSymlinkDepth)
22		if err != nil {
23			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
24				return readResult{}
25			}
26			if errors.Is(err, errSymlinkLimit) {
27				return readResult{code: DiagnosticSymlinkLimit}
28			}
29			return readResult{code: DiagnosticUnreadable}
30		}
31		if spec.projectRoot != "" {
32			inside, err := pathx.Contains(spec.projectRoot, resolved)
33			if err != nil || !inside {
34				return readResult{code: DiagnosticProjectSymlinkEscape}
35			}
36		}
37	
38		file, openedInfo, err := safefile.OpenRegular(resolved)
39		if err != nil {
40			switch {
41			case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
42				return readResult{}
43			case errors.Is(err, safefile.ErrNotRegular):
44				return readResult{code: DiagnosticNotRegular}
45			default:
46				return readResult{code: DiagnosticUnreadable}
47			}
48		}
49		defer file.Close()
50		if openedInfo.Size() > s.options.MaxFileBytes {
51			return readResult{code: DiagnosticTooLarge}
52		}
53		if spec.projectRoot != "" {
54			currentPath, err := resolveBoundedSymlinks(spec.path, s.options.MaxSymlinkDepth)
55			if err != nil {
56				return readResult{code: DiagnosticProjectSymlinkEscape}
57			}
58			inside, err := pathx.Contains(spec.projectRoot, currentPath)
59			currentInfo, statErr := os.Stat(currentPath)
60			if err != nil || !inside || statErr != nil || !os.SameFile(openedInfo, currentInfo) {
61				return readResult{code: DiagnosticProjectSymlinkEscape}
62			}
63		}
64	
65		body, err := safefile.ReadAll(ctx, file, s.options.MaxFileBytes)
66		if err != nil {
67			switch {
68			case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled), errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
69				return readResult{}
70			case errors.Is(err, safefile.ErrTooLarge):
71				return readResult{code: DiagnosticTooLarge}
72			default:
73				return readResult{code: DiagnosticUnreadable}
74			}
75		}
76		return readResult{data: body, present: true}
```

```text
216			StaticDeclarationsOnly: true,

228	type Filter struct {
229		Agent          Agent
230		Scope          Scope

232		Transport      Transport

235		Enabled        *bool
236		HasCredentials *bool
237	}
238	
239	// Match reports whether a declaration satisfies f.
240	func (f Filter) Match(d Declaration) bool {
241		if f.Agent != "" && d.Agent != f.Agent ||
242			f.Scope != "" && d.Scope != f.Scope ||
243			f.Source != "" && d.Source != f.Source ||
244			f.Transport != "" && d.Transport != f.Transport ||
245			f.Repository != "" && d.Repository != f.Repository {
246			return false
247		}
248		if f.NameContains != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(d.Name), strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(f.NameContains))) {
249			return false
250		}
251		if f.Enabled != nil && (d.Enabled == nil || *d.Enabled != *f.Enabled) {
252			return false
253		}
254		if f.HasCredentials != nil && (len(d.Credentials) > 0) != *f.HasCredentials {
255			return false
256		}
257		return true
258	}
259	
260	// FilterDeclarations returns matching rows without changing their order.
261	func FilterDeclarations(rows []Declaration, f Filter) []Declaration {
262		out := make([]Declaration, 0, len(rows))
263		for _, row := range rows {
264			if f.Match(row) {
265				out = append(out, row)
266			}
267		}
268		return out
269	}

271	// SortDeclarations establishes the stable order used by Scan.
272	func SortDeclarations(rows []Declaration) {
273		sort.SliceStable(rows, func(i, j int) bool {
274			a, b := rows[i], rows[j]
275			ak := []string{string(a.Agent), scopeSortKey(a.Scope), strings.ToLower(a.Repository), a.RepositoryPath, a.Checkout, a.LocalProjectPath, a.ConfigPath, string(a.Source), strings.ToLower(a.Plugin), a.Plugin, strings.ToLower(a.Name), a.Name}
276			bk := []string{string(b.Agent), scopeSortKey(b.Scope), strings.ToLower(b.Repository), b.RepositoryPath, b.Checkout, b.LocalProjectPath, b.ConfigPath, string(b.Source), strings.ToLower(b.Plugin), b.Plugin, strings.ToLower(b.Name), b.Name}
277			for n := range ak {
278				if ak[n] != bk[n] {
279					return ak[n] < bk[n]
280				}
281			}
282			return false
283		})
284	}
285	
286	func scopeSortKey(scope Scope) string {

290		case ScopeLocal:
291			return "1-local"
292		case ScopeUser:
293			return "2-user"
294		case ScopeCustom:
```

```text
403		sort.Slice(installations, func(i, j int) bool {
404			if installations[i].RealPath != installations[j].RealPath {
405				return installations[i].RealPath < installations[j].RealPath
406			}
407			return installations[i].Path < installations[j].Path
408		})
409		var agents []string

411			agents = append(agents, installation.AgentIDs...)
412		}
413		agentIDs := uniqueSorted(agents)
414		agents = agentDisplayNames(agentIDs)
415		row := Skill{

421			ManagedBy: ManagedByExternal, UpdateStatus: UpdateUnknown,

424		if len(installations) > 0 {

427		if directManagedSkillName(name) {

429				row.ManagedBy = ManagedByDev
430				row.Source = "dev binary"

482	func applyBundledIntegrity(row *Skill) {
483		files, err := skill.Files()

490		row.IntegrityDetail = "all embedded files match this dev binary"
491		for index := range row.Installations {
492			status, detail := bundledIntegrity(row.Installations[index].RealPath, files)
493			row.Installations[index].Integrity = status
494			row.Installations[index].IntegrityDetail = detail
```

```text
12	// AgentSkillOptions selects native scopes and the explicit remote freshness
13	// pass. With neither scope selected, project and global rows are both returned.
14	type AgentSkillOptions struct {
15		Project bool
16		Global  bool
17		Check   bool
18		Limiter *Limiter
19	}
20	
21	// CollectAgentSkills scans each repository target through the shared local
22	// process limiter, scans global paths once, and only then groups remote source
23	// checks across the complete result.
24	func CollectAgentSkills(ctx context.Context, targets []agenttarget.Target, options AgentSkillOptions) (agentskill.Result, error) {
25		if ctx == nil {
26			ctx = context.Background()
27		}
28		project, global := options.Project, options.Global
29		if !project && !global {
30			project, global = true, true
31		}
32		targets = agenttarget.Dedupe(targets)
33		partCount := 0
34		if project {
35			partCount += len(targets)
36		}
37		globalIndex := -1
38		if global {
39			globalIndex = partCount
40			partCount++
41		}
42		parts := make([]agentskill.Result, partCount)
43		errs := make([]error, partCount)
44		limiter := options.Limiter
45		if limiter == nil {
46			limiter = NewLimiter(8)
47		}
48	
49		var wait sync.WaitGroup
50		launch := func(index int, scan func() (agentskill.Result, error)) {
51			wait.Go(func() {
52				release, ok := limiter.Acquire(ctx)
53				if !ok {
54					errs[index] = ctx.Err()
55					return
56				}
57				defer release()
58				parts[index], errs[index] = scan()
59			})
60		}
61		if project {
62			for index, target := range targets {
63				target := target
64				launch(index, func() (agentskill.Result, error) {
65					return agentskill.Scan(ctx, []agenttarget.Target{target}, agentskill.ListOptions{Project: true})
66				})
67			}
68		}
69		if global {
70			launch(globalIndex, func() (agentskill.Result, error) {
71				return agentskill.Scan(ctx, nil, agentskill.ListOptions{Global: true})
72			})
73		}
74		wait.Wait()
75	
76		result := agentskill.MergeResults(parts...)
77		if options.Check && ctx.Err() == nil {
78			result.Skills = agentskill.CheckUpdates(ctx, result.Skills)
79		}
80		joined := errors.Join(errs...)
81		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
82			joined = errors.Join(joined, ctxErr)
83		}
84		return result, joined
85	}
```

```text
217	func Scan(ctx context.Context, targets []Target) (Result, error) {
218		return NewScanner(DefaultOptions()).Scan(ctx, targets)
219	}
220	
221	// Scan returns all static declarations it can decode and fixed diagnostics for
222	// individual source failures. Cancellation is the only normal top-level scan
223	// failure and is returned as ctx.Err(), with any rows already collected.
224	func (s *Scanner) Scan(ctx context.Context, targets []Target) (Result, error) {
225		if ctx == nil {
226			ctx = context.Background()
227		}
228		targets = normalizeTargets(targets, s.options.WorkingDirectory)
229		result := Result{
230			Declarations: make([]Declaration, 0),
231			Diagnostics:  make([]Diagnostic, 0),
232			Coverage:     defaultCoverage(),
233		}
234		type cachedRead struct {
235			ready  chan struct{}
236			result readResult
237		}
238		var readMu sync.Mutex
239		reads := map[string]*cachedRead{}
240		readSource := func(ctx context.Context, spec sourceSpec) readResult {
241			key := spec.path + "\x00" + spec.projectRoot
242			readMu.Lock()
243			entry := reads[key]
244			if entry == nil {
245				entry = &cachedRead{ready: make(chan struct{})}
246				reads[key] = entry
247				readMu.Unlock()
248				entry.result = s.readSource(ctx, spec)
249				close(entry.ready)
250				return entry.result
251			}
252			readMu.Unlock()
253			select {
254			case <-ctx.Done():
255				return readResult{}
256			case <-entry.ready:
257				return entry.result
258			}
259		}
260	
261		for _, spec := range s.hostSources() {
262			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
263				finalizeResult(&result)
264				return result, err
265			}
266			rows, diagnostics := s.scanSource(ctx, spec, targets, readSource)
267			result.Declarations = append(result.Declarations, rows...)
268			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, diagnostics...)
269		}
270		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
271			finalizeResult(&result)
272			return result, err
273		}
274	
275		projectResults := make([]Result, len(targets))
276		jobs := make(chan int)
277		workers := s.options.Concurrency
278		if workers > len(targets) {
279			workers = len(targets)
280		}
281		var wg sync.WaitGroup
282		for range workers {
283			wg.Add(1)
284			go func() {
285				defer wg.Done()
286				for {
287					select {
288					case <-ctx.Done():
289						return
290					case index, ok := <-jobs:
291						if !ok {
292							return
293						}
294						for _, spec := range s.projectSources(targets[index]) {
295							if ctx.Err() != nil {
296								return
297							}
298							rows, diagnostics := s.scanSource(ctx, spec, nil, readSource)
299							projectResults[index].Declarations = append(projectResults[index].Declarations, rows...)
300							projectResults[index].Diagnostics = append(projectResults[index].Diagnostics, diagnostics...)
301						}
302					}
303				}
304			}()
305		}
306		for index := range targets {
307			select {
308			case jobs <- index:
309			case <-ctx.Done():
310				close(jobs)
311				wg.Wait()
312				for _, partial := range projectResults {
313					result.Declarations = append(result.Declarations, partial.Declarations...)
314					result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, partial.Diagnostics...)
315				}
316				finalizeResult(&result)
317				return result, ctx.Err()
318			}
319		}
320		close(jobs)
321		wg.Wait()
```

```text
160	// look like:
161	//
162	//	ESC [ < Cb ; Cx ; Cy (M or m)
163	//
164	// where:
165	//
166	//	Cb is the encoded button code
167	//	Cx is the x-coordinate of the mouse
168	//	Cy is the y-coordinate of the mouse
169	//	M is for button press, m is for button release
170	//
171	// https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html#h3-Extended-coordinates
172	func parseSGRMouseEvent(buf []byte) MouseEvent {
173		str := string(buf[3:])
174		matches := mouseSGRRegex.FindStringSubmatch(str)
175		if len(matches) != 5 { //nolint:gomnd
176			// Unreachable, we already checked the regex in `detectOneMsg`.
177			panic("invalid mouse event")
178		}
179	
180		b, _ := strconv.Atoi(matches[1])
181		px := matches[2]
182		py := matches[3]
183		release := matches[4] == "m"
184		m := parseMouseButton(b, true)
185	
186		// Wheel buttons don't have release events
187		// Motion can be reported as a release event in some terminals (Windows Terminal)
188		if m.Action != MouseActionMotion && !m.IsWheel() && release {
189			m.Action = MouseActionRelease
190			m.Type = MouseRelease
191		}
192	
193		x, _ := strconv.Atoi(px)
194		y, _ := strconv.Atoi(py)
195	
196		// (1,1) is the upper left. We subtract 1 to normalize it to (0,0).
197		m.X = x - 1
198		m.Y = y - 1
199	
200		return m
201	}
202	
203	const x10MouseByteOffset = 32
204	
205	// Parse X10-encoded mouse events; the simplest kind. The last release of X10
206	// was December 1986, by the way. The original X10 mouse protocol limits the Cx
207	// and Cy coordinates to 223 (=255-032).
208	//
209	// X10 mouse events look like:
210	//
211	//	ESC [M Cb Cx Cy
212	//
213	// See: http://www.xfree86.org/current/ctlseqs.html#Mouse%20Tracking
214	func parseX10MouseEvent(buf []byte) MouseEvent {
215		v := buf[3:6]
216		m := parseMouseButton(int(v[0]), false)
217	
218		// (1,1) is the upper left. We subtract 1 to normalize it to (0,0).
219		m.X = int(v[1]) - x10MouseByteOffset - 1
220		m.Y = int(v[2]) - x10MouseByteOffset - 1
221	
222		return m
223	}
224	
225	// See: https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html#h3-Extended-coordinates
226	func parseMouseButton(b int, isSGR bool) MouseEvent {
227		var m MouseEvent
228		e := b
229		if !isSGR {
230			e -= x10MouseByteOffset
231		}
232	
233		const (
234			bitShift  = 0b0000_0100
235			bitAlt    = 0b0000_1000
236			bitCtrl   = 0b0001_0000
237			bitMotion = 0b0010_0000
238			bitWheel  = 0b0100_0000
239			bitAdd    = 0b1000_0000 // additional buttons 8-11
240	
241			bitsMask = 0b0000_0011
242		)
243	
244		if e&bitAdd != 0 {
245			m.Button = MouseButtonBackward + MouseButton(e&bitsMask)
246		} else if e&bitWheel != 0 {
247			m.Button = MouseButtonWheelUp + MouseButton(e&bitsMask)
248		} else {
249			m.Button = MouseButtonLeft + MouseButton(e&bitsMask)
250			// X10 reports a button release as 0b0000_0011 (3)
251			if e&bitsMask == bitsMask {
252				m.Action = MouseActionRelease
253				m.Button = MouseButtonNone
254			}
255		}
256	
257		// Motion bit doesn't get reported for wheel events.
258		if e&bitMotion != 0 && !m.IsWheel() {
259			m.Action = MouseActionMotion
260		}
261	
262		// Modifiers
263		m.Alt = e&bitAlt != 0
264		m.Ctrl = e&bitCtrl != 0
265		m.Shift = e&bitShift != 0
266	
267		// backward compatibility
268		switch {
269		case m.Button == MouseButtonLeft && m.Action == MouseActionPress:
270			m.Type = MouseLeft
271		case m.Button == MouseButtonMiddle && m.Action == MouseActionPress:
272			m.Type = MouseMiddle
273		case m.Button == MouseButtonRight && m.Action == MouseActionPress:
274			m.Type = MouseRight
275		case m.Button == MouseButtonNone && m.Action == MouseActionRelease:
276			m.Type = MouseRelease
277		case m.Button == MouseButtonWheelUp && m.Action == MouseActionPress:
278			m.Type = MouseWheelUp
279		case m.Button == MouseButtonWheelDown && m.Action == MouseActionPress:
280			m.Type = MouseWheelDown
281		case m.Button == MouseButtonWheelLeft && m.Action == MouseActionPress:
282			m.Type = MouseWheelLeft
283		case m.Button == MouseButtonWheelRight && m.Action == MouseActionPress:
284			m.Type = MouseWheelRight
285		case m.Button == MouseButtonBackward && m.Action == MouseActionPress:
286			m.Type = MouseBackward
287		case m.Button == MouseButtonForward && m.Action == MouseActionPress:
288			m.Type = MouseForward
289		case m.Action == MouseActionMotion:
290			m.Type = MouseMotion
291			switch m.Button { //nolint:exhaustive
292			case MouseButtonLeft:
293				m.Type = MouseLeft
294			case MouseButtonMiddle:
295				m.Type = MouseMiddle
296			case MouseButtonRight:
297				m.Type = MouseRight
298			case MouseButtonBackward:
299				m.Type = MouseBackward
300			case MouseButtonForward:
301				m.Type = MouseForward
302			}
303		default:
304			m.Type = MouseUnknown
305		}
306	
307		return m
308	}
309
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
197	func shellQuote(s string) string {

202		for _, r := range s {
```

```text
1	// Package safefile provides bounded reads that reject non-regular files
2	// without blocking on repository-controlled FIFOs.
3	package safefile
4	
5	import (
6		"bytes"
7		"context"
8		"errors"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	)
12	
13	var (
14		ErrNotRegular = errors.New("file is not regular")
15		ErrTooLarge   = errors.New("file exceeds size limit")
16	)
17	
18	// OpenRegular opens path without blocking on Unix special files and verifies
19	// the opened descriptor rather than trusting a path-level stat.
20	func OpenRegular(path string) (*os.File, os.FileInfo, error) {
21		file, err := openReadOnly(path)
22		if err != nil {
23			return nil, nil, err
24		}
25		info, err := file.Stat()
26		if err != nil {
27			_ = file.Close()
28			return nil, nil, err
29		}
30		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
31			_ = file.Close()
32			return nil, nil, ErrNotRegular
33		}
34		return file, info, nil
35	}
36	
37	// ReadAll reads at most max bytes from an already verified descriptor.
38	func ReadAll(ctx context.Context, file *os.File, max int64) ([]byte, error) {
39		if ctx == nil {
40			ctx = context.Background()
41		}
42		var body bytes.Buffer
43		chunk := make([]byte, 32*1024)
44		for {
45			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
46				return nil, err
47			}
48			n, readErr := file.Read(chunk)
49			if n > 0 {
50				if int64(body.Len()+n) > max {
51					return nil, ErrTooLarge
52				}
53				_, _ = body.Write(chunk[:n])
54			}
55			if readErr != nil {
56				if errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
57					return body.Bytes(), nil
58				}
59				return nil, readErr
60			}
61		}
62	}
63	
64	// ReadRegular opens and reads a regular file under a hard byte bound.
65	func ReadRegular(ctx context.Context, path string, max int64) ([]byte, error) {
66		file, info, err := OpenRegular(path)
67		if err != nil {
68			return nil, err
69		}
70		defer file.Close()
71		if info.Size() > max {
72			return nil, ErrTooLarge
73		}
74		return ReadAll(ctx, file, max)
75	}
76
```

```text
1	# Context
2	
3	The dashboard is keyboard-first today, so a user cannot click a visible tab or row and there is no common row-action surface. SKILLS and MCP correctly default to the exact startup context, but there is no session-level way to inspect every repository; MCP also lets the `SERVER` column consume all extra terminal width, which pushes `TRANSPORT`, `STATE`, and `SOURCE` far away on wide screens. Finally, capability rows expose configuration paths but cannot open or copy those files.
4	
5	Add mouse input as an enhancement without weakening keyboard behavior, keep startup-context capability discovery as the default, offer a shared context/all toggle, compact MCP’s table, and give SKILLS/MCP explicit local-file open/copy actions. Per the requested local-tool behavior, raw configuration copying is supported as an explicit action; it never uploads or contacts a server, but the UI/docs will note that the entire file may contain credentials and enters the system clipboard.
6	
7	## 1. Add shared mouse geometry and dispatch
8	
9	- Start the dashboard with `tea.WithMouseCellMotion()` beside `tea.WithAltScreen()` in `internal/cli/tui.go`. This supports clicks, releases, drag, and wheel without enabling noisy all-motion tracking; Bubble Tea restores terminal mouse state on exit.
10	- Add focused mouse logic in a new `internal/tui/mouse.go` and route `tea.MouseMsg` from `Model.Update` with the same precedence as keyboard input:
11	  - active note/input/help/form/confirmation/stat/copy modes do not pass clicks through to the list;
12	  - the common action menu handles its own clicks and wheel;
13	  - an active clone still permits tab switching, row selection, and wheel navigation, but not context actions.
14	- Define the interaction contract:
15	  - unmodified left-button press on a rendered tab switches directly to it and calls existing `afterViewSwitch` so lazy loading and cursor clamping remain intact;
16	  - unmodified left-button press on a visible data row selects only;
17	  - unmodified right-button press selects the row and opens its action menu;
18	  - wheel up/down over the list body moves three rows through existing `setAt`; horizontal wheel, motion, releases, extra buttons, and modified clicks are ignored;
19	  - do not infer double-clicks or open rows on click—Enter/`o` and menu actions remain the explicit activation paths.
20	- Refactor `internal/tui/view.go:renderHeader` into one pure header-layout helper returning both the rendered line and visible tab cell spans. Compute spans with `lipgloss.Width` so full, summary-free, compact, and current-tab-only layouts cannot drift from hit testing.
21	- Derive row hitboxes from existing `listPreambleLines`, `listHeight`, and `window` results. Map only rendered data rows (`2 + listPreambleLines()` onward) back to `window.from + offset`; reject the header, loading banner, scroll note, detail, and footer. Do not persist coordinates from a prior `View`, so resize/filter/load changes recompute geometry from current model state.
22	
23	## 2. Generalize the row action menu for every tab
24	
25	- Evolve the Try-only menu in `internal/tui/overlay.go` into a generic full-screen row action overlay while retaining the existing form/confirmation overlays.
26	- Represent menu entries with a small `listAction` enum and fixed-size value arrays in `overlayState`; do not store closures, maps, or shared mutable slices in the value-copied Bubble Tea model.
27	- Pin the menu to a `selectionToken` containing the view and a stable row identity (task ID; canonical repo plus checkout path; host plus repo path; Try catalog ID; existing remote identity; Skill scope/checkout/path/name; MCP agent/scope/config path/project/plugin/name). Re-resolve before execution and fail closed if a refresh removed or changed the target instead of acting on the current cursor index.
28	- Extract menu-visible behavior from `updateList` into a shared `runListAction(actionID)` dispatcher. Keyboard bindings and right-click choices call the same action implementation; mouse code must not invoke domain callbacks directly or synthesize key messages.
29	- Build each menu from actions that are actually legal for that row, omitting unavailable choices rather than rendering misleading disabled entries. Reuse the existing operations across all tabs: open, notes/task lifecycle, worktree expansion/metadata/start/copy/stats, fleet open, Try lifecycle, remote clone/open, Skill add/check/update/config actions, and MCP config actions. Destructive or multi-step actions continue through their existing prompt/form/confirmation flow.
30	- In the menu, left-clicking an option selects and executes it, wheel moves the menu cursor by one, clicking outside closes it, and all keyboard `j/k`, Enter, and Escape behavior remains available.
31	
32	## 3. Add a shared SKILLS/MCP context/all scope
33	
34	- Add an exported value enum in `internal/tui` (startup context vs all repositories) and a `capabilityScope` field on `Model`, defaulting to startup context.
35	- Change `Actions.ReloadSkills`, `ReloadSkillsWithRepos`, `ReloadMCP`, and `ReloadMCPWithRepos` to receive that scope. Capture it in `reloadSkills`, `reloadUpdatedSkill`, and `reloadMCP` so every producer is bound to the generation and scope that started it.
36	- Bind uppercase `A` in both SKILLS and MCP to toggle the shared session-only scope; lowercase `a` remains Skill installation. Show `A scope:context` or `A scope:all` in both footers/help and reserve `A` in `internal/config/config.go` so an external tool cannot shadow it.
37	- On toggle, cancel and generation-bump both capability loads, clear old-scope rows/errors/warnings/check state and reset both cursors. Immediately load the current capability view; leave the other invalidated so it preserves existing lazy-load behavior and loads under the new scope when visited. If REPOS is still loading, use the existing waiting path; if it failed terminally, surface that dependency error. Late results from the old scope must be rejected by existing generation checks.

39	  - startup context keeps current behavior—inside Git, only the exact startup checkout; outside Git, accepted non-Try REPOS targets plus the ordinary startup directory;

41	- Preserve the selected scope across manual refresh, configuration refresh, REPOS refresh, Skill update/check, and tab changes. Do not implement this as a post-scan row filter: target selection controls which project-local declarations are read.

46	  - `OpenFile(path)` returns an editor process for `tea.ExecProcess`;
47	  - `ReadFile(ctx, path)` returns bounded local regular-file contents for the existing clipboard callback.

51	  - a missing/lock-only Skill uses `Skill.Lock.File` when present;
52	  - MCP uses `Declaration.ConfigPath` and never executes `Declaration.Command` or opens `Declaration.Endpoint`.
53	- Make `e` open that selected capability file in `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR`. On successful return, reload only the originating SKILLS or MCP view under the current capability scope; do not run the dev `config.toml` reload path.
54	- Generalize `modeCopy`/copy helpers without changing existing REPOS chords:
55	  - SKILLS: copy selected file path, deterministic sanitized row summary, sanitized source URL, or raw selected file contents;
56	  - MCP: copy `ConfigPath`, deterministic sanitized declaration summary, or raw `ConfigPath` contents;

58	- Keep safe summaries limited to normalized inventory fields. Raw copy is separately and clearly labeled “copy raw file”; for MCP it copies the entire source file, which may include other server declarations, tokens, headers, env/OAuth material, or helper commands. Report clipboard/read failures with capability-specific messages rather than the current REPOS-only `dev repo context` fallback.
59	
60	## 5. Compact MCP’s responsive table
61	
62	- Replace the unbounded `serverW = max(minimum, width-budget)` logic in `internal/tui/view.go:renderMCP` with a helper based on the widest server name in the full accepted MCP snapshot (not the filtered rows):
```

```text
13	func resolverOutcome(err error) perftrace.Outcome {

16		}

20	// tuiRuntimeResolver moves runtime auto-detection off the first-view path while
21	// sharing exactly one result across inventory loads and actions.
22	type tuiRuntimeResolver struct {
23		trace   *perftrace.Recorder
24		resolve func() runtime.Runtime
25		once    sync.Once
26		ready   chan struct{}
27		rt      runtime.Runtime
28	}

30	func newTUIRuntimeResolver(app *App) *tuiRuntimeResolver {
31		snapshot := *app
32		return &tuiRuntimeResolver{
33			trace: app.trace, resolve: snapshot.Runtime, ready: make(chan struct{}),
34		}
35	}
36	
37	func (r *tuiRuntimeResolver) Resolve(ctx context.Context) (runtime.Runtime, error) {
38		r.once.Do(func() {
39			go func() {
40				finish := r.trace.Start(perftrace.TUIRuntimeResolve, perftrace.Fields{})
41				r.rt = r.resolve()
42				finish(perftrace.OutcomeSuccess)
43				close(r.ready)
44			}()
45		})
46		if ctx == nil {
47			ctx = context.Background()
48		}
49		select {
50		case <-ctx.Done():
51			return nil, ctx.Err()
52		case <-r.ready:
53			return r.rt, nil
54		}
55	}
```

```text
300				diagnostics = append(diagnostics, decorateDiagnostic(Diagnostic{
301					Kind: DiagnosticSkillFrontmatter, Scope: scope,
302					Path: filepath.Join(child, "SKILL.md"), Message: err.Error(),
303				}, target))
304				continue
305			}
306			physical := child
307			if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(child); err == nil {
308				physical = filepath.Clean(resolved)
309			}
310			var logicalPaths, agentIDs []string
311			for _, logical := range location.Logical {
312				logicalPaths = append(logicalPaths, filepath.Join(logical.Path, entry.Name()))
313				agentIDs = append(agentIDs, logical.AgentIDs...)
314			}
315			logicalPaths = uniqueSorted(logicalPaths)
316			agentIDs = uniqueSorted(agentIDs)
317			installation := Installation{
318				RealPath: physical, LogicalPaths: logicalPaths, AgentIDs: agentIDs,
319				Attribution: registryAttribution(agentIDs), Integrity: IntegrityUnknown,
320			}
321			if len(logicalPaths) > 0 {
322				installation.Path = logicalPaths[0]
323			}
324			skills = append(skills, scannedSkill{Name: name, Installation: installation})
325		}
326		return skills, diagnostics
327	}
328	
329	func readSkillName(filename string) (string, bool, error) {
330		file, _, err := safefile.OpenRegular(filename)
331		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
332			return "", false, nil
333		}
334		if errors.Is(err, safefile.ErrNotRegular) {
335			return "", true, errors.New("SKILL.md is not a regular file")
336		}
337		if err != nil {
338			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("could not read SKILL.md: %w", err)
339		}
340		defer file.Close()
341	
342		// Bound only the frontmatter, not the skill body. A valid skill may have a
343		// large reference body, and inventory never needs to read it.
344		reader := bufio.NewReader(io.LimitReader(file, maxFrontmatterBytes+1))
345		first, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
346		consumed := int64(len(first))
347		if readErr != nil && !errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
348			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("could not read SKILL.md: %w", readErr)
349		}
350		first = strings.TrimPrefix(first, string(rune(0xfeff)))
351		if strings.TrimSpace(first) != "---" {
352			return "", true, errors.New("SKILL.md must begin with YAML frontmatter")
353		}
354		var frontmatter strings.Builder
355		closed := false
356		for {
357			line, lineErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
358			consumed += int64(len(line))
359			if consumed > maxFrontmatterBytes {
360				return "", true, fmt.Errorf("SKILL.md frontmatter exceeds %d bytes", maxFrontmatterBytes)
361			}
362			if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "---" {
363				closed = true
364				break
365			}
366			frontmatter.WriteString(line)
367			if lineErr != nil {
368				if errors.Is(lineErr, io.EOF) {
369					break
370				}
371				return "", true, fmt.Errorf("could not read SKILL.md: %w", lineErr)
372			}
373		}
374		if !closed {
375			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("SKILL.md frontmatter is not closed within %d bytes", maxFrontmatterBytes)
376		}
377		var metadata struct {
378			Name        string `yaml:"name"`
379			Description string `yaml:"description"`
380		}
381		if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(frontmatter.String()), &metadata); err != nil {
382			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("invalid SKILL.md YAML frontmatter: %w", err)
383		}
384		metadata.Name = strings.TrimSpace(metadata.Name)
```

```text
61	func projectScanLocations(root string, definitions []AgentDefinition, document lockDocument) []physicalScanLocation {
62		logical := make([]logicalScanLocation, 0, len(definitions))

84				}
85				if info, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(subagentRoot, entry.Name())); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
86					subagents[entry.Name()] = true

119	func dedupeScanLocations(input []logicalScanLocation) []physicalScanLocation {

123			current := byLogical[path]

132		for path := range byLogical {

134		}
135		sort.Strings(logicalPaths)

139			logical := *byLogical[path]
140			logical.AgentIDs = uniqueSorted(logical.AgentIDs)
141			physical := path
142			if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path); err == nil {
143				physical = filepath.Clean(resolved)

194				installation = &copy

197				installation.AgentIDs = append(installation.AgentIDs, found.Installation.AgentIDs...)

201			if len(installation.LogicalPaths) > 0 {
202				installation.Path = installation.LogicalPaths[0]
```

```text
70	func newTUIProjectRootResolver(trace *perftrace.Recorder, ctx context.Context) *tuiProjectRootResolver {
71		if ctx == nil {
72			ctx = context.Background()
73		}
74		return &tuiProjectRootResolver{
75			trace: trace, ctx: ctx, getwd: os.Getwd, resolve: agenttarget.Current,
76			ready: make(chan struct{}),
77		}
78	}

80	func (r *tuiProjectRootResolver) ResolveTarget(ctx context.Context) (agenttarget.Target, error) {
81		r.once.Do(func() {
82			go func() {
83				finish := r.trace.Start(perftrace.TUIProjectRootResolve, perftrace.Fields{})
84				cwd, err := r.getwd()
85				if err == nil {
86					r.target, err = r.resolve(r.ctx, cwd)
87				}
88				r.err = err
89				finish(resolverOutcome(err))
90				close(r.ready)
91			}()
92		})
93		if ctx == nil {
94			ctx = context.Background()
95		}
96		select {
97		case <-ctx.Done():
98			return agenttarget.Target{}, ctx.Err()
99		case <-r.ready:
100			return r.target, r.err
101		}
102	}
103	
104	func (r *tuiProjectRootResolver) Resolve(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
105		target, err := r.ResolveTarget(ctx)
106		return target.CheckoutRoot, err
107	}

112			return r.target.CheckoutRoot, r.err == nil
113		default:
114			return "", false
```

```text
1	// Package agenttarget resolves the repository checkouts inspected by agent
2	// configuration inventories. It deliberately contains no skill, MCP, or UI
3	// policy so those domains can share one definition of a target.
4	package agenttarget
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/repo"
18	)
19	
20	// Target identifies one concrete checkout of one repository. RepoPath is the
21	// repository's main navigation path (which may be a configured symlink alias),
22	// while CheckoutRoot is the exact worktree to inspect. Linked worktrees share
23	// RepoPath and CommonDir but remain distinct targets through CheckoutRoot.
24	type Target struct {
25		RepoName     string `json:"repo_name"`
26		RepoDisplay  string `json:"repo_display"`
27		RepoPath     string `json:"repo_path"`
28		CheckoutRoot string `json:"checkout_root"`
29		CommonDir    string `json:"common_dir"`
30	}
31	
32	// Key is stable for one checkout of one clone. It is intentionally stricter
33	// than gitx.Repo.Key, which identifies the clone regardless of checkout.
34	func (t Target) Key() string {
35		return comparablePath(t.CommonDir) + "\x00" + comparablePath(t.CheckoutRoot)
36	}
37	
38	// Current resolves the checkout containing cwd. A linked worktree remains the
39	// target checkout; outside Git, the absolute directory remains a useful project
40	// scope for agents that support configuration in ordinary folders.
41	func Current(ctx context.Context, cwd string) (Target, error) {
42		target, err := ResolvePath(ctx, cwd)
43		if err == nil {
44			return target, nil
45		}
46		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
47			return Target{}, ctxErr
48		}
49		if !errors.Is(err, gitx.ErrNotARepo) {
50			return Target{}, err
51		}
52		root, pathErr := absoluteDirectory(cwd)
53		if pathErr != nil {
54			return Target{}, pathErr
55		}
56		name := filepath.Base(root)
57		return Target{
58			RepoName: name, RepoDisplay: name, RepoPath: root,
59			CheckoutRoot: root, CommonDir: root,
60		}, nil
61	}
62	
63	// ResolvePath resolves an explicit path to the checkout containing it.
64	func ResolvePath(ctx context.Context, value string) (Target, error) {
65		absolute, err := absoluteDirectory(value)
66		if err != nil {
67			return Target{}, err
68		}
69		found, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, absolute)
70		if err != nil {
71			return Target{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve target path %q: %w", value, err)
72		}
73		return fromGit(found)
74	}
75	
76	// ResolveRepository resolves an explicit repository reference using repo's
77	// normal name/path rules, then probes the selected path so an explicit linked
78	// worktree path is preserved.
79	func ResolveRepository(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Target, error) {
80		found, _, err := repo.Resolve(ctx, roots, ref)
81		if err != nil {
82			return Target{}, err
83		}
84		target, err := ResolvePath(ctx, found.Path)
85		if err != nil {
86			return Target{}, err
87		}
88		// A named canonical repository contributes its configured alias/category.
89		// An explicit linked-worktree path keeps the main repository identity from
90		// Git, but its checkout root remains the navigation path the caller selected.
91		switch {
92		case comparablePath(found.Path) == comparablePath(target.RepoPath):
93			if found.Name != "" {
94				target.RepoName = found.Name
95			}
96			if display := found.Display(); display != "" {
97				target.RepoDisplay = display
98			}
99			target.RepoPath = navigationPath(found.Path)
100			target.CheckoutRoot = target.RepoPath
101		case comparablePath(found.Path) == comparablePath(target.CheckoutRoot):
102			target.CheckoutRoot = navigationPath(found.Path)
103		}
104		return target, nil
105	}
106	
107	// ResolveRepo is a concise compatibility name for ResolveRepository.
108	func ResolveRepo(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Target, error) {
109		return ResolveRepository(ctx, roots, ref)
110	}
111	
112	// FromRepository converts one canonical repo discovery result without another
113	// filesystem walk or Git process. Bare and non-Git inventory entries have no
114	// checkout to inspect and are skipped.
115	func FromRepository(found repo.Repo) (Target, bool) {
116		if !found.HasGit || found.Bare {
117			return Target{}, false
118		}
119		checkout := firstNonEmpty(found.Path, found.MainRoot, found.RealPath)
120		commonDir := found.CommonDir
121		if checkout == "" || commonDir == "" {
122			return Target{}, false
123		}
124		// Preserve the first discovery root's navigation alias. CommonDir remains
125		// physical identity, so aliases still deduplicate correctly.
126		checkout = navigationPath(checkout)
127		repository := navigationPath(firstNonEmpty(found.Path, found.MainRoot, found.RealPath, checkout))
128		commonDir = canonicalPath(commonDir)
129		name := found.Name
130		if name == "" {
131			name = filepath.Base(repository)
132		}
133		display := found.Display()
134		if display == "" {
135			display = name
136		}
137		return Target{
138			RepoName: name, RepoDisplay: display, RepoPath: repository,
139			CheckoutRoot: checkout, CommonDir: commonDir,
140		}, true
```

```text
1	package tui
2	
3	import tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
4	
5	const mouseWheelRows = 3
6	
7	func (m Model) updateMouse(message tea.MouseMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
8		event := tea.MouseEvent(message)
9		if event.Shift || event.Alt || event.Ctrl {
10			return m, nil
11		}
12		if m.overlay.kind == overlayActionMenu {
13			return m.updateActionMenuMouse(event)
14		}
15		if m.noteMode() || m.overlay.kind != overlayNone || m.mode != modeList {
16			return m, nil
17		}
18	
19		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
20			if !m.mouseOverList(event.X, event.Y) {
21				return m, nil
22			}
23			delta := mouseWheelRows
24			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
25				delta = -delta
26			}
27			m.setAt(m.at() + delta)
28			return m, nil
29		}
30		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress {
31			return m, nil
32		}
33	
34		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonLeft && event.Y == 0 {
35			for _, hit := range m.buildHeaderLayout().tabs {
36				if event.X < hit.from || event.X >= hit.to {
37					continue
38				}
39				if m.view == hit.view {
40					return m, nil
41				}
42				m.view = hit.view
43				return m.afterViewSwitch()
44			}
45			return m, nil
46		}
47	
48		row, ok := m.mouseRow(event.X, event.Y)
49		if !ok {
50			return m, nil
51		}
52		switch event.Button {
53		case tea.MouseButtonLeft:
54			m.setAt(row)
55		case tea.MouseButtonRight:
56			m.setAt(row)
57			if !m.remoteClone.active() {
58				m = m.openActionMenu()
59			}
60		}
61		return m, nil
62	}
63	
64	func (m Model) mouseRow(x, y int) (int, bool) {
65		if x < 0 || x >= m.width {
66			return 0, false
67		}
68		count := m.count()
69		from, to := m.window(count)
70		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
71		if y < first || y >= first+(to-from) {
72			return 0, false
73		}
74		return from + y - first, true
75	}
76	
77	func (m Model) mouseOverList(x, y int) bool {
78		if x < 0 || x >= m.width || m.count() == 0 {
79			return false
80		}
81		from, to := m.window(m.count())
82		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
83		return y >= 2 && y < first+(to-from)
84	}
85	
86	func (m Model) updateActionMenuMouse(event tea.MouseEvent) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
87		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
88			if m.overlay.optionCount == 0 {
89				return m, nil
90			}
91			delta := 1
92			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
93				delta = -1
94			}
95			m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + delta + m.overlay.optionCount) % m.overlay.optionCount
96			return m, nil
97		}
98		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress || event.Button != tea.MouseButtonLeft {
99			return m, nil
100		}
101		first := 4
102		if m.overlay.detail != "" {
103			first++
104		}
105		if event.Y < first || event.Y >= first+m.overlay.optionCount {
106			m.overlay = overlayState{}
107			return m, nil
108		}
109		m.overlay.optionIndex = event.Y - first
110		return m.runOverlayAction()
```

```text
95			overlay.title = "graduate " + row.Item.DisplayName()
96			overlay.addField("category", "category", "optional project category", "")
97			overlay.addField("name", "name", "optional project name", "")
98		default:
99			m.err = fmt.Errorf("Try action %q has no form", action)
100			return m, nil
101		}
102		m.overlay = overlay
103		m.err = nil
104		return m.focusOverlayField(0)
105	}

107	func (m Model) openTryConfirmation(action TryAction, row TryRow) (Model, tea.Cmd) {
108		overlay := overlayState{
109			kind: overlayTryConfirm, title: "confirm " + string(action),
110			target: row, action: action,
111		}
112		overlay.addField("confirm", "confirm", "type YES exactly", "")
113		m.overlay = overlay
114		m.err = nil
115		return m.focusOverlayField(0)
116	}

118	func (o *overlayState) addField(key, label, placeholder, value string) {
119		if o.fieldCount >= len(o.fields) {
120			return
121		}
122		input := textinput.New()
123		input.CharLimit = 300
124		input.Placeholder = placeholder
125		input.SetValue(value)
126		input.CursorEnd()
127		o.fields[o.fieldCount] = formField{key: key, label: label, input: input}
128		o.fieldCount++
129	}
130	
131	func (m Model) focusOverlayField(index int) (Model, tea.Cmd) {
132		if m.overlay.fieldCount == 0 {
133			return m, nil
134		}
135		if index < 0 {
136			index = m.overlay.fieldCount - 1
137		}
138		if index >= m.overlay.fieldCount {
139			index = 0
140		}
141		for fieldIndex := 0; fieldIndex < m.overlay.fieldCount; fieldIndex++ {
142			m.overlay.fields[fieldIndex].input.Blur()
143		}
144		m.overlay.fieldIndex = index
145		return m, m.overlay.fields[index].input.Focus()
146	}
147	
148	func (m Model) updateOverlay(message tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
149		switch m.overlay.kind {
150		case overlayHelp:
151			switch message.String() {
152			case "esc", "?", "q":
153				m.overlay = overlayState{}
154			}
155			return m, nil
156	
157		case overlayActionMenu:
158			switch message.String() {
159			case "esc", "q":
160				m.overlay = overlayState{}
161				return m, nil
162			case "j", "down":
163				if m.overlay.optionCount > 0 {
164					m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + 1) % m.overlay.optionCount
165				}
166				return m, nil
167			case "k", "up":
168				if m.overlay.optionCount > 0 {
169					m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + m.overlay.optionCount - 1) % m.overlay.optionCount
170				}
171				return m, nil
172			case "enter":
173				return m.runOverlayAction()
174			}
175			return m, nil
176	
177		case overlayRepoForm, overlayTryForm, overlayTryConfirm:
178			switch message.String() {
179			case "esc":
180				m.overlay = overlayState{}
181				m.err = nil
182				return m, nil
183			case "tab", "down":
184				return m.focusOverlayField(m.overlay.fieldIndex + 1)
185			case "shift+tab", "up":
186				return m.focusOverlayField(m.overlay.fieldIndex - 1)
187			case "enter":
188				return m.submitTryOverlay()
189			}
190			index := m.overlay.fieldIndex
191			input, command := m.overlay.fields[index].input.Update(message)
192			m.overlay.fields[index].input = input
193			return m, command
194		}
195		return m, nil
196	}
197	
198	func (m Model) submitTryOverlay() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
199		value := func(key string) string {
200			for index := 0; index < m.overlay.fieldCount; index++ {
201				if m.overlay.fields[index].key == key {
202					return strings.TrimSpace(m.overlay.fields[index].input.Value())
203				}
204			}
205			return ""
206		}
207		if m.overlay.kind == overlayRepoForm {
208			row := m.overlay.repoTarget
209			tags := splitTagInput(value("tags"))
210			note := value("note")
211			m.overlay = overlayState{}
212			m.err = nil
213			m.status = "updating repository metadata…"
214			return m, m.applyRepoPatch(row, tags, note)
215		}
216	
217		request := TryRequest{Action: m.overlay.action, ID: m.overlay.target.Item.ID}
218		switch m.overlay.action {
219		case TryCreate:
220			request.Name, request.Clone = value("name"), value("clone")
221			if request.Name == "" && request.Clone == "" {
222				m.err = fmt.Errorf("a new Try needs a name or clone reference")
223				return m, nil
224			}
225			gitInit, ok := parseBoolInput(value("git"), true)
226			if !ok {
227				m.err = fmt.Errorf("git init must be yes or no")
228				return m, nil
229			}
230			request.NoGit = !gitInit
231		case TryMark:
232			request.Tags = splitTagInput(value("tags"))
233			request.Note = value("note")
234		case TryRestore:
235			request.To = value("to")
236		case TryGraduate:
237			request.Category, request.Name = value("category"), value("name")
238		case TryArchive:
239			if value("confirm") != "YES" {
240				m.err = fmt.Errorf("confirmation must be exactly YES")
241				return m, nil
242			}
243		default:
244			m.err = fmt.Errorf("unsupported Try form action %q", m.overlay.action)
245			return m, nil
246		}
247		m.overlay = overlayState{}
248		m.err = nil
249		m.status = string(request.Action) + " in progress…"
250		return m, m.applyTry(request)
251	}
252	
253	func (m Model) renderOverlay() string {
254		var builder strings.Builder
255		builder.WriteString(styleTitle.Render("dev  "+strings.ToUpper(m.overlay.title)) + "\n\n")
256		switch m.overlay.kind {
257		case overlayHelp:
258			builder.WriteString("  navigation\n")
259			builder.WriteString("    j/k, arrows move · ctrl+d/u page · g/G first/last · tab/h/l switch view\n")
260			builder.WriteString("    left click row/tab · wheel 3 rows · right click row actions · click never opens\n")
261			builder.WriteString("    / filter · 0 clear · r reload · esc close/clear/quit · q quit\n\n")
262			builder.WriteString("  TASKS   enter open · n add note · N notes · p park · c next · 1/2/3 state · a done\n")
263			builder.WriteString("  REPOS   enter open · n add note · N notes · space worktrees · m metadata · y copy · s worktree task · d direct task · O/R sort\n")
264			builder.WriteString("  FLEET   enter Herdr/SSH open · e edit remotes.toml · r refresh · read-only Git overview\n")
265			builder.WriteString("  TRY     enter open · n create · space actions · a history · O/R sort\n")
266			builder.WriteString("  REMOTE  enter open local · n/N notes when cloned · c clone (enter stay / o open)\n")
267			builder.WriteString("  SKILLS  a add · c check · u update · e open file · y copy · A context/all scope\n")
268			builder.WriteString("  MCP     static declarations only · e open config · y copy · A context/all scope · r reload\n\n")
269			builder.WriteString("  " + styleHelp.Render("? / esc / q close help"))
270	
271		case overlayActionMenu:
272			builder.WriteString("  " + m.overlay.subject + "\n")
273			if m.overlay.detail != "" {
274				builder.WriteString("  " + m.overlay.detail + "\n")
275			}
276			builder.WriteString("\n")
277			for index := 0; index < m.overlay.optionCount; index++ {
278				prefix := "  "
279				line := m.overlay.optionLabels[index]
280				if index == m.overlay.optionIndex {
281					prefix = "▸ "
282					line = styleSelected.Render(line)
283				}
284				builder.WriteString(prefix + line + "\n")
285			}
286			builder.WriteString("\n  " + styleHelp.Render("j/k choose · enter continue · esc cancel"))
287	
288		case overlayRepoForm, overlayTryForm, overlayTryConfirm:
289			if m.overlay.target.Item.ID != "" {
290				builder.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("  %s\n  %s\n\n", m.overlay.target.Item.DisplayName(), contract(m.overlay.target.Item.Live.CurrentPath)))
291			} else if m.overlay.repoTarget.Repo.Path != "" {
292				builder.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("  %s\n  %s\n\n", m.overlay.repoTarget.Repo.Display(), contract(m.overlay.repoTarget.Repo.Path)))
293			}
294			for index := 0; index < m.overlay.fieldCount; index++ {
295				marker := "  "
296				if index == m.overlay.fieldIndex {
297					marker = "▸ "
298				}
299				builder.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("%s%-10s %s\n", marker, m.overlay.fields[index].label+":", m.overlay.fields[index].input.View()))
300			}
301			if m.err != nil {
302				builder.WriteString("\n  " + styleErr.Render("✗ "+m.err.Error()))
303			}
304			builder.WriteString("\n\n  " + styleHelp.Render("tab field · enter submit · esc cancel"))
305		}
306		return builder.String()
307	}
```

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers - `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls. (Exception: the `prompt-audit` subcommand is non-interactive and does not stop here - it records non-Anthropic provider markers in its report's stated assumptions and never proposes switching a non-Anthropic file to the Anthropic SDK.)

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) - only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two - don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation - either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying - write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 5, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-5`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` - it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events

## Warning: API Drift - Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025-2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing - the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5/5.1 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 / 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) - see the Server Tools QR below. |
| PHP parameter names | snake_case wire names as named args (`max_tokens`) | Top-level named args are camelCase (`maxTokens`). Nested array keys vary by feature (e.g. `'taskBudget'`, `'skillID'`, `'mcp_server_name'`) - copy the exact key from the documented example; do not bulk-convert. |
| Managed Agents credentials | Keep secrets host-side via custom tools (the only option before vaults shipped) | Vault `environment_variable` credentials - stored by Anthropic, substituted at egress, never visible in the sandbox (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` -> Vaults). Host-side custom tools remain the fallback for self-hosted sandboxes. |
| Files API / Skills | `client.beta.files.*` / `client.beta.skills.*` with beta `files-api-2025-04-14` / `skills-2025-10-02` | Out of beta: `client.files.*` / `client.skills.*`, no beta header. In current SDKs `client.beta.files` / `client.beta.skills` have breaking shape changes from previous versions, matching the stable namespaces - migrate per `shared/live-sources.md` -> Files API / Skills Guide. |

The `{lang}/` files in this skill are authoritative over recalled patterns.
