788	func collectTries(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, includeAll bool) ([]tui.TryRow, error) {
789		options := experiment.ListOptions{All: includeAll}
790		return collectTriesWithOptions(ctx, app, rt, options, nil, false)
791	}
792	
793	func collectTriesWithOptions(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, options experiment.ListOptions,
794		sessions []runtime.Session, sessionsSet bool) ([]tui.TryRow, error) {
795		service, err := newExperimentService(app)
796		if err != nil {
797			return nil, err
798		}
799		items, diagnostics, listErr := service.List(ctx, options)
800		warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, diagnostics)
801		if !sessionsSet {
802			sessions, _ = rt.List(ctx)
803		}
804		rows := make([]tui.TryRow, 0, len(items))
805		for _, item := range items {
806			row := tui.TryRow{Item: item}
807			if item.Entry != nil {
808				if location, ok := item.Entry.LocationFor(config.Hostname()); ok {
809					copy := location
810					row.Location = &copy
811				}
812			}
813			sizeRepo := item.Live.Repo
814			if sizeRepo == nil && item.Live.CurrentPath != "" {
815				if discovered, discoverErr := gitx.Discover(ctx, item.Live.CurrentPath); discoverErr == nil {
816					sizeRepo = &discovered
817				}
818			}
819			if sizeRepo != nil {
820				worktreeCount := 0
821				if worktrees, worktreeErr := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, item.Live.CurrentPath); worktreeErr == nil && len(worktrees) > 1 {
822					worktreeCount = len(worktrees) - 1
823				}
824				row.SizeTarget = diskusage.FromGit(*sizeRepo, worktreeCount)
825			} else if item.Live.CurrentPath != "" {
826				row.SizeTarget = diskusage.Plain(item.Live.CurrentPath)
827			}
828			if item.Live.Present && item.Live.Repo != nil {
829				row.Topology, row.TopologyErr = gitx.RecoveryTopologyOf(ctx, item.Live.CurrentPath)
830			}
831			if item.Live.Present {
832				for _, session := range sessions {
833					if session.Covers(item.Live.CurrentPath) ||
834						(item.Live.RealPath != "" && session.Covers(item.Live.RealPath)) {
835						row.Live = true
836						row.Runtime, row.RuntimeHandle, row.RuntimeStatus = rt.Name(), session.Handle, session.AgentStatus
837						break
838					}
839				}
840			}
841			rows = append(rows, row)
842		}
843		return rows, listErr
844	}
845	
846	func applyTryAction(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, request tui.TryRequest) (tui.TryActionResult, error) {
847		service, err := newExperimentService(app)
848		if err != nil {
849			return tui.TryActionResult{}, err
850		}
851		resolve := func() (experiment.Item, error) {
852			item, diagnostics, resolveErr := service.ResolveWithOptions(ctx, request.ID, experiment.ResolveOptions{
853				IncludeDeprecated: true, IncludeArchived: true,
854				IncludeEvicted: true, IncludeGraduated: true,
855			})
856			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, diagnostics)
857			return item, resolveErr
858		}
859		open := func(item experiment.Item, status string) (tui.TryActionResult, error) {
860			if !item.Live.Present || item.Live.CurrentPath == "" {
861				return tui.TryActionResult{}, fmt.Errorf("Try %s is not present on this host", item.DisplayName())
862			}
863			handle, openErr := openCheckout(ctx, rt, item.Live.CurrentPath, item.DisplayName())
864			if openErr != nil {
865				return tui.TryActionResult{}, openErr
866			}
867			result := tui.TryActionResult{Status: status, RefreshRepos: true}
868			if rt.Name() == "none" {
869				result.CD = item.Live.CurrentPath
870			} else {
871				result.Status += fmt.Sprintf(" in %s (%s)", rt.Name(), handle.Handle)
872				result.RuntimeHandle = handle.Handle
873			}
874			if _, touchErr := service.Touch(ctx, item.ID); touchErr != nil {
875				return result, fmt.Errorf("%s, but could not record activity: %w", status, touchErr)
876			}
877			return result, nil
878		}
879	
880		switch request.Action {
881		case tui.TryOpen:
882			item, resolveErr := resolve()
883			if resolveErr != nil {
884				return tui.TryActionResult{}, resolveErr
885			}
886			return open(item, "opened "+item.DisplayName())
887	
888		case tui.TryCreate:
889			created, createErr := service.ResolveOrCreate(ctx, experiment.CreateRequest{
890				Name: request.Name, Clone: request.Clone, NoGit: request.NoGit,
891			})
892			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, created.Diagnostics)
893			if created.InitWarning != nil {
894				app.warnf("could not git init: %v", created.InitWarning)
895			}
896			if createErr != nil {
897				return tui.TryActionResult{}, createErr
898			}
899			status := "created " + created.Item.DisplayName()
900			if created.Existing {
901				status = "opened existing " + created.Item.DisplayName()
902			}
903			result, openErr := open(created.Item, status)
904			result.RefreshRepos = true
905			return result, openErr
906	
907		case tui.TryMark:
908			item, resolveErr := resolve()
909			if resolveErr != nil {
910				return tui.TryActionResult{}, resolveErr
911			}
912			desired := catalog.NormalizeTags(request.Tags)
913			remove := append([]string(nil), item.Tags...)
914			note := request.Note
915			updated, diagnostics, patchErr := service.Patch(ctx, experiment.PatchRequest{
916				Ref: item.ID, AddTags: desired, RemoveTags: remove, Note: &note,
917			})
918			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, diagnostics)
919			return tui.TryActionResult{
920				Status: "updated metadata for " + updated.DisplayName(), RefreshRepos: true,
921			}, patchErr
922	
923		case tui.TryDeprecate:
924			transition, transitionErr := service.Deprecate(ctx, experiment.TransitionRequest{Ref: request.ID})
925			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, transition.Diagnostics)
926			return tui.TryActionResult{Status: "deprecated " + transition.Item.DisplayName()}, transitionErr
927	
928		case tui.TryReactivate:
929			transition, transitionErr := service.Reactivate(ctx, experiment.TransitionRequest{Ref: request.ID})
930			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, transition.Diagnostics)
931			return tui.TryActionResult{Status: "reactivated " + transition.Item.DisplayName()}, transitionErr
932	
933		case tui.TryArchive:
934			transition, transitionErr := service.Archive(ctx, experiment.TransitionRequest{Ref: request.ID})
935			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, transition.Diagnostics)
936			return tui.TryActionResult{
937				Status: "archived " + transition.Item.DisplayName(), RefreshRepos: true,
938			}, transitionErr
939	
940		case tui.TryRestore:
941			transition, transitionErr := service.Restore(ctx, experiment.TransitionRequest{Ref: request.ID, To: request.To})
942			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, transition.Diagnostics)
943			return tui.TryActionResult{
944				Status: "restored " + transition.Item.DisplayName(), RefreshRepos: true,
945			}, transitionErr
946	
947		case tui.TryGraduate:
948			graduated, graduateErr := service.Graduate(ctx, experiment.GraduateRequest{
949				Ref: request.ID, Category: request.Category, Name: request.Name,
950			})
951			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, graduated.Diagnostics)
952			if graduateErr != nil {
953				return tui.TryActionResult{}, graduateErr
954			}
955			result, openErr := open(graduated.Item, "graduated "+graduated.Plan.Name)
956			result.RefreshRepos = true
957			return result, openErr
958		}
959		return tui.TryActionResult{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown Try action %q", request.Action)
960	}
961	
962	// repoCollectOptions leaves an opt-in path for the future TRY view while the
963	// ordinary repository inventory suppresses active and deprecated Tries.
964	type repoCollectOptions struct {
965		IncludeTries bool
966		Sessions     []runtime.Session
967		SessionsErr  error
968		SessionsSet  bool
969		Tasks        []*task.Task
970		TasksSet     bool
971		Repos        []repo.Repo
972		ReposSet     bool
973		Limiter      *inventory.Limiter
974	}
975	
976	// collectRepos builds the default repository view: what exists, plus how much
977	// of it is in flight, excluding cataloged active/deprecated Tries.
978	func collectRepos(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime) ([]tui.RepoRow, error) {
979		return collectReposWithOptions(ctx, app, rt, repoCollectOptions{})
980	}
981	
982	func collectReposWithOptions(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, options repoCollectOptions) ([]tui.RepoRow, error) {
983		repos := options.Repos
984		var err error
985		if !options.ReposSet {
986			repos, err = repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
987			if err != nil {
988				return nil, err
989			}
990		}
991		assets, catalogComplete, err := joinRepoAssets(app, repos)
992		if err != nil {
993			return nil, err
994		}
995		if !options.IncludeTries {
996			visibleRepos := make([]repo.Repo, 0, len(repos))
997			visibleAssets := make([]*catalog.Entry, 0, len(repos))
998			for index, repository := range repos {
999				if suppressTryRepo(assets[index], catalogComplete) {
1000					continue
1001				}
1002				visibleRepos = append(visibleRepos, repository)
1003				visibleAssets = append(visibleAssets, assets[index])
1004			}
1005			repos, assets = visibleRepos, visibleAssets
1006		}
1007		tasks := options.Tasks
1008		var taskDiagnostics []task.Diagnostic
1009		if !options.TasksSet {
1010			tasks, taskDiagnostics, err = app.Tasks.ListWithDiagnostics()
1011			if err != nil {
1012				return nil, err
1013			}
1014		}
1015		var taskInventoryErr error
1016		for _, diagnostic := range taskDiagnostics {
1017			taskInventoryErr = errors.Join(taskInventoryErr, diagnostic)
1018		}
1019		byRepo := map[string][]*task.Task{}
1020		for _, tracked := range tasks {
1021			byRepo[tracked.RepoPath] = append(byRepo[tracked.RepoPath], tracked)
1022		}
1023		sessions := options.Sessions
1024		runtimeErr := options.SessionsErr
1025		if !options.SessionsSet {
1026			sessions, runtimeErr = rt.List(ctx)
1027		}
1028		notesByRepo := map[string][]*note.Note{}
1029		if app.Notes != nil {
1030			allNotes, noteErr := app.Notes.List("")
1031			if noteErr != nil {
1032				return nil, noteErr
1033			}
1034			for _, n := range allNotes {
1035				notesByRepo[n.RepositoryID] = append(notesByRepo[n.RepositoryID], n)
1036			}
1037		}
1038	
1039		out := make([]tui.RepoRow, len(repos))
1040		// Each repo needs status, worktree and remote subprocesses. Serialising
1041		// ~3*56 git processes was the measured 4.2s startup bottleneck; eight
1042		// workers brings that down without forking hundreds at once. TUI callers
1043		// share the limiter with task enrichment.
1044		limiter := options.Limiter
1045		if limiter == nil {
1046			limiter = inventory.NewLimiter(8)
1047		}
1048		var wg sync.WaitGroup
1049		for i, r := range repos {
1050			wg.Add(1)
1051			go func(i int, r repo.Repo) {
1052				defer wg.Done()
1053				release, ok := limiter.Acquire(ctx)
1054				if !ok {
1055					return
1056				}
1057				defer release()
1058	
1059				row := tui.RepoRow{Repo: r, Asset: assets[i]}
1060				if row.Asset != nil {
1061					repoNotes := notesByRepo[row.Asset.ID]
1062					row.NoteCount = len(repoNotes)
1063					if len(repoNotes) > 0 {
1064						row.LatestNote = repoNotes[0]
1065					}
1066				}
1067				if r.HasGit {
1068					row.Topology, row.TopologyErr = gitx.RecoveryTopologyOf(ctx, r.Path)
1069				}
1070				row.Tasks = append(row.Tasks, byRepo[r.Path]...)
1071				if r.RealPath != "" && r.RealPath != r.Path {
1072					row.Tasks = append(row.Tasks, byRepo[r.RealPath]...)
1073				}
1074				row.Context = inventory.CollectRepoContext(ctx, r, row.Tasks, sessions, rt.Name())
1075				row.Context.TaskErr = taskInventoryErr
1076				row.Context.RuntimeErr = runtimeErr
1077				row.LastActivity = row.Context.LastActivity
1078				row.Worktrees = row.Context.WorktreeCount
1079				if main, ok := row.Context.Main(); ok {
1080					row.Status = main.Status
1081				}
1082				if !r.Bare {
1083					row.RemoteForge, row.RemoteName = forge.IdentityFromURL(gitx.RemoteFromConfig(r.CommonDir, "origin"))
1084				}
1085				if live := row.Context.Sessions(); len(live) > 0 {
1086					row.Live, row.Runtime = true, rt.Name()
1087					row.RuntimeHandle, row.RuntimeStatus = live[0].Handle, live[0].AgentStatus
1088				}
1089				if r.HasGit {
1090					row.SizeTarget = diskusage.FromGit(gitx.Repo{
1091						Root: r.Path, GitDir: r.GitDir, GitCommonDir: r.CommonDir,
1092						MainRoot: r.MainRoot, Name: r.Name, Bare: r.Bare,
1093					}, row.Worktrees)
1094				} else {
1095					row.SizeTarget = diskusage.Plain(r.Path)
1096				}
1097				out[i] = row
1098			}(i, r)
1099		}
1100		wg.Wait()
1101		return out, ctx.Err()
1102	}
1103	
1104	// externalTools resolves the configured tool bindings.
1105	//
1106	// Configurable rather than fixed because which program you reach for is
1107	// personal, and because the useful ones are often your own scripts and
1108	// aliases, not just the well-known tools.
1109	func externalTools(app *App) []tui.Tool {
1110		var out []tui.Tool
1111		for _, t := range app.Cfg.EffectiveTools() {
1112			run := t.Run
1113			name := t.Name
1114			if name == "" {
1115				name = firstWord(run)
1116			}
1117			command := []string{shellPath(), "-c", run}
1118			if t.Interactive {
1119				// The command string passed to shell -lic is parsed before some
1120				// shells finish loading aliases. Parse only eval "$1" up front,
1121				// then evaluate the configured command after rc loading, so both
1122				// aliases (vibe) and functions (claude-plans-here) work.
1123				command = []string{shellPath(), "-lic", `eval "$1"`, "dev-tui-tool", run}
1124			}
1125			out = append(out, tui.Tool{
1126				Key: t.Key, Name: name, Command: command,
1127				Probe: commandRunnable(run, t.Interactive),
1128			})
1129		}
1130		return out
1131	}
1132	
1133	// commandRunnable resolves the command's first word on PATH, expanding a
1134	// leading environment variable so "$EDITOR ." checks the editor itself. The
1135	// returned probe is run by a bounded Bubble Tea command, never by View.
1136	func commandRunnable(run string, interactive bool) func(context.Context) bool {
1137		return func(ctx context.Context) bool { return checkCommandRunnable(ctx, run, interactive) }
1138	}
1139	
1140	func checkCommandRunnable(ctx context.Context, run string, interactive bool) bool {
1141		if ctx == nil {
1142			ctx = context.Background()
1143		}
1144		word := firstWord(run)
1145		if strings.HasPrefix(word, "$") {
1146			word = os.Getenv(strings.TrimPrefix(word, "$"))
1147			if word == "" {
1148				return false
1149			}
1150			word = firstWord(word)
1151		}
1152		if word == "" {
1153			return false
1154		}
1155		if interactive {
1156			// Ask the configured shell after it loads its rc files; LookPath
1157			// cannot see aliases or functions.
1158			probeCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 3*time.Second)
1159			defer cancel()
1160			probe := exec.CommandContext(probeCtx, shellPath(), "-lic",
1161				`command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1`, "dev-tool-probe", word)
1162			return probe.Run() == nil
1163		}
1164		if filepath.IsAbs(word) {
1165			_, err := os.Stat(word)
1166			return err == nil
1167		}
1168		_, err := exec.LookPath(word)
1169		return err == nil
1170	}
1171	
1172	func firstWord(s string) string {
1173		f := strings.Fields(s)
1174		if len(f) == 0 {
1175			return ""
1176		}
1177		return f[0]
1178	}
1179	
1180	func shellPath() string {
1181		if s := os.Getenv("SHELL"); s != "" {
1182			return s
1183		}
1184		return "/bin/sh"
1185	}
1186	
1187	// remoteCachePath is private because the inventory can contain names and URLs
1188	// of private repositories.
1189	func remoteCachePath() string {
1190		return filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev", "remotes.json")
1191	}
1192	
1193	func remoteCacheSourceID(app *App) string {
1194		parts := []string{
1195			"forge-source-v1",
1196			"GH_HOST=" + os.Getenv("GH_HOST"),
1197			"GITLAB_HOST=" + os.Getenv("GITLAB_HOST"),
1198			"GLAB_HOST=" + os.Getenv("GLAB_HOST"),
1199		}
1200		for _, target := range app.Cfg.Forge.AzureDevOps {
1201			parts = append(parts, "azure="+target.Organization+"\x00"+target.Project)
1202		}
1203		sort.Strings(parts)
1204		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(strings.Join(parts, "\x00")))
1205		return fmt.Sprintf("%x", sum[:])
1206	}
1207	
1208	// cachedRemoteRows reads only the private JSON cache — no repository scan or
1209	// subprocess — so it is safe on the startup path. Local clone markers are
1210	// filled when the background local inventory arrives.
1211	func cachedRemoteRows(app *App) ([]tui.RemoteRow, bool, bool) {
1212		cache, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
1213		sourceID := remoteCacheSourceID(app)
1214		if !ok || cache.SourceID != sourceID {
1215			return nil, false, false
1216		}
1217		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(cache.Repos))
1218		for _, rr := range cache.Repos {
1219			out = append(out, tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr})
1220		}
1221		return out, true, !cache.FreshFor(app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration, sourceID)
1222	}
1223	
1224	// cachedRemotesForRepoRows uses the local repo data the dashboard already
1225	// collected, avoiding another process-spawning scan on startup.
1226	func cachedRemotesForRepoRows(app *App, locals []tui.RepoRow) ([]tui.RemoteRow, bool) {
1227		cache, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
1228		if !ok || !cache.FreshFor(app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration, remoteCacheSourceID(app)) {
1229			return nil, false
1230		}
1231		return matchRemoteRepoRows(cache.Repos, locals), true
1232	}
1233	
1234	func matchRemoteRepoRows(remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo, locals []tui.RepoRow) []tui.RemoteRow {
1235		byRemote := map[string]tui.RepoRow{}
1236		ambiguous := map[string]bool{}
1237		for _, r := range locals {
1238			if r.RemoteForge == forge.Unknown || r.RemoteName == "" {
1239				continue
1240			}
1241			key := string(r.RemoteForge) + "/" + strings.ToLower(r.RemoteName)
1242			if ambiguous[key] {
1243				continue
1244			}
1245			if _, exists := byRemote[key]; exists {
1246				delete(byRemote, key)
1247				ambiguous[key] = true
1248				continue
1249			}
1250			byRemote[key] = r
1251		}
1252		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(remoteRepos))
1253		for _, rr := range remoteRepos {
1254			row := tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr}
1255			if local, ok := byRemote[string(rr.Forge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(rr.FullName)]; ok {
1256				row.LocalPath, row.LocalName = local.Repo.Path, local.Repo.Display()
1257				row.LocalKind = catalog.KindRepository
1258				if local.Asset != nil {
1259					row.LocalKind = local.Asset.Kind
1260				}
1261			}
1262			out = append(out, row)
1263		}
1264		return out
1265	}
1266	
1267	// cachedRemotes returns a fresh, already-local-matched cache for instant TUI
1268	// navigation. Local paths are recomputed rather than cached because clones can
1269	// move independently of the forge inventory.
1270	func cachedRemotes(ctx context.Context, app *App) ([]tui.RemoteRow, bool) {
1271		cache, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
1272		if !ok || !cache.FreshFor(app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration, remoteCacheSourceID(app)) {
1273			return nil, false
1274		}
1275		return matchRemoteLocals(ctx, app, cache.Repos), true
1276	}
1277	
1278	func cachedRemotesAny(ctx context.Context, app *App) ([]tui.RemoteRow, forge.Cache, bool) {
1279		cache, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
1280		if !ok || (cache.SourceID != "" && cache.SourceID != remoteCacheSourceID(app)) {
1281			return nil, forge.Cache{}, false
1282		}
1283		return matchRemoteLocals(ctx, app, cache.Repos), cache, true
1284	}
1285	
1286	// collectRemotes aggregates configured forge CLIs, caches the normalised response, then
1287	// marks remotes that already have a checkout under the configured scan roots.
1288	// Calls run concurrently so one slow forge does not serialise the other.
1289	type remoteCollectOptions struct {
1290		Locals       []tui.RepoRow
1291		LocalsSet    bool
1292		Providers    []forge.Forge
1293		ProvidersSet bool
1294	}
1295	
1296	func collectRemotes(ctx context.Context, app *App) ([]tui.RemoteRow, error) {
1297		return collectRemotesWithOptions(ctx, app, remoteCollectOptions{})
1298	}
1299	
1300	func collectRemotesForRows(ctx context.Context, app *App, locals []tui.RepoRow) ([]tui.RemoteRow, error) {
1301		return collectRemotesWithOptions(ctx, app, remoteCollectOptions{Locals: locals, LocalsSet: true})
1302	}
1303	
1304	func collectRemotesWithOptions(ctx context.Context, app *App, options remoteCollectOptions) ([]tui.RemoteRow, error) {
1305		type result struct {
1306			kind  forge.Kind
1307			repos []forge.RemoteRepo
1308			err   error
1309		}
1310		sourceID := remoteCacheSourceID(app)
1311		matchRows := func(repos []forge.RemoteRepo) []tui.RemoteRow {
1312			if options.LocalsSet {
1313				return matchRemoteRepoRows(repos, options.Locals)
1314			}
1315			return matchRemoteLocals(ctx, app, repos)
1316		}
1317		providers := options.Providers
1318		if !options.ProvidersSet {
1319			providers = configuredForges(app)
1320		}
1321		ch := make(chan result, len(providers))
1322		var wg sync.WaitGroup
1323		available := 0
1324		var unavailable []error
1325		expected := map[forge.Kind]bool{}
1326		var unavailableKinds []forge.Kind
1327		for _, f := range providers {
1328			if !f.Available() {
1329				// GitHub and GitLab remain opportunistic, but an explicit Azure
1330				// target should report why it did not contribute any repositories.
1331				if f.Kind() == forge.AzureDevOps {
1332					unavailable = append(unavailable, &forge.ErrNoCLI{Kind: forge.AzureDevOps, Bin: "az"})
1333					expected[f.Kind()] = true
1334					unavailableKinds = append(unavailableKinds, f.Kind())
1335				}
1336				continue
1337			}
1338			expected[f.Kind()] = true
1339			available++
1340			wg.Add(1)
1341			go func(f forge.Forge) {
1342				defer wg.Done()
1343				r, err := f.ListRepos(ctx)
1344				ch <- result{kind: f.Kind(), repos: r, err: err}
1345			}(f)
1346		}
1347		wg.Wait()
1348		close(ch)
1349		if available == 0 {
1350			if cached, ok := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath()); ok && cached.SourceID == sourceID {
1351				rows := matchRows(cached.Repos)
1352				if len(unavailable) > 0 {
1353					return rows, errors.Join(unavailable...)
1354				}
1355				return rows, fmt.Errorf("no supported forge CLI is installed")
1356			}
1357			if len(unavailable) > 0 {
1358				return nil, errors.Join(unavailable...)
1359			}
1360			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no supported forge CLI is installed")
1361		}
1362	
1363		old, _ := forge.LoadCacheAny(remoteCachePath())
1364		if old.SourceID != sourceID {
1365			old = forge.Cache{}
1366		}
1367		byProvider := map[forge.Kind][]forge.RemoteRepo{}
1368		statuses := map[forge.Kind]forge.ProviderStatus{}
1369		for _, r := range old.Repos {
1370			byProvider[r.Forge] = append(byProvider[r.Forge], r)
1371		}
1372		for kind, status := range old.Providers {
1373			statuses[kind] = status
1374		}
1375		errs := append([]error(nil), unavailable...)
1376		successful := 0
1377		now := time.Now().UTC()
1378		for _, kind := range unavailableKinds {
1379			status := statuses[kind]
1380			status.Error = "provider CLI unavailable"
1381			statuses[kind] = status
1382		}
1383		for res := range ch {
1384			if res.err != nil {
1385				errs = append(errs, res.err)
1386				status := statuses[res.kind]
1387				status.Error = res.err.Error()
1388				if len(byProvider[res.kind]) == 0 && len(res.repos) > 0 {
1389					byProvider[res.kind] = res.repos
1390					status.FetchedAt = now
1391					status.Complete = false
1392				}
1393				statuses[res.kind] = status
1394				continue
1395			}
1396			successful++
1397			byProvider[res.kind] = res.repos
1398			statuses[res.kind] = forge.ProviderStatus{FetchedAt: now, Complete: true}
1399		}
1400		var remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo
1401		complete := true
1402		providerStatuses := map[forge.Kind]forge.ProviderStatus{}
1403		for kind := range expected {
1404			status, ok := statuses[kind]
1405			if !ok || !status.Complete {
1406				complete = false
1407			}
1408			if ok {
1409				providerStatuses[kind] = status
1410			}
1411			remoteRepos = append(remoteRepos, byProvider[kind]...)
1412		}
1413		sortRemoteRepos(remoteRepos)
1414		if successful > 0 {
1415			_ = forge.SaveCacheStateContext(ctx, remoteCachePath(), forge.Cache{
1416				Version: forge.CacheVersion, SourceID: sourceID, FetchedAt: now, Complete: complete,
1417				Providers: providerStatuses, Repos: remoteRepos,
1418			})
1419		}
1420		return matchRows(remoteRepos), errors.Join(errs...)
1421	}
1422	
1423	func sortRemoteRepos(repos []forge.RemoteRepo) {
1424		sort.SliceStable(repos, func(i, j int) bool {
1425			if !repos[i].UpdatedAt.Equal(repos[j].UpdatedAt) {
1426				return repos[i].UpdatedAt.After(repos[j].UpdatedAt)
1427			}
1428			return repos[i].Label() < repos[j].Label()
1429		})
1430	}
1431	
1432	func configuredForges(app *App) []forge.Forge {
1433		providers := forge.All()
1434		if app == nil || len(app.Cfg.Forge.AzureDevOps) == 0 {
1435			return providers
1436		}
1437		targets := make([]forge.AzureDevOpsTarget, 0, len(app.Cfg.Forge.AzureDevOps))
1438		for _, target := range app.Cfg.Forge.AzureDevOps {
1439			targets = append(targets, forge.AzureDevOpsTarget{
1440				Organization: target.Organization,
1441				Project:      target.Project,
1442			})
1443		}
1444		return forge.All(forge.NewAzureDevOps(targets))
1445	}
1446	
1447	func matchRemoteLocals(ctx context.Context, app *App, remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo) []tui.RemoteRow {
1448		locals, _ := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
1449		assets, _, assetErr := joinRepoAssets(app, locals)
1450		if assetErr != nil {
1451			app.warnf("could not join catalog metadata to remote locals: %v", assetErr)
1452			assets = make([]*catalog.Entry, len(locals))
1453		}
1454		type localMatch struct {
1455			repository repo.Repo
1456			asset      *catalog.Entry
1457		}
1458		localByRemote := map[string]localMatch{}
1459		ambiguous := map[string]bool{}
1460		for index, r := range locals {
1461			if r.Bare {
1462				continue
1463			}
1464			kind, name := forge.IdentityFromURL(gitx.RemoteFromConfig(r.CommonDir, "origin"))
1465			if kind == forge.Unknown || name == "" {
1466				continue
1467			}
1468			key := string(kind) + "/" + strings.ToLower(name)
1469			if ambiguous[key] {
1470				continue
1471			}
1472			if _, exists := localByRemote[key]; exists {
1473				delete(localByRemote, key)
1474				ambiguous[key] = true
1475				continue
1476			}
1477			localByRemote[key] = localMatch{repository: r, asset: assets[index]}
1478		}
1479		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(remoteRepos))
1480		for _, rr := range remoteRepos {
1481			row := tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr}
1482			if local, ok := localByRemote[string(rr.Forge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(rr.FullName)]; ok {
1483				row.LocalPath, row.LocalName = local.repository.Path, local.repository.Display()
1484				row.LocalKind = catalog.KindRepository
1485				if local.asset != nil {
1486					row.LocalKind = local.asset.Kind
1487				}
1488			}
1489			out = append(out, row)
1490		}
1491		// Linked-worktree Tries are intentionally absent from repo.Discover's project
1492		// inventory, so use their explicit catalog identity as a second safe source.
1493		applyCatalogRemoteMatches(app, out)
1494		return out
1495	}
1496	
1497	func applyCatalogRemoteMatches(app *App, rows []tui.RemoteRow) {
1498		if app == nil || app.Catalog == nil || len(rows) == 0 {
1499			return
1500		}
1501		entries, diagnostics, err := app.Catalog.ListWithDiagnostics()
1502		if err != nil {
1503			app.warnf("could not read catalog for remote matching: %v", err)
1504			return
1505		}
1506		for _, diagnostic := range diagnostics {
1507			app.warnf("%s", diagnostic.Error())
1508		}
1509		if len(diagnostics) > 0 {
1510			return
1511		}
1512		host := config.Hostname()
1513		byIdentity := make(map[string][]*catalog.Entry)
1514		for _, entry := range entries {
1515			location, ok := entry.LocationFor(host)
1516			if !ok || location.State != catalog.LocationPresent || entry.RemoteIdentity == "" ||
1517				liveCatalogLocationPath(location) == "" {
1518				continue
1519			}
1520			byIdentity[entry.RemoteIdentity] = append(byIdentity[entry.RemoteIdentity], entry)
1521		}
1522		for index := range rows {
1523			identity := catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(rows[index].Repo.CloneURL)
1524			matches := byIdentity[identity]
1525			if identity == "" || len(matches) != 1 {
1526				continue
1527			}
1528			location, _ := matches[0].LocationFor(host)
1529			rows[index].LocalPath = liveCatalogLocationPath(location)
1530			rows[index].LocalName = matches[0].Name
1531			rows[index].LocalKind = matches[0].Kind
1532		}
1533	}
1534	
1535	func liveCatalogLocationPath(location catalog.Location) string {
1536		for _, candidate := range []string{location.CurrentPath, location.RealPath} {
1537			if candidate == "" {
1538				continue
1539			}
1540			if info, err := os.Stat(candidate); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
1541				return candidate
1542			}
1543		}
1544		return ""
1545	}
1546	
1547	func prepareTUINoteEdit(app *App, n *note.Note) (tui.NoteEdit, error) {
1548		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp("", "dev-note-*.md")
1549		if err != nil {
1550			return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
1551		}
1552		path := tmp.Name()
1553		if _, err := io.WriteString(tmp, n.Body); err != nil {
1554			_ = tmp.Close()
1555			_ = os.Remove(path)
1556			return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
1557		}
1558		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
1559			_ = os.Remove(path)
1560			return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
1561		}
1562		proc, _, err := editorProcess(path, "")
1563		if err != nil {
1564			_ = os.Remove(path)
1565			return tui.NoteEdit{}, err
1566		}
1567		return tui.NoteEdit{
1568			Command: proc,
1569			Complete: func(runErr error) error {
1570				if runErr != nil {
1571					_ = os.Remove(path)
1572					return runErr
1573				}
1574				body, err := os.ReadFile(path)
1575				if err != nil {
1576					return fmt.Errorf("read edited body (preserved at %s): %w", path, err)
1577				}
1578				if strings.TrimSpace(string(body)) == "" {
1579					_ = os.Remove(path)
1580					return fmt.Errorf("edited note body is empty; not saved")
1581				}
1582				_, err = app.Notes.Update(context.Background(), n.ID, n.Revision(), string(body), n.Tags)
1583				if err != nil {
1584					return fmt.Errorf("save edited note: %w; edited body preserved at %s", err, path)
1585				}
1586				_ = os.Remove(path)
1587				return nil
1588			},
1589		}, nil
1590	}

1	package tui

3	import tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
4	
5	const mouseWheelRows = 3
6	
7	func (m Model) updateMouse(message tea.MouseMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
8		event := tea.MouseEvent(message)
9		if event.Shift || event.Alt || event.Ctrl {
10			return m, nil
11		}
12		if m.overlay.kind == overlayActionMenu {
13			return m.updateActionMenuMouse(event)
14		}
15		if m.noteMode() || m.overlay.kind != overlayNone || m.mode != modeList {
16			return m, nil
17		}
18	
19		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
20			if !m.mouseOverList(event.X, event.Y) {
21				return m, nil
22			}
23			delta := mouseWheelRows
24			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
25				delta = -delta
26			}
27			m.setAt(m.at() + delta)
28			return m, nil
29		}
30		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress {
31			return m, nil
32		}
33	
34		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonLeft && event.Y == 0 {
35			for _, hit := range m.buildHeaderLayout().tabs {
36				if event.X < hit.from || event.X >= hit.to {
37					continue
38				}
39				if m.view == hit.view {
40					return m, nil
41				}
42				m.view = hit.view
43				return m.afterViewSwitch()
44			}
45			return m, nil
46		}
47	
48		row, ok := m.mouseRow(event.X, event.Y)
49		if !ok {
50			return m, nil
51		}
52		switch event.Button {
53		case tea.MouseButtonLeft:
54			m.setAt(row)
55		case tea.MouseButtonRight:
56			m.setAt(row)
57			if !m.remoteClone.active() {
58				m = m.openActionMenu()
59			}
60		}
61		return m, nil
62	}
63	
64	func (m Model) mouseRow(x, y int) (int, bool) {
65		if x < 0 || x >= m.width {
66			return 0, false
67		}
68		count := m.count()
69		from, to := m.window(count)
70		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
71		if y < first || y >= first+(to-from) {
72			return 0, false
73		}
74		return from + y - first, true
75	}
76	
77	func (m Model) mouseOverList(x, y int) bool {
78		if x < 0 || x >= m.width || m.count() == 0 {
79			return false
80		}
81		from, to := m.window(m.count())
82		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
83		return y >= 2 && y < first+(to-from)
84	}

86	func (m Model) updateActionMenuMouse(event tea.MouseEvent) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
87		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
88			if m.overlay.optionCount == 0 {
89				return m, nil
90			}
91			delta := 1
92			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
93				delta = -1
94			}
95			m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + delta + m.overlay.optionCount) % m.overlay.optionCount
96			return m, nil
97		}
98		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress || event.Button != tea.MouseButtonLeft {
99			return m, nil
100		}
101		first := 4
102		if m.overlay.detail != "" {
103			first++
104		}
105		if event.Y < first || event.Y >= first+m.overlay.optionCount {
106			m.overlay = overlayState{}
107			return m, nil
108		}
109		m.overlay.optionIndex = event.Y - first
110		return m.runOverlayAction()
111	}

382		token := m.overlay.selection

5	const mouseWheelRows = 3
6	
7	func (m Model) updateMouse(message tea.MouseMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
8		event := tea.MouseEvent(message)
9		if event.Shift || event.Alt || event.Ctrl {
10			return m, nil
11		}
12		if m.overlay.kind == overlayActionMenu {
13			return m.updateActionMenuMouse(event)
14		}
15		if m.noteMode() || m.overlay.kind != overlayNone || m.mode != modeList {
16			return m, nil
17		}
18	
19		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
20			if !m.mouseOverList(event.X, event.Y) {
21				return m, nil
22			}
23			delta := mouseWheelRows
24			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
25				delta = -delta
26			}
27			m.setAt(m.at() + delta)
28			return m, nil
29		}
30		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress {
31			return m, nil
32		}
33	
34		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonLeft && event.Y == 0 {
35			for _, hit := range m.buildHeaderLayout().tabs {
36				if event.X < hit.from || event.X >= hit.to {
37					continue
38				}
39				if m.view == hit.view {
40					return m, nil
41				}
42				m.view = hit.view
43				return m.afterViewSwitch()
44			}
45			return m, nil
46		}
47	
48		row, ok := m.mouseRow(event.X, event.Y)
49		if !ok {
50			return m, nil
51		}
52		switch event.Button {
53		case tea.MouseButtonLeft:
54			m.setAt(row)
55		case tea.MouseButtonRight:
56			m.setAt(row)
57			if !m.remoteClone.active() {
58				m = m.openActionMenu()
59			}
60		}
61		return m, nil
62	}
63	
64	func (m Model) mouseRow(x, y int) (int, bool) {
65		if x < 0 || x >= m.width {
66			return 0, false
67		}
68		count := m.count()
69		from, to := m.window(count)
70		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
71		if y < first || y >= first+(to-from) {
72			return 0, false
73		}
74		return from + y - first, true
75	}
76	
77	func (m Model) mouseOverList(x, y int) bool {
78		if x < 0 || x >= m.width || m.count() == 0 {
79			return false
80		}
81		from, to := m.window(m.count())
82		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
83		return y >= 2 && y < first+(to-from)
84	}
85	
86	func (m Model) updateActionMenuMouse(event tea.MouseEvent) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
87		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
88			if m.overlay.optionCount == 0 {
89				return m, nil
90			}
91			delta := 1
92			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
93				delta = -1
94			}
95			m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + delta + m.overlay.optionCount) % m.overlay.optionCount
96			return m, nil
97		}
98		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress || event.Button != tea.MouseButtonLeft {
99			return m, nil
100		}
101		first := 4
102		if m.overlay.detail != "" {
103			first++
104		}
105		if event.Y < first || event.Y >= first+m.overlay.optionCount {
106			m.overlay = overlayState{}
107			return m, nil
108		}
109		m.overlay.optionIndex = event.Y - first
110		return m.runOverlayAction()

 # Changelog
 
 All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
 
 The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and releases use [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
 
 ## [Unreleased]
 
+### Added
+
+- The dashboard now supports cell-motion mouse input: left-click selects rows or
+  switches visible tabs, the wheel moves three rows, and right-click opens the
+  selected row's existing actions without making a click implicitly open it.
+- SKILLS and MCP share a session-only `A` context/all scope toggle and can open
+  the selected local configuration in `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` or copy its path,
+  sanitized summary, and explicitly requested raw file. Raw file copy is bounded
+  to 1 MiB but may put credentials and other declarations into the system
+  clipboard. `A` is now a reserved TUI tool key.
+
+### Changed
+
+- MCP caps its content-responsive `SERVER` column at 32 cells, keeping transport,
+  state, and source columns together instead of pushing them to the far edge of a
+  wide terminal.
+
 ## [0.2.12] - 2026-09-04
 
 ### Changed
 
 - The TUI SKILLS and MCP views are now startup-context-first. From a Git
   checkout they scan only the exact current worktree plus global/user sources,
   matching what an agent launched there can read instead of listing unrelated
   projects. Outside Git they retain the cross-repository inventory and include
   every accepted REPOS target.
 
 ## [0.2.11] - 2026-09-04
 
 ### Added
 
 - `dev pr list` shows the pull and merge requests you opened and the ones
   awaiting your review, and joins reported head branches to local task and
   checkout health. Account and per-repository surfaces remain explicit;
   personal per-repository queries may call once per requested role, engaged

```text
250	```
251	
252	Archive is a reversible same-filesystem move under `tries_root/.dev`; it does
253	not reclaim disk space. Phase 1 has no evict/delete action. The catalog keeps a
254	stable ID, per-host location, tags/note, last-opened time and graduation
255	history; Git and size facts remain live/derived.
256	
257	REMOTE:
258	
259	```
260	n / N      notes, only when a local clone exists
261	enter / o  open an existing local clone
262	c          confirm an absent repo; then enter stays or o opens after clone
263	q / ctrl-c request cancellation while clone/refresh/open is pending
264	r          refresh configured forge CLIs, replacing the cache
265	```
266	
267	SKILLS:
268	
269	```
270	a          open the interactive installer (default personal skill catalog)
271	c          check lock-managed Git sources without installing updates
272	u          confirm and update only the selected lock-managed skill
273	A          toggle shared context/all repository scope for this TUI session
274	e          open selected SKILL.md, or the lock file for a missing skill
275	y          p path · s safe summary · u source URL · f whole raw file
276	r          reload local project/global state without network access
277	```
278	
279	The detail pane separates repository/checkout, local presence/integrity, agent
280	compatibility, source, manager, and upstream freshness. Filters include
281	`repo:api`, `scope:global`, `agent:Codex`, `presence:missing`, and
282	`update:update_available`.
283	
284	MCP:
285	
286	```
287	A          toggle the same context/all repository scope
288	e          open the selected declaration's ConfigPath
289	y          p path · s safe summary · f whole raw config file
290	r          reload static declarations; no server is started or probed
291	```
292	
293	The MCP detail pane contains sanitized config/source/transport/policy facts,
294	exact Claude local project identity, bounded credential-reference summaries, and
295	redaction markers—never raw args, environment/header/OAuth values, indirect file
296	content, or connection health. That normalization still governs rows, safe
297	summaries, and JSON. Explicit `yf` instead reads the entire local source file (up
298	to 1 MiB) into the system clipboard; it performs no network access but may copy
299	credentials and other declarations from the same file.
300	
301	## Heatmap and editors
302	
303	```
304	H   open the selected repository's one-year activity heatmap
305	    b backfills only that repo; r rereads stats; H / esc returns
306	
307	e   edit effective dev config on ordinary views; edit the selected capability file on SKILLS/MCP
308	r   reparse config and reload local/remote data and tool bindings
309	```
310	
311	An empty heatmap is actionable: press `b` to derive only the selected repo's
312	history into stats.db and automatically redraw. `r` does not manufacture data;
313	it rereads what collectors/backfill have stored.
314	
315	Returning from an ordinary-view `e` live-reloads dev config; returning from a
316	SKILLS/MCP editor reloads only that capability inventory. Changes to scan roots, worktree
317	policy, forge cache settings and `[[tui.tools]]` take effect immediately. A
318	runtime backend change needs a restart because existing callbacks and sessions
319	belong to the backend the TUI opened with; the status line says so rather than
320	pretending to switch underneath a live workspace.
321	
322	## External tools are explicit configuration
323	
324	```bash
325	dev tui tools
326	```
327	
328	shows every binding, the exact command, its source, and whether it can run on
329	this machine. `dev config init` writes the defaults out in full:
330	
331	```toml
332	[[tui.tools]]
333	key  = "L"
334	name = "lazygit"
335	run  = "lazygit"
336	
337	[[tui.tools]]
338	key  = "Y"
339	name = "yazi"
340	run  = "yazi"
341	
342	[[tui.tools]]
343	key  = "V"
344	name = "nvim"
345	run  = "nvim ."
346	
347	[[tui.tools]]
348	key  = "B"
349	name = "vibe"
350	run  = "vibe"
351	interactive = true
352	
353	[[tui.tools]]
354	key  = "P"
355	name = "plans here"
356	run  = "claude-plans-here"
357	interactive = true
358	```
359	
360	A configured list replaces the defaults entirely. Commands run through
361	`$SHELL` in the selected row's checkout, so arguments, environment variables
362	and executable scripts work. `interactive = true` runs through `$SHELL -lic`
363	and deliberately evaluates the command *after* rc loading, so this machine's
364	`vibe` alias and `claude-plans-here` function work. Prefer a real script on PATH
365	when the binding should be portable to machines with different shell configs.
366	The dashboard resolves availability in a bounded background load after the first
367	view; rendering itself never launches the shell. Unknown or missing bindings are
368	hidden and fail closed until the current config generation has been checked.

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers - `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls. (Exception: the `prompt-audit` subcommand is non-interactive and does not stop here - it records non-Anthropic provider markers in its report's stated assumptions and never proposes switching a non-Anthropic file to the Anthropic SDK.)

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) - only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two - don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation - either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying - write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 5, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-5`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` - it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events

## Warning: API Drift - Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025-2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing - the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5/5.1 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 / 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) - see the Server Tools QR below. |
| PHP parameter names | snake_case wire names as named args (`max_tokens`) | Top-level named args are camelCase (`maxTokens`). Nested array keys vary by feature (e.g. `'taskBudget'`, `'skillID'`, `'mcp_server_name'`) - copy the exact key from the documented example; do not bulk-convert. |
| Managed Agents credentials | Keep secrets host-side via custom tools (the only option before vaults shipped) | Vault `environment_variable` credentials - stored by Anthropic, substituted at egress, never visible in the sandbox (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` -> Vaults). Host-side custom tools remain the fallback for self-hosted sandboxes. |
| Files API / Skills | `client.beta.files.*` / `client.beta.skills.*` with beta `files-api-2025-04-14` / `skills-2025-10-02` | Out of beta: `client.files.*` / `client.skills.*`, no beta header. In current SDKs `client.beta.files` / `client.beta.skills` have breaking shape changes from previous versions, matching the stable namespaces - migrate per `shared/live-sources.md` -> Files API / Skills Guide. |

The `{lang}/` files in this skill are authoritative over recalled patterns.

Before reading code examples, determine which language the user is working in (exception: for the `prompt-audit` subcommand, skip this section's ask steps - the audit is non-interactive and its inventory is language-agnostic; when no language is inferable, proceed without asking and state the assumption in the report):

 - `*.py`, `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `Pipfile` -> **Python** - read from `python/`
 - `*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` -> **TypeScript** - read from `typescript/`
 - `*.js`, `*.jsx` (no `.ts` files present) -> **TypeScript** - JS uses the same SDK, read from `typescript/`
 - `*.java`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle` -> **Java** - read from `java/`
 - `*.kt`, `*.kts`, `build.gradle.kts` -> **Java** - Kotlin uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`
 - `*.scala`, `build.sbt` -> **Java** - Scala uses the Java SDK, read from `java/`
 - `*.go`, `go.mod` -> **Go** - read from `go/`
 - `*.rb`, `Gemfile` -> **Ruby** - read from `ruby/`
 - `*.cs`, `*.csproj` -> **C#** - read from `csharp/`
 - `*.php`, `composer.json` -> **PHP** - read from `php/`

2. **If multiple languages detected** (e.g., both Python and TypeScript files):

 - Check which language the user's current file or question relates to
 - If still ambiguous, ask: "I detected both Python and TypeScript files. Which language are you using for the Claude API integration?"

3. **If language can't be inferred** (empty project, no source files, or unsupported language):

 - Use AskUserQuestion with options: Python, TypeScript, Java, Go, Ruby, cURL/raw HTTP, C#, PHP
 - If AskUserQuestion is unavailable, default to Python examples and note: "Showing Python examples. Let me know if you need a different language."

4. **If unsupported language detected** (Rust, Swift, C++, Elixir, etc.):

 - Suggest cURL/raw HTTP examples from `curl/` and note that community SDKs may exist
 - Offer to show Python or TypeScript examples as reference implementations

5. **If user needs cURL/raw HTTP examples**, read from `curl/`.

### Language-Specific Feature Support

Every SDK language above supports both the beta Tool Runner and Managed Agents (beta) - Python (`@beta_tool` decorator), TypeScript (`betaZodTool` + Zod), Java (annotated classes), Go (`BetaToolRunner` in the `toolrunner` pkg), Ruby (`BaseTool` + `tool_runner`), C# (`BetaToolRunner` + raw JSON schema), PHP (`BetaRunnableTool` + `toolRunner()`); code entry points are in the Tool Use Patterns quick reference below. cURL is raw HTTP (no SDK features) and supports Managed Agents.

> **Managed Agents code examples**: see the reading guide in the `## Managed Agents (Beta)` section below.

## Which Surface Should I Use?

> **Start simple.** Default to the simplest tier that meets your needs. Single API calls and workflows handle most use cases - only reach for agents when the task genuinely requires open-ended, model-driven exploration. "Simplest" means the least code you own: for a hosted, scheduled, or memory-backed agent, Managed Agents is usually the simplest option (no loop code, no state files, no scheduler), even though it's a bigger platform.

| Use Case                                        | Tier            | Recommended Surface       | Why                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Classification, summarization, extraction, Q&A  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | One request, one response                                    |
| Batch processing or embeddings                  | Single LLM call | **Claude API**            | Specialized endpoints                                        |
| Multi-step pipelines with code-controlled logic | Workflow        | **Claude API + tool use** | You orchestrate the loop                                     |
| Custom agent with your own tools                | Agent           | **Claude API + tool use** | Maximum flexibility                                          |
| Server-managed stateful agent with workspace    | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Anthropic runs the loop and hosts the tool-execution sandbox |
| Persisted, versioned agent configs              | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Agents are stored objects; sessions pin to a version         |
| Long-running multi-turn agent with file mounts  | Agent           | **Managed Agents**        | Per-session containers, SSE event stream, Skills + MCP       |
| Agent that runs on a schedule (cron, "every night") | Agent       | **Managed Agents** - scheduled deployments | Deployments fire sessions autonomously; no client-side scheduler |

> **Note:** Managed Agents is the right choice when you want Anthropic to run the agent loop *and* host the container where tools execute - file ops, bash, code execution all run in the per-session workspace. If you want to host the compute yourself or run your own custom tool runtime, Claude API + tool use is the right choice - use the tool runner for the agentic loop - its per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, logging, error interception, and conditional execution (see `shared/tool-use-concepts.md`) - or the manual loop when you want to own the entire loop yourself.

> **Cloud-provider access.** **Claude Platform on AWS** is Anthropic-operated with same-day API parity - see `shared/claude-platform-on-aws.md` for client setup. For per-feature availability on **Claude Platform on AWS**, **Amazon Bedrock**, **Google Vertex AI**, and **Microsoft Foundry**, see `shared/platform-availability.md` - that table is the single source of truth in this skill; do not infer availability from anywhere else.

### Building an Agent: Four Approaches

Once you've decided you actually need an agent (open-ended, model-driven tool use), there are four distinct ways to build one. Two independent questions separate them: **who supplies the harness** (the agent loop + context management) and **who supplies the deployment** (the infra the agent runs on). The Tool Runner and the Claude Agent SDK both supply a *harness only* - you still host and deploy them yourself - which is why they're easy to conflate. Managed Agents (CMA) is the only option that supplies **both** the harness *and* managed deployment; the manual loop supplies neither.

| # | Approach | You write | Harness & deployment | Tools available | Use when |
|---|----------|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|----------|
| 1 | **Claude API - manual loop** | The `while stop_reason == "tool_use"` loop yourself | You build the harness; you host | Only tools you define | You want to own the *entire* loop - no beta dependency, or a control flow the Tool Runner's per-turn hooks don't fit |
| 2 | **Claude API - Tool Runner** (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner` + `@beta_tool` / `betaZodTool`) | Just the tool functions | SDK supplies the loop (**harness only**); you host | Only tools you define | A custom-tool agent without hand-writing the loop (most cases). Per-turn hooks still give you approval gates, error interception, result modification (e.g. `cache_control`), retries, streaming, and compaction |
| 3 | **Managed Agents** (REST, beta) | Agent config + your tool results | Anthropic supplies the harness **and** hosts a per-session sandbox (**harness + deployment**) | Anthropic-hosted sandbox (bash, files, code exec) + Skills/MCP + your tools | You want Anthropic to run the loop *and* host the per-session workspace; persisted/versioned configs; long-running sessions |
| 4 | **Claude Agent SDK** - *separate product* (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) | A prompt + options | SDK supplies the Claude Code harness + built-in tools (**harness only**); you host | Built-in Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep/WebSearch/WebFetch + MCP + subagents | You want a batteries-included coding/filesystem agent running on your own infra |

The harness/deployment split is the key mental model: options 1, 2, and 4 all **leave deployment to you**; only option 3 (CMA) adds managed deployment. Options 1-3 are what this skill generates; option 4 is a different library with its own docs - see the disambiguation below.

> **Tool Runner != Claude Agent SDK.** These sound alike but are different packages:
> - **Tool Runner** is part of the regular Anthropic API SDK (`anthropic` / `@anthropic-ai/sdk`), reached via `client.beta.messages.tool_runner`. It automates the request -> execute -> loop cycle *for tools you define*. No built-in tools, no filesystem access, no sandbox - you supply every tool and host the compute. It is option 2 above, a thin helper over `POST /v1/messages`.
> - **Claude Agent SDK** (`claude-agent-sdk` / `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) is Claude Code packaged as a library. It ships built-in tools (file read/write/edit, bash, grep, web search), the full agent loop, context management, hooks, subagents, permissions, and sessions. You call `query(prompt, options)` and it drives everything.
>
> Both are **harness-only - you host and deploy them.** The difference is scope of harness: the Tool Runner loops over tools *you* define (with per-turn hooks for approval, interception, result modification, and retries - but no built-in tools); the Agent SDK is the full Claude Code harness with built-in tools. Neither provides managed deployment - that's what **Managed Agents (CMA)** adds (Anthropic hosts the loop and a per-session sandbox).
>
> **This skill covers the Claude API and Managed Agents (options 1-3); it does not generate Claude Agent SDK code.** If the user actually wants the Claude Agent SDK, point them to its docs (`code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk`) - don't substitute the API Tool Runner for it, or vice-versa.

### Should I Build an Agent?

Before choosing the agent tier, check all four criteria:

- **Complexity** - Is the task multi-step and hard to fully specify in advance? (e.g., "turn this design doc into a PR" vs. "extract the title from this PDF")
- **Value** - Does the outcome justify higher cost and latency?
- **Viability** - Is Claude capable at this task type?
- **Cost of error** - Can errors be caught and recovered from? (tests, review, rollback)

If the answer is "no" to any of these, stay at a simpler tier (single call or workflow).

---

## Architecture

Everything goes through `POST /v1/messages`. Tools and output constraints are features of this single endpoint - not separate APIs.

**User-defined tools** - You define tools (via decorators, Zod schemas, or raw JSON), and the SDK's tool runner handles calling the API, executing your functions, and looping until Claude is done. For full control, you can write the loop manually.

**Server-side tools** - Anthropic-hosted tools that run on Anthropic's infrastructure. Code execution is fully server-side (declare it in `tools`, Claude runs code automatically). Computer use can be server-hosted or self-hosted.

**Structured outputs** - Constrains the Messages API response format (`output_config.format`) and/or tool parameter validation (`strict: true`). The recommended approach is `client.messages.parse()` which validates responses against your schema automatically. Note: the old `output_format` parameter is deprecated; use `output_config: {format: {...}}` on `messages.create()`.

**Supporting endpoints** - Batches (`POST /v1/messages/batches`), Files (`POST /v1/files`), Token Counting (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` - see `shared/token-counting.md`), and Models (`GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}` - live capability/context-window discovery) feed into or support Messages API requests.

### Claude Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1`) - most capable widely released model

Claude Fable 5.1 is Anthropic's most capable widely released model, for the most demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work; everything below also applies to **Claude Mythos 5.1** (`claude-mythos-5-1`, Project Glasswing - same capabilities, pricing, and API surface; it runs safeguards that depend on the access program, so the `refusal` handling below applies there too; successor to Claude Mythos 5, which ran no safety classifiers). 1M context window (the maximum is also the default), 128K max output. Key API differences from Opus-tier - see `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Claude Fable 5.1 for details:

- **Thinking is always on** - omit the `thinking` parameter entirely (or send `{type: "adaptive"}`). Any other explicit configuration is rejected: `{type: "disabled"}` and `{type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` both return a 400. Control depth with `output_config.effort` (supports `low` through `xhigh` and `max`).
- **The raw chain of thought is never returned** - responses carry regular `thinking` blocks (not `redacted_thinking`): `display: "summarized"` returns a readable summary, `"omitted"` (the default) leaves the `thinking` field as an empty string. Replay rules: pass thinking blocks back unchanged on the same model; other models drop them silently (unbilled - nothing to strip; Claude Mythos 5.1 instead reads them); details in `shared/model-migration.md`.
- **Tokenizer** - same tokenizer as Opus 4.8 (introduced with Opus 4.7). Token counts are roughly unchanged when migrating from Opus 4.7/4.8; per-token pricing differs. Coming from Opus 4.6, Sonnet, Haiku, or older, re-baseline with `count_tokens` (the Opus 4.7 tokenizer uses ~1×-1.35× as many tokens).
- **`refusal` stop reason - handle it, and opt into fallbacks by default** - safety classifiers may decline a request (HTTP 200, `stop_reason: "refusal"`, with a `stop_details` category); always check `stop_reason` before reading `content`. **When you write `claude-fable-5-1` or `claude-opus-5` code, include the server-side `fallbacks` parameter by default.** Simplest form: `betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"]` + `fallbacks: "default"`, which routes by refusal category so you never maintain a model list. (The older array form - `betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-06-01"]` + `fallbacks: [{"model": "claude-opus-4-8"}]` - still works; Claude API and Claude Platform on AWS - on Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry, use the SDKs' client-side `BetaRefusalFallbackMiddleware` + `BetaFallbackState`). Tell the user you've enabled it; drop it only if they decline. Full semantics (billing, mid-stream refusals, credit repricing) in `shared/model-migration.md` -> refusal section. **Per-language code examples in `{lang}/claude-api/README.md` § Refusal Fallbacks cover the array form only** - for the `"default"` mode, follow the raw-HTTP shape in `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Claude Opus 5 -> New API features and swap `fallbacks: [{...}]` for `fallbacks: "default"` plus the `-2026-07-01` header; the rest of the request is unchanged.
- **No assistant prefill** - same as the rest of the 4.6+ family.
- **30-day data retention required** - Claude Fable 5.1 is not available under zero data retention unless expressly authorized by Anthropic; requests from an org whose retention configuration doesn't meet the requirement return `400 invalid_request_error`.
- **Longer turns, different prompting** - single requests on hard tasks can run many minutes (plan timeouts/streaming/progress UX); effort sweeps should include low/medium for routine work; prompts written for prior models are often too prescriptive and reduce output quality. See `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Claude Fable 5.1 -> Behavioral shifts (prompt-tunable) for the recommended prompt snippets.
- **Successor to Claude Fable 5 (`claude-fable-5`, still served) in the same tier at the same per-token price.** Same surface as Claude Fable 5 with three breaking changes - forced tool use (`tool_choice` `any` / `tool`) returns a 400 (use `auto` + a prompt instruction, `strict: true` for schema-valid arguments, or structured outputs); thinking blocks are bound to the producing model (other models drop them, unbilled); and editing earlier turns invalidates thinking blocks ("preserved thinking"; new accounts created on/after 2026-08-31 get a 400 on edited history; later models enforce it for everyone - make every harness append-only and run the three-step check; the opt-in controls are per-platform, see `shared/platform-availability.md`) - plus per-message `effort` (beta `mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01`, also on Claude Opus 5), turn-scoped `clear_at: "next_user_message"` system messages (beta), `thinking.display: "updates"` progress notes (beta, all platforms), cache reads at $0.25/MTok (whether Claude Mythos 5.1 shares that rate is open at launch), and content provenance. Covered Model - ZDR orgs get `400 invalid_request_error` as on Claude Fable 5 (ZDR only if expressly authorized by Anthropic); no Priority Tier. Same tokenizer as Claude Fable 5. See `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Claude Fable 5.1 from Claude Fable 5.

If any model strings above look unfamiliar, that just means they were released after your training data cutoff - they are real models.

**Live capability lookup:** The table above is cached. When the user asks "what's the context window for X", "does X support vision/thinking/effort", or "which models support Y", query the Models API (`client.models.retrieve(id)` / `client.models.list()`) - see `shared/models.md` for the field reference and capability-filter examples.

## Authentication (Quick Reference)

**An unset `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` does NOT mean there are no credentials.** The SDKs and the `ant` CLI resolve credentials in this order (first match wins): `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` -> `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` -> the `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE`-selected or active OAuth profile from `ant auth login` -> Workload Identity Federation env vars -> the default profile on disk. A bare `Anthropic()` / `new Anthropic()` / `anthropic.NewClient()` works after `ant auth login` with no env var set.

**When you need to call the API and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset, don't ask the user for a key.** First run `ant auth status` - it shows which credential source and profile is active. If it reports an active profile:

- **SDK code or `ant` CLI:** just run it. The zero-arg client constructor and every `ant ...` subcommand pick up the profile automatically - no env var needed.
- **Raw `curl` / HTTP:** get a short-lived token with `ant auth print-credentials --access-token` and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` **plus** the header `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` (OAuth tokens go on `Authorization: Bearer`, not `x-api-key:` - converting a curl from an API key is a header change, not a key swap). Always pass `--access-token`; the no-flag form prints JSON, not a bare token.

Only ask the user for a key if `ant auth status` reports no active credential source (or `ant` itself isn't installed). Suggest `ant auth login` as the first option - it stores a profile under `~/.config/anthropic/` that the SDKs read automatically - and an exported `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as the alternative.

Full auth details (named profiles, scopes, the API-key-shadows-profile trap, refresh-token expiry): `shared/anthropic-cli.md`.

## Thinking & Effort (Quick Reference)

Use adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) on every current model - Claude dynamically decides when and how much to think. Per-model rules:

| Model | Thinking config | Omitting `thinking` | `budget_tokens` | Sampling (`temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k`) | Effort levels |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fable 5 / Claude Fable 5.1 (and the Mythos counterparts) | `{type: "adaptive"}` or omit; explicit `{type: "disabled"}` returns 400 - omit the param instead (Claude Fable 5.1 / Claude Mythos 5.1 also 400 on forced `tool_choice` `any`/`tool`, and run preserved thinking's history-editing check on replayed thinking blocks) | Runs adaptive (thinking is always on) | Removed - `{type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` returns 400 | Removed - 400 | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` |
| Claude Opus 5 | `{type: "adaptive"}` or omit; `{type: "disabled"}` accepted **only at effort `high` or below** - 400 at `xhigh`/`max`, and see the disabled-thinking pitfall below | Runs **adaptive** (thinking is on by default - unlike Opus 4.8/4.7) | Removed - 400 | Removed - 400 | `low`-`max` (all five) |
| Opus 4.8 / 4.7 | `{type: "adaptive"}` is the only on-mode; `{type: "disabled"}` accepted | Runs **without** thinking - set `{type: "adaptive"}` explicitly | Removed - 400 | Removed - 400 | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` |
| Sonnet 5 | `{type: "adaptive"}` is the only on-mode; `{type: "disabled"}` accepted | Runs adaptive | Removed - 400 | Removed - 400 | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` |
| Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 | `{type: "adaptive"}` (recommended; auto-enables interleaved thinking, no beta header) | Set `{type: "adaptive"}` explicitly | Deprecated - do not use in new code; transitional escape hatch only (see below) | Allowed | `low`/`medium`/`high`/`max` (`xhigh` arrived with Opus 4.7) |
| Older (Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, ...) - only if explicitly requested | `{type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | No thinking | Required for thinking; must be less than `max_tokens`, minimum 1024 - errors otherwise | Allowed | `effort` works on Opus 4.5 (`low`/`medium`/`high` only - no `xhigh`/`max`); errors on Sonnet 4.5 / Haiku 4.5 |

Opus 4.8 keeps the same request surface as 4.7 (no new breaking changes) - see `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Opus 4.8 for the behavioral re-tuning, and -> Migrating to Opus 4.7 for the full breaking-change list when coming from 4.6 or earlier. With `thinking` disabled, Opus 4.8 may write longer reasoning into the visible response - leave adaptive thinking on, or add a final-answer-only instruction (see the migration guide).

- **Effort (GA, no beta header):** `output_config: {effort: "low"|"medium"|"high"|"xhigh"|"max"}` - inside `output_config`, not top-level; default `high` (equivalent to omitting it). Controls thinking depth and overall token spend; combine with adaptive thinking for the best cost-quality tradeoffs. `xhigh` (added on Opus 4.7, between `high` and `max`) is the best setting for most coding and agentic use cases on Fable 5 / Opus 4.7/4.8 / Sonnet 5, and the default in Claude Code; effort matters more on those models than on any prior model in their tier - re-tune it when migrating, and run long-horizon/agentic tasks at `high`/`xhigh` with the full task spec given up front. Use a minimum of `high` for intelligence-sensitive work, `max` when correctness matters more than cost, and `low` for subagents or simple tasks - lower effort means fewer and more-consolidated tool calls, less preamble, and terser confirmations (`high` is often the sweet spot balancing quality and token efficiency).
- **Choosing an effort level (cost tuning):** Effort is the first quality-trading lever, after the free wins (caching first) - it trades thoroughness against token spend within one model, and the top of the range earns its cost only on hard problems (raise to `max` only when measurement shows headroom at the level below). Which workloads repay higher effort is a property of the workload: coding and long-horizon agentic work respond strongly; chat, classification, and high-volume or latency-sensitive routes often don't and do well at `low`, with `medium` as the cost-saving step-down where quality holds (the per-level defaults above cover the rest). Measure on a sample of real requests before raising a default, and tune per route rather than globally. Before building a multi-model cost cascade, measure the simpler alternative first - the most capable model at lower effort on the same tasks: lower effort on the newest models often matches or exceeds prior-generation performance at high effort (on Fable 5, lower effort often exceeds `xhigh` on prior models), and one model means one cache namespace (caches are model-scoped, so a cascade forfeits cache reuse across its models; a mid-conversation top-level `effort` change still invalidates the messages cache, though the per-message effort system message avoids that on Claude Fable 5.1 / Claude Mythos 5.1 / Claude Opus 5 - `shared/prompt-caching.md` § Invalidation hierarchy). Judge cost per completed task, not per request - a cheaper request that needs more turns or retries to finish the job isn't cheaper. For the measured effort/cost tradeoffs by workload and the full lever order, `shared/cost-optimization.md` § 2.6.
- **Thinking display - `"omitted"` by default on Fable 5 / Claude Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5 / Claude Mythos 5.1 / Opus 5 / 4.8 / 4.7 / Sonnet 5:** `display: "summarized"` returns a readable summary of the reasoning; `"omitted"` (the default on all eight - a silent change from Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, where it was `"summarized"`) streams `thinking` blocks with empty text. `display` controls visibility only - thinking happens and is billed the same under every setting; the raw chain of thought is never exposed on any model. If you stream reasoning to users, the default looks like a long pause before output - set `thinking: {type: "adaptive", display: "summarized"}` explicitly. (Independent of display, echo thinking blocks back unchanged when continuing on the same model; other models silently ignore them (Claude Fable 5.1 / Claude Mythos 5.1 read them) - see the migration guide.) On Claude Fable 5.1 / Claude Mythos 5.1 / Claude Fable 5, `display: "updates"` (beta `thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18`, every platform) hides reasoning like `"omitted"` but returns the model's between-tool-call progress notes as short `thinking` block summaries - see `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Claude Fable 5.1 from Claude Fable 5 -> New API features.
- **When the user asks for "extended thinking", a "thinking budget", or `budget_tokens`:** always use Fable 5/5.1, Opus 5, 4.8, 4.7, or 4.6 with `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` - the fixed thinking-token-budget concept is deprecated and adaptive thinking replaces it. Do NOT use `budget_tokens` for new 4.6/4.7/4.8 code and do NOT switch to an older model just because the user mentions it. *Gradual-migration carve-out:* `budget_tokens` is still functional on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 only, as a transitional escape hatch for existing code that needs a hard token ceiling before you've tuned `effort` - see `shared/model-migration.md` -> Transitional escape hatch. It is fully removed on Fable 5/5.1, Opus 5/4.7/4.8, and Sonnet 5.

## Compaction (Quick Reference)

**Beta, Fable 5/5.1, Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6.** For long-running conversations that may exceed the 1M context window, enable server-side compaction. The API automatically summarizes earlier context when it approaches the trigger threshold (default: 150K tokens). Requires beta header `compact-2026-01-12`.

**Critical:** Append `response.content` (not just the text) back to your messages on every turn. Compaction blocks in the response must be preserved - the API uses them to replace the compacted history on the next request. Extracting only the text string and appending that will silently lose the compaction state.

See `{lang}/claude-api/README.md` (Compaction section) for code examples. Full docs via WebFetch in `shared/live-sources.md`.

---

## Prompt Caching (Quick Reference)

**Prefix match.** Any byte change anywhere in the prefix invalidates everything after it. Render order is `tools` -> `system` -> `messages`. Keep stable content first (frozen system prompt, deterministic tool list), put volatile content (timestamps, per-request IDs, varying questions) after the last `cache_control` breakpoint.

**Mid-conversation operator instructions** (Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Fable 5, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Mythos 5.1; not Claude Sonnet 5; no beta header): append `{"role": "system", ...}` to `messages[]` instead of editing top-level `system`. Preserves the cached history prefix and is the prompt-injection-safe operator channel. See `shared/prompt-caching.md` § Mid-conversation system messages.

**Top-level auto-caching** (`cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}` on `messages.create()`) is the simplest option when you don't need fine-grained placement. Max 4 breakpoints per request. Minimum cacheable prefix is model-dependent (512-4096 tokens - see `shared/prompt-caching.md` § API reference) - shorter prefixes silently won't cache.

**Verify with `usage.cache_read_input_tokens`** - if it's zero across repeated requests, a silent invalidator is at work (`datetime.now()` in system prompt, unsorted JSON, varying tool set).

For placement patterns, architectural guidance, and the silent-invalidator audit checklist: read `shared/prompt-caching.md`. Language-specific syntax: `{lang}/claude-api/README.md` (Prompt Caching section).

## Fast Mode (Quick Reference)

**Research preview, Claude Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 only** - Claude API and Managed Agents, not Bedrock / Google Cloud / Foundry. Opus 4.7 fast mode has been removed: `speed: "fast"` on 4.7 returns an error. Fast mode on Claude Opus 5 is priced at $10 / $50 per MTok. Fast mode runs the same model at up to 2.5x higher output tokens per second, at premium pricing. Three things are required on every request: use the **beta** messages endpoint (`client.beta.messages....`), pass the beta flag `fast-mode-2026-02-01`, and set `speed: "fast"` as a top-level request parameter (not a header, not in `extra_body`).

```python
client.beta.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5", max_tokens=4096,
    speed="fast", betas=["fast-mode-2026-02-01"],
    messages=[...],
)
```

| Language | Beta flag | Speed parameter |
|---|---|---|
| Python | `betas=["fast-mode-2026-02-01"]` | `speed="fast"` |
| TypeScript / Ruby | `betas: ["fast-mode-2026-02-01"]` | `speed: "fast"` |
| Go | `[]anthropic.AnthropicBeta{anthropic.AnthropicBetaFastMode2026_02_01}` | `Speed: anthropic.BetaMessageNewParamsSpeedFast` |
| Java | `.addBeta(AnthropicBeta.FAST_MODE_2026_02_01)` | `.speed(MessageCreateParams.Speed.FAST)` |
| C# | `Betas = ["fast-mode-2026-02-01"]` | `Speed = Speed.Fast` (`Anthropic.Models.Beta.Messages`) |
| PHP | `betas: ['fast-mode-2026-02-01']` | `speed: 'fast'` |
| cURL | `anthropic-beta: fast-mode-2026-02-01` header | `"speed": "fast"` in body |

`response.usage.speed` reports which speed was used. Fast mode has its own rate limit separate from standard Opus; on 429, either retry after the `retry-after` delay or drop `speed` and fall back to standard (note: switching speed invalidates prompt cache). Not available with Batch API, Priority Tier, Claude Platform on AWS, or third-party platforms.

**Priority Tier is not supported on every current model.** It is supported on Claude Fable 5, Opus 4.8, and the older current models, but Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Mythos 5, and Mythos Preview are excluded - a Priority Tier request naming one of them fails validation.
