255		builder.WriteString(styleTitle.Render("dev  "+strings.ToUpper(m.overlay.title)) + "\n\n")
256		switch m.overlay.kind {
257		case overlayHelp:
258			builder.WriteString("  navigation\n")
259			builder.WriteString("    j/k, arrows move · ctrl+d/u page · g/G first/last · tab/h/l switch view\n")
260			builder.WriteString("    left click row/tab · wheel 3 rows · right click row actions · click never opens\n")
261			builder.WriteString("    / filter · 0 clear · r reload · esc close/clear/quit · q quit\n\n")
262			builder.WriteString("  TASKS   enter open · n add note · N notes · p park · c next · 1/2/3 state · a done\n")
263			builder.WriteString("  REPOS   enter open · n add note · N notes · space worktrees · m metadata · y copy · s worktree task · d direct task · O/R sort\n")
264			builder.WriteString("  FLEET   enter Herdr/SSH open · e edit remotes.toml · r refresh · read-only Git overview\n")
265			builder.WriteString("  TRY     enter open · n create · space actions · a history · O/R sort\n")
266			builder.WriteString("  REMOTE  enter open local · n/N notes when cloned · c clone (enter stay / o open)\n")
267			builder.WriteString("  SKILLS  a add · c check · u update · e open file · y copy · A context/all scope\n")
268			builder.WriteString("  MCP     static declarations only · e open config · y copy · A context/all scope · r reload\n\n")
269			builder.WriteString("  " + styleHelp.Render("? / esc / q close help"))
270	
271		case overlayActionMenu:
272			builder.WriteString("  " + m.overlay.subject + "\n")
273			if m.overlay.detail != "" {
274				builder.WriteString("  " + m.overlay.detail + "\n")
275			}
276			builder.WriteString("\n")
277			for index := 0; index < m.overlay.optionCount; index++ {
278				prefix := "  "
279				line := m.overlay.optionLabels[index]
280				if index == m.overlay.optionIndex {
281					prefix = "▸ "
282					line = styleSelected.Render(line)
283				}
284				builder.WriteString(prefix + line + "\n")
285			}
286			builder.WriteString("\n  " + styleHelp.Render("j/k choose · enter continue · esc cancel"))
287	
288		case overlayRepoForm, overlayTryForm, overlayTryConfirm:
289			if m.overlay.target.Item.ID != "" {
290				builder.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("  %s\n  %s\n\n", m.overlay.target.Item.DisplayName(), contract(m.overlay.target.Item.Live.CurrentPath)))
291			} else if m.overlay.repoTarget.Repo.Path != "" {
292				builder.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("  %s\n  %s\n\n", m.overlay.repoTarget.Repo.Display(), contract(m.overlay.repoTarget.Repo.Path)))
293			}
294			for index := 0; index < m.overlay.fieldCount; index++ {
295				marker := "  "
296				if index == m.overlay.fieldIndex {
297					marker = "▸ "
298				}
299				builder.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("%s%-10s %s\n", marker, m.overlay.fields[index].label+":", m.overlay.fields[index].input.View()))
300			}
301			if m.err != nil {
302				builder.WriteString("\n  " + styleErr.Render("✗ "+m.err.Error()))
303			}
304			builder.WriteString("\n\n  " + styleHelp.Render("tab field · enter submit · esc cancel"))
305		}
306		return builder.String()
307	}

566			m.status = string(tryAction) + " in progress…"
567			return m, m.applyTry(TryRequest{Action: tryAction, ID: row.Item.ID})

569			return m, nil

402	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
403		cfg := Default()
404		if path == "" {
405			path = ConfigFile()
406		}
407		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
408		switch {
409		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
410			return cfg, nil
411		case err != nil:
412			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
413		}
414		if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
415			// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
416			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
417			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
418		}
419		cfg.Source = path
420		return cfg, cfg.Validate()

459	func (m Model) toggleSelectedRepo() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
460		item, ok := m.currentRepoItem()
461		if !ok || item.Repo.Worktrees == 0 {
462			return m, nil
463		}
464		if item.Repo.Context.WorktreeErr != nil {
465			m.err = item.Repo.Context.WorktreeErr
466			return m, nil
467		}
468		if item.child() {
469			for i := m.repoCursor - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
470				if !m.visibleRepoItems()[i].child() {
471					m.repoCursor = i
472					break
473				}
474			}
475		}
476		m.toggleRepo(item.Repo)
477		return m, nil
478	}
479	
480	func (m Model) promptSelectedRemoteClone() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
481		row, ok := m.currentRemote()
482		if !ok || row.Cloned() {
483			return m, nil
484		}
485		if row.CloneProblemPath != "" {
486			if _, err := os.Lstat(row.CloneProblemPath); err == nil {
487				m.err = fmt.Errorf("inspect or move the existing clone destination at %s before retrying", config.Contract(row.CloneProblemPath))
488				return m, nil
489			}
490			m.setRemoteCloneProblem(row, "")
491		}
492		if !m.reposReadyForClone() {
493			m.setViewStatus(ViewRemote, "wait for local repositories to finish loading")
494			return m, nil
495		}
496		m.remoteClonePrompt = row
497		return m.prompt(modeConfirmClone, row.Repo.FullName, "enter clone; o clone and open; esc cancel")
498	}
499	
500	func (m Model) promptSelectedSkillUpdate() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
501		if m.viewLoad(ViewSkills).loading {
502			m.setViewStatus(ViewSkills, "wait for the current skill reload/check to finish")
503			return m, nil
504		}
505		row, ok := m.currentSkill()
506		if !ok {
507			return m, nil
508		}
509		if !agentskill.CanUpdate(row) {
510			m.err = fmt.Errorf("%s has no update-safe provider lock", row.Name)
511			return m, nil
512		}
513		m.skillUpdateTarget = row
514		m.mode = modeConfirmSkillUpdate
515		return m, nil
516	}

79	func (r RepoRow) IsTry() bool {
80		return r.Asset != nil && r.Asset.Kind == catalog.KindTry && r.Asset.Experiment != nil &&
81			(r.Asset.Experiment.Phase == catalog.PhaseActive || r.Asset.Experiment.Phase == catalog.PhaseDeprecated)

84	func (r RepoRow) HotTasks() int {
85		n := 0

89			}
90		}
91		return n
92	}
93	
94	// StateSummary renders the repository's tasks as a compact per-state tally,
95	// which is what makes the list scannable at forty repositories.
96	func (r RepoRow) StateSummary() string {
97		if len(r.Tasks) == 0 {
98			return ""
99		}
100		counts := map[task.State]int{}
101		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
102			counts[t.State]++
103		}
104		var parts []string
105		for _, s := range task.States {
106			if counts[s] > 0 {
107				parts = append(parts, s.Icon()+strconv.Itoa(counts[s]))
108			}
109		}
110		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
111	}

144			b.WriteString(" ")
145			b.WriteString(checkout.Branch())
146			b.WriteString(" ")

152	func (r RepoRow) matches(query string) bool {
153		query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
154		for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
155			key, value, structured := strings.Cut(term, ":")
156			if structured {
157				switch key {
158				case "tag":
159					if r.Asset == nil || !r.Asset.HasTag(value) {
160						return false
161					}
162					continue
163				case "remote":
164					if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Topology.Summary()), value) {
165						return false
166					}
167					continue
168				case "size":
169					if !matchesSize(r.Usage, value) {
170						return false
171					}
172					continue
173				case "kind":
174					kind := catalog.KindRepository
175					if r.Asset != nil {
176						kind = r.Asset.Kind
177					}
178					if string(kind) != value {
179						return false
180					}
181					continue
182				}
183			}
184			if !strings.Contains(r.searchText(), term) {
185				return false
186			}
187		}
188		return true
189	}

The copies already differ only in load reason/entry guard and in a few hard-coded Fleet status/dispatcher choices that existing generic helpers can express.

3629			m.capabilityScope = CapabilityStartupContext
3630		} else {
3631			m.capabilityScope = CapabilityAllRepositories
3632		}
3633		m.resetCapabilityView(ViewSkills)
3634		m.resetCapabilityView(ViewMCP)
3635		m.err, m.status = nil, ""
3636	
3637		view := m.view
3638		m.beginViewLoad(view, loadRefresh)
3639		if err := m.dependentReposUnavailable(view); err != nil {
3640			state := m.viewLoad(view)
3641			m.applyViewResult(view, state.generation, false, "", "", 0, err, false)
3642			return m, nil
3643		}
3644		if m.viewWaitsForRepos(view) {
3645			m.setViewStatus(view, "waiting for local repositories…")
3646			return m, nil
3647		}
3648		m.setViewStatus(view, dependentLoadingStatus(view))
3649		return m, m.reloadDependentView(view)
3650	}
3651	
3652	func (m Model) viewUsesRepos(view View) bool {
3653		switch view {
3654		case ViewFleet:
3655			return m.actions.ReloadFleetWithRepos != nil
3656		case ViewSkills:
3657			return m.actions.ReloadSkillsWithRepos != nil
3658		case ViewMCP:
3659			return m.actions.ReloadMCPWithRepos != nil
3660		default:
3661			return false
3662		}
3663	}
3664	
3665	func (m Model) viewWaitsForRepos(view View) bool {
3666		return m.viewUsesRepos(view) && m.viewLoad(ViewRepos).loading
3667	}
3668	
3669	func (m Model) dependentReposUnavailable(view View) error {
3670		if !m.viewUsesRepos(view) {
3671			return nil
3672		}
3673		repos := m.viewLoad(ViewRepos)
3674		if repos.loading || (repos.hasSnapshot && repos.freshness == perftrace.FreshnessFresh) {
3675			return nil
3676		}
3677		if err := m.viewError(ViewRepos); err != nil {
3678			return fmt.Errorf("local repository inventory: %w", err)
3679		}
3680		return errors.New("local repository inventory is unavailable")
3681	}
3682	
3683	func dependentLoadingStatus(view View) string {
3684		switch view {
3685		case ViewFleet:
3686			return "loading configured dev hosts…"
3687		case ViewSkills:
3688			return "loading agent skills…"
3689		case ViewMCP:
3690			return "loading MCP declarations…"
3691		default:
3692			return "loading…"
3693		}
3694	}
3695	
3696	func (m Model) reloadDependentView(view View) tea.Cmd {
3697		switch view {
3698		case ViewFleet:
3699			return m.reloadFleet()
3700		case ViewSkills:
3701			return m.reloadSkills()
3702		case ViewMCP:
3703			return m.reloadMCP()
3704		default:
3705			return nil
3706		}
3707	}
3708	
3709	func (m *Model) afterReposResult(valid bool, err error) tea.Cmd {
3710		fresh := valid && err == nil
3711		var commands []tea.Cmd
3712		for _, view := range []View{ViewFleet, ViewSkills, ViewMCP} {
3713			if !m.viewUsesRepos(view) {
3714				continue
3715			}
3716			state := m.viewLoad(view)
3717			if state.loading || m.view == view {
3718				m.beginViewLoad(view, loadRefresh)
3719				if fresh {
3720					m.setViewStatus(view, dependentLoadingStatus(view))
3721					commands = append(commands, m.reloadDependentView(view))
3722					continue
3723				}
3724				dependencyErr := err
3725				if dependencyErr == nil {
3726					dependencyErr = errors.New("local repository inventory is unavailable")
3727				}
3728				current := m.viewLoad(view)
3729				m.applyViewResult(view, current.generation, false, "", "", 0, dependencyErr, false)
3730				continue
3731			}
3732			if state.hasSnapshot {
3733				m.invalidateView(view)
3734			}
3735		}
3736		return batchCommands(commands...)
3737	}
3738	
3739	// afterViewSwitch lazily loads optional inventories only when their view is
3740	// first opened, so starting the dashboard never waits on the network, a forge
3741	// CLI, or Node tooling.
3742	func (m Model) afterViewSwitch() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
3743		m.setAt(m.at())

3777				}
3778				m.setViewStatus(ViewSkills, dependentLoadingStatus(ViewSkills))

3780			}
3781		case ViewMCP:
3782			if m.viewNeedsLoad(ViewMCP) {

3784				if err := m.dependentReposUnavailable(ViewMCP); err != nil {

3793				m.setViewStatus(ViewMCP, dependentLoadingStatus(ViewMCP))
3794				return m, m.reloadMCP()
3795			}

1	---
2	description: Record dev-cli dependencies, upstream preview status, documentation constraints, and behavior that is intentionally incomplete.
3	authority: project-and-upstream
4	status: evolving
5	verified_on: 2026-09-03
6	tested_with: Claude Code 2.1.259
7	---
8	
9	# Compatibility and known limitations
10	
11	This page separates graceful degradation from real limitations. Reverify it whenever command/runtime code or version-sensitive Claude Code documentation changes.
12	
13	## dev-cli capability matrix
14	
15	| Capability | Dependency | Without it |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| core repository/task/worktree operations | Git | unavailable; Git is the only hard runtime dependency |
18	| rich grouped runtime and agent activity | Herdr server + CLI | `auto` tries tmux, then Zellij, then none |
19	| named terminal session | tmux or compatible Zellij | `none` preserves core behavior and shell navigation |
20	| GitHub pull requests/remotes | `gh` authenticated | branch still pushes when Git works; browser/manual flow may be needed |
21	| GitLab merge requests/remotes | `glab` authenticated | same graceful fallback |
22	| repository bootstrap publishing | authenticated `gh` or `glab` | local repository/scaffold still works; the wizard explains how to log in |
23	| remote repository snapshot template | Git plus network/authentication for the source | validation fails before the destination is created and rendered URL userinfo is redacted; local templates still work |
24	| native skill inventory | local filesystem plus the versioned `skills@1.5.23` path registry | always available; explicit add/update requires a directly installed `skills` executable and may use the network; repository-local npm bins are skipped and cooperating mutations are serialized |
25	| static MCP inventory | readable supported agent config files | missing sources are empty; malformed/unsupported sources produce fresh partial diagnostics, and runtime health is intentionally unavailable |
26	| setup-capable project skills | skills provider plus the entrypoint interpreter | unselected skills are skipped; selected required setup fails before scaffold mutation when its interpreter is unavailable; a clone acquired first is retained |
27	| staged lazygit message prefill | a lazygit version that reads `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` | files remain staged and dev prints the suggested message; normal Git commit remains available |
28	| worktree dependency setup | ecosystem manager (`uv`, npm, Cargo, etc.) | plan reports the missing tool and keeps the checkout |
29	| remote portable-file plan/apply | Git, SSH target running a compatible `dev`, matching existing clone/branch/commit; apply also needs a verified machine UUID pin | fails before content is sent or leaves the target unchanged; no clone/task fallback is inferred |
30	| interactive dashboard | terminal input/output | bare `dev` prints the plain task list when piped |
31	| preview repository flow | terminal input/output | `dev flow` refuses non-TTY use and points to `dev repo context` / JSON inventory |
32	| interactive repository picker | terminal input/output; optional configured `fzf`-compatible selector | a missing selector uses dev's built-in picker; non-TTY input keeps line prompts |
33	| repository-note search | linked `modernc.org/sqlite` with FTS5 | no external `sqlite3` executable is required |
34	| static SSH alias discovery/completion | readable user OpenSSH config | unavailable/unsafe files are diagnosed; no `ssh` process or network is needed |
35	| SSH effective values, fresh probes, bootstrap, and fleet transport | system `ssh` client | static `ssh list`, dry-run, and local config plans remain available; effectful SSH operations fail with capability guidance |
36	| public companion derivation and Ed25519 generation | system `ssh-keygen` | an existing validated `.pub` can still be used; derivation/generation is unavailable |
37	| Windows OpenSSH target bootstrap/fleet helper | remote PowerShell + OpenSSH server | POSIX targets remain available; Windows-specific installer/launcher fails without PowerShell rather than using a shell fallback |
38	| terminal multiplexing on Windows | tmux/Zellij/Herdr (POSIX only) | Windows always uses the `none` backend; `dev shell-init powershell` still moves the shell |
39	| in-place self-update | standalone install (not Homebrew/Scoop/`go install`) | `dev upgrade` delegates to the package manager's upgrade command instead |
40	| verified ephemeral worktree apply | Git, compatible bounded Claude Workflow metadata, known task/artifact state, and every available runtime inventory | report remains available, but missing/unknown proof is never apply-eligible |
41	
42	## Confirmed project limitations
43	
44	### MCP inventory is static and intentionally incomplete
45	
46	`dev mcp list` reads documented static files for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. An absolute `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` relocates Claude user sources; local Claude rows retain their project key, and documented user/project/local/managed project approvals annotate declaration state. That narrow approval calculation is not a general runtime merge. The scanner does not start servers, execute helpers, contact endpoints, query health, or resolve credentials. Plugin caches, hosted connectors, remote organization configuration, inline `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, and command-line-only inputs are omitted. Keep the JSON `coverage` object, additive `local_project_path`, and scope-qualified duplicate rows when automating against this inventory.
47	
48	### Note search and filesystem durability vary by text and platform
49	
50	Latin note queries use term-wise prefix FTS and SQLite ranking. Non-ASCII queries use literal term-wise substring matching because SQLite's `unicode61` tokenizer does not segment arbitrary CJK substrings; those results do not use the same FTS ranking.
51	
52	Note writes sync the file and atomically rename it on every supported platform. Unix also syncs the containing directory after rename/delete. The Windows implementation cannot provide that directory-fsync step, so a sudden power loss has a narrower durability guarantee there. Concurrent mutations by cooperating `dev` processes are serialized and each Markdown replacement is atomic; arbitrary external writers do not participate in that lock.
53	
54	### A merged pull request does not retire its worktree
55	
56	`dev done --pr` pushes and opens a pull/merge request, then leaves the task,
57	runtime, and worktree unchanged because review owns integration. `dev flow` can
58	run an explicit, run-local query for the exact head/base review and report only
59	portable existence, open/draft/merged/closed state, URL, provider, and observation
60	time. It does not query review decisions or checks, persist that evidence, or
61	turn it into DONE. Current `dev sweep` does not query the forge either. Verify
62	integration with exact local ancestry and finish deliberately.
63	
64	`dev pr list --scope local --state merged` now reports which requests the forge considers merged, and which local checkout each belongs to. `dev sweep` still does not consult it, and that is deliberate: a squashed merge produces a commit that is not an ancestor of the local branch, so a forge saying "merged" cannot prove the work is recoverable from the remote. `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` proves containment locally with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, and `dev done --merged` requires an explicit `--confirm-squash` attestation. Treat the pull-request list as a prompt to look, not as permission to delete.
65	
66	### Claude Workflow ephemeral cleanup is strict and version-sensitive
67	
68	`dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees` supports the private layout verified with
69	Claude Code 2.1.259: validated fixed-depth `wf_*.json`, matching worktree meta and
70	journal paths, `runId`, `status`, `workflowProgress` agent state/isolation,
71	`worktreePath`, `spawnedWithWorktree`, journal `started`/`result`, and same-ID
72	resume existence. Unknown add-only JSON fields are tolerated because upstream has
73	no metadata schema version. A missing/wrong required type, changed or unsafe
74	source file, duplicate/path mismatch, exhausted bound, or uncertain timestamp
75	makes the affected evidence unknown or unavailable; dev does not guess another
76	layout or decode payload fields.
77	
78	The 2.1.259 layout does not record provider-observed branch, HEAD, common-dir, or
79	an opaque non-replayable worktree-registration generation. Those are mandatory
80	current-ownership facts, so this adapter leaves `provider-git-identity` unknown
81	and its claims remain report-only. A canonical path, naming convention, or GitDir
82	pathname can be reused and is deliberately not accepted; stale metadata must not
83	attach to a replacement checkout.
84	
85	V1 has no operator attestation. `killed` without a matching child result,
86	progress, or any same-ID resumed transcript remains `unknown` regardless of age.
87	Apply is available only when provider inactivity and every Git/task/artifact/
88	caller/runtime fact are known and safe. `--no-runtime` may produce a report but
89	cannot apply. Missing, prunable, unregistered, and orphan paths are report-only.
90	The command never closes runtimes, prunes worktree registrations, deletes Claude
91	metadata, or force-removes/rescues/stashes/commits dirty or ignored work.
92	
93	This adapter is provider-specific behind a provider-neutral audit/service; no
94	other agent harness is inferred from a path or branch name. If Claude changes the
95	private layout, the safe behavior is an unavailable capability plus unknown
96	candidates until the adapter, fixtures, tested version, and both documentation
97	locales are updated.
98	
99	### Pull-request inventory is limited by the provider surfaces
100	
101	GitHub's `gh search prs` account surface cannot report a head branch, review decision, or check status, so those rows are `detail: "summary"` and cannot be joined to a worktree. An absent field on a summary row means the surface could not report it, not that the value is empty. GitLab's account list does carry branch/merge detail and therefore returns full rows, but its list surfaces report neither pipeline checks nor a normalized review decision.
102	
103	Personal per-repository inventory may make one paginated query per requested role for each repository (author and reviewer by default). It covers repositories `dev` has a task for unless `--all-repos` widens the scan. `--repo` filters both account rows and local targets. Account search cannot distinguish merged from closed, so requesting merged/closed/all narrows an account/all request to local collection; JSON reports that effective scope.
104	
105	The schema-version-1 local join reports expected and live branches, checkout existence, worktree registration, status availability/error, and whether the expected branch is actually checked out. Git details are omitted unless those live checks succeed. Azure DevOps pull requests are not listed at all; a configured target is reported as unsupported rather than failing the command.
106	
107	### Prompt open uses the current terminal, not runtime placement
108	
109	`dev prompt open <recipe>` runs one configured child in the foreground of the
110	terminal/TTY that invoked it. It does not create, focus, reuse, or inject into a
111	Herdr, tmux, or Zellij pane. Inside Herdr it naturally remains in the current
112	pane. To use another Herdr pane, create or focus it manually, enter the exact
113	checkout, and run `prompt open` there.
114	
115	This is intentionally separate from `dev start --run`, whose dispatch target is
116	only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree.
117	`prompt open` neither supplies a fresh runtime surface nor weakens that
118	exact-pane proof. `run` is the non-interactive alternative; it receives no user
119	stdin and defaults to a 10-minute timeout, while `open` reserves stdin for the
120	conversation and has no default timeout.
121	
122	The configured child retains its own permission policy. Recipe instructions are
123	read-only guidance, not a sandbox; `dev` does not add permission flags, answer
124	approval prompts, or parse the response into an action.
125	
126	### Prompt closeout reports do not authorize cleanup
127	
128	`session-close` computes runtime-closure evidence only. An `idle` or `done`
129	covering agent can satisfy that one activity gate, but does not prove that work
130	is committed, artifacts are finalized, review is complete, or task intent is
131	done. Caller-contained, mixed-purpose, active, unknown, and unrecognized
132	sessions remain blocked or unknown as their evidence requires.
133	
134	`workspace-closeout` performs the broader read-only audit: target kind,
135	registration/path, status availability, clean Git state, no in-progress Git
136	operation, known base and containment, task completion, artifact
137	reachability/finalization, and runtime eligibility. A merged pull request is only
138	evidence. Even an `eligible` audit is advisory; `dev retire` recollects and
139	revalidates fresh state before any mutation. Neither recipe closes a runtime,
140	changes Git/task state, deletes a branch/worktree, or grants permission to do so.
141	
142	### Zellij exited sessions are closed but keep their names
143	
144	Zellij keeps exited sessions available for resurrection. `dev` recognizes only
145	the exact `(EXITED - attach to resurrect)` marker, omits those sessions from live
146	coverage, and refuses to create over their names; reclaim one with
147	`zellij delete-session <name>`. A live session name containing `EXITED` is not an
148	exit marker. If a session exits between native listing and layout inspection,
149	open fails closed and asks for a retry rather than resurrecting an old layout at
150	the requested checkout.
151	
152	### Forge CLI sign-in is reported, never retried
153	
154	`gh` and `glab` are optional and independent, and `dev` never authenticates on your behalf. When a provider's stored credential is missing or rejected, `dev` reports which provider and the exact login command — for example ``glab is signed out — run `glab auth login --hostname gitlab.com` `` — and continues with whatever the other provider returned. `dev repo remote` and the TUI REMOTE view render the partial result and warn; `dev pr` fails only when no provider is authenticated at all. `dev doctor` probes sign-in state, so an installed but signed-out CLI is visible before a command needs it.
155	
156	Only a missing or rejected credential is reported this way. A rate limit, a permissions or scope failure, and a network error keep their full diagnostic text including the command that failed, because signing in again would not fix them. The original command and provider output remain in the wrapped error in every case.
157	
158	### Agent session capture is reserved, not wired
159	
160	The task schema has an `AgentSession` field and Herdr inventory can expose live agent session IDs. The production start/park/resume path does not yet capture or attach that ID. Treat the field and live inventory as observability/future integration, not a promise that `dev resume` restores the coding-agent conversation.
161	
162	### Built-in forge cache TTL differs from generated config
163	
164	`dev config init` writes `forge.cache_ttl = "15m"`. With no config file, the current built-in `Forge.CacheTTL` zero value means an existing valid cache is not rejected by age; explicit `r` refresh still replaces it. Freshness also requires a source fingerprint matching the configured GH/GL hosts and Azure targets, so an endpoint change is never hidden by the zero TTL. Legacy source-less caches remain available only through explicit `--cached` and are reported stale. Run `config init` or set the TTL when freshness matters.
165	
166	Older generated configs may contain `forge.remote_limit = 100`. The field is
167	still accepted, but complete forge inventories are now paginated and it no
168	longer caps synchronization. `dev config init` no longer writes it. The
169	`--limit` flag on `dev repo remote` limits rendered matches after the complete
170	inventory has been searched.
171	
172	### Lazygit staged-message prefill is best effort
173	
174	`repo --check-in=stage` writes a pending message in the exact worktree Git
175	directory. [Lazygit v0.59.0 uses that file for lowercase
176	`c`](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216), but it is a
177	lazygit implementation detail rather than a Git interface; uppercase `C` and
178	plain `git commit` do not consume it. Dev never overwrites a different existing
179	draft. A draft-write failure is warning-only: staging remains successful and
180	is never rolled back. If the integration changes upstream, the staged index
181	and printed message remain the recovery path.
182	
183	### Portable files are not project transfer or backup
184	
185	`dev fleet files` moves only explicitly selected, bounded files that both hosts
186	prove are untracked and ignored. It does not acquire a missing clone, transfer
187	task ownership/catalog/notes, run worktree provisioning, watch for later changes,
188	propagate deletion, remove source bytes, produce a remote-backup receipt, verify
189	restore, or authorize eviction. Private transaction staging is not a user-facing
190	backup/restore promise.
191	
192	The source and target must already match by fetch identity, attached branch, and
193	exact commit. Apply additionally needs a verified `machine_id` pin. Native
194	Windows payloads remain disabled until ACL, reparse-point, held-root, and atomic
195	replacement guarantees are implemented and tested there; machine identity
196	diagnostics remain content-free.
197	
198	### Windows has native SSH support and a smaller runtime surface
199	
200	`dev` compiles and runs on `windows/amd64` and `windows/arm64`, and every release ships a `.zip` for each. Core repository/task/worktree operations and the SSH host domain are native: static discovery, protected-DACL managed fragments, reparse-point rejection, native `ssh-keygen.exe`, Windows Job Object cancellation, and POSIX/Windows remote bootstrap are covered. Fleet can also target Windows OpenSSH through its encoded PowerShell launcher. What still differs:
201	
202	- There is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr, so the runtime backend is always `none`. Grouped runtime/agent activity and named sessions are unavailable; the `cd` directive and PowerShell wrapper still work.
203	- Shell integration is `dev shell-init powershell`. POSIX shells hand the directory back on file descriptor 3; PowerShell cannot inherit it, so the wrapper passes a temp-file path in `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` instead.
204	- `dev fleet open` starts a child shell (`%COMSPEC%`) rather than replacing the process, because Windows has no `exec(2)`.
205	- `dev fleet machine-id` can perform its content-free `_capability` probe, but native `fleet files` plan/apply payload helpers are denied before content is sent.
206	- CI keeps an advisory broad Windows suite for unrelated POSIX assumptions, but `internal/sshhost`, `internal/fleet`, and the SSH/fleet/doctor CLI contracts run in a separate required native `windows-latest` gate. Affected tests/packages and the CLI are also compiled for `windows/arm64`.
207	
208	### SSH host management is intentionally narrow
209	
210	Static `dev ssh list` is a provenance/candidate scanner, not a second OpenSSH evaluator. Dynamic `Match`, unsupported Include expansion, cycles, and scan bounds produce `complete: false`; they can block mutation even when plain `ssh` would eventually choose a value. `dev ssh show` and setup route resolution use plain `ssh -G`, so configured resolver and `Match exec` behavior may run. Fresh probes preserve `KnownHostsCommand`, `UpdateHostKeys`, and host-key policy rather than forcing a convenient answer.
211	
212	Setup requires an explicit key or explicit Ed25519 generation and installs public material only. It supports bounded ProxyJump forms plus fixed POSIX and Windows OpenSSH installers; `ProxyCommand`, custom `AuthorizedKeysFile`, forced-shell policy, and ACL-incapable filesystems require manual remediation. Once a remote installer starts, cancellation/failure is `unknown` because the key may have been appended. Dev retains local config/generated keys and never attempts key revocation, private-key deletion/copying, `known_hosts` cleanup, password storage/fallback, or automatic credential rollback. Alias rename/adoption, bulk onboarding, arbitrary directives, and an SSH TUI are also deferred.
213	
214	### Direct mode has a smaller lifecycle
215	
216	A direct task uses the canonical checkout and cannot go COLD, because cold cleanup would remove a directory the repository needs. Use branch-only or worktree mode for cross-machine reconstruction.
217	
218	### Flow intentionally omits expert overrides
219	
220	`dev flow` offers normal managed lifecycle actions, exact unmanaged metadata-only
221	Adopt/clean branch-preserving Remove, and explicit remote evidence. It does not
222	offer dirty commit/discard, WIP, shared-writer, ownership takeover, force, unknown-
223	runtime, or assume-no-runtime choices. A blocked plan shows remediation and the
224	compatible CLI fallback; existing command flags and structured contracts remain
225	available.
226	
227	Task-backed lifecycle and exact unmanaged linked-checkout actions share
228	`internal/taskflow`. Explicit unmanaged path retirement remains an isolated
229	compatibility implementation, while `sweep` retains record-only reaping, orphan
230	salvage, and other narrow reconciliation paths. Do not assume every cleanup path
231	has the same planner. Raw Git and configured external tools also bypass dev's
232	PlanID, locks, revalidation, and result ledger.
233	
234	## Current behaviors that are implemented
235	
236	These were historical gaps and should not be reintroduced as limitations:
237	
238	- `dev repo new|create`, `repo clone`, and `repo setup` share a preset-driven bootstrap pipeline. A plain explicit `repo new NAME` remains minimal, while a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name routes through clone acquisition and preserves source history/remote. The no-argument new-repository wizard detects the same reference in its first field; for a new repository, a default-no customization gate keeps the normal `agent-ready` flow concise. Bare `repo clone` selects exact URLs from the existing forge cache; outside a checkout, bare `start` selects a fast-discovered local repository, while the in-repository path keeps its immediate current default. Both retain manual entry. A configured line selector is optional, with a built-in fallback. Text fields use a TTY inline editor, so cursor keys edit rather than inserting raw escape bytes; non-TTY readers retain line-oriented behavior.
239	- `repo new` can snapshot a local directory/repository or Git source at an optional branch, tag, or commit and confined subdirectory into a fresh history. An unpinned local Git tree includes tracked plus untracked non-ignored files; a non-Git directory includes its full current tree. Source `.git` metadata is excluded, URL userinfo is redacted, unsafe file types/paths fail before destination creation, and held root/file handles confine mutable-path races. Human plans preview paths and warn when the snapshot is live; presets can select catalog-repository subfolders.
240	- Repository setup supports `--check-in=commit|stage|none` (`auto` for preset compatibility). Staged setup runs before-commit setup and `git add -A` without an `after_commit` phase, cannot publish or hand off to `start`, and may prefill lazygit lowercase `c` as described above.
241	- `agent-ready` uses one explicitly incomplete, non-fabricating `AGENTS.md` starter across built-in and native setup paths. Its common top-level ignore excludes only `.specstory/statistics.json`; history, project identity, and config remain visible. Selected skills with matching source and agent targets share one installer invocation. The optional `agent-history-hygiene` initializer additionally writes pre-commit/gitleaks policy and merges missing machine-local `.project.json`/`statistics.json` rules into `.specstory/.gitignore`; custom content and transcript history remain trackable.
242	- Project `.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` are constrained to portable setup policy. Executable project configuration is keyed to the canonical Git common directory and an exact content hash; a changed hash is untrusted until approved again.
243	- `dev ssh init/list/show/setup/probe/remove` provides explicit OpenSSH host onboarding without a separate host database. Dev owns only its dedicated Include, canonical `dev.d` fragments, and opt-in generated fleet registrations; all public SSH JSON is one versioned object, and TSV listing is a documented six-field selector.
244	- Fleet merges user-authored primary `remotes.toml` with strict generated `remotes.d` fragments, tracks `remote_os`, and uses a hidden-helper-only encoded PowerShell launcher for Windows targets. Primary duplicate aliases remain compatible; any generated alias collision fails closed.
245	- `dev repo context --json` exposes additive schema-v1 local/remote evidence with source, age, freshness, completeness, null/error preservation, and scoped readiness; external probes happen only with `--refresh`. `dev status` reuses the cheap local readiness projection without network access.
246	- `dev fleet machine-id` reports an observed UUID without changing configuration. `dev fleet files` is report-only by default, uses a separate `[local_files]` allowlist, negotiates downward-only limits before content, and requires explicit apply/replacement controls plus a matching target pin.
247	
248	- `dev start --focus` activates the runtime after non-JSON creation.
249	- `dev start --run '<shell command>'` dispatches only to an exact root pane from
250	  a newly created first-class Herdr worktree. It is incompatible with `--json`,
251	  non-worktree modes, and non-Herdr runtimes, and does not wait for command exit.
252	- TUI navigation refuses to open a missing COLD checkout and directs the user to `dev resume`.
253	- Preview-labelled `dev flow [repo]` is an independent full-screen TTY model. It resolves canonical/linked cwd to the exact surface, uses a picker outside Git, shows every registered worktree plus task-only records, and makes every mutation Enter-to-plan then approve. Apply revalidates task revision and exact repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact authority and retains partial step results. Local `r` is network-free; `R` explicitly selects fetch/query/both and keeps minimal review evidence run-local.
254	- `DEV_TUI_TRACE` starts at `cli.Execute`; it cannot include OS process loading. `tui.initial_view_returned` measures model construction, not renderer flush or physical terminal paint. Use it for same-profile comparisons rather than universal hardware/network guarantees.
255	- Runtime handles now record backend provenance and are revalidated before cleanup.
256	- `auto` runtime selection includes Zellij between tmux and none.
257	
258	- `dev done` opens an interactive finish wizard on a TTY when `--ff`/`--pr` are both omitted, analyzing a dirty checkout against the base (commit, discard, or cancel) instead of rejecting any uncommitted change outright; a non-interactive caller still passes an explicit `--dirty` policy and `--yes` for a destructive discard.
259	- Human-readable output now carries semantic color (`--color auto|always|never`), automatically disabled when `NO_COLOR` is set, `TERM=dumb`, or stdout/stderr is not a terminal.
260	- `dev done` records MERGED only: it never closes the invoking runtime, removes a worktree, or deletes a branch. Cleanup moved to `dev retire`, which runs from outside the target workspace, refuses active agents and mixed-purpose workspaces, and revalidates Git state after every runtime closure. `dev done --delete-branch` is now an error pointing at `dev retire --delete-branch`, and `--keep-worktree` warns as a no-op.
261	- `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` enumerates linked worktrees from Git rather than from the task registry, so unmanaged worktrees whose branches are contained in the base become retirable. Containment alone is never permission; dirty state, unfinalized artifacts, in-progress Git operations, and runtime refusals all still block it, and branches survive unless `--delete-branches` is passed.
262	- `dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees` adds a separate schema-v1 Claude Workflow report. The path/branch convention is only discovery; exact bounded provider linkage plus fresh Git/task/artifact/caller/runtime evidence authorizes TTY/per-item apply. Apply locks and re-fingerprints, removes without force, retains branches by default, and allows only explicit-base unchanged/contained/zero-unique `branch -d`.
263	- `dev sweep` reports a branch-backed task whose branch Git no longer has as dead and offers to reap the record. Such a task cannot be finished, resumed, or retired, because every one of those paths resolves the branch first; the suggestion stays report-only until `--apply`.
264	- An unknown command is reported instead of discarded. `dev` silences cobra's own error printing and previously also skipped printing anything whose message began with `unknown command`, so a mistyped command produced no output at all on either stream. The message, cobra's "Did you mean this?" suggestions, and a pointer to `--help` are now printed to stderr with exit status 1.
265	- A stray argument to a command family is an error rather than a silent help render. `dev wt bogus` used to print `dev wt` help and exit 0 because a family has no `Run` of its own; every family node now reports the unknown subcommand and exits 1, while a bare family still prints its help and exits 0.
266	- Argument-count and flag errors print the failing command's usage block. `--color` still governs whether that block is colorized.
267	- Each command family's help carries an ASCII orientation diagram and a `See also: dev help <topic>` pointer, and `dev help <command>` resolves a command name or alias to its topic, so `dev help wt` reaches the worktrees page.
268	- Semantic color covers every human-readable surface, including the interactive dashboard: `dev --color never`, `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb` now disable dashboard color too, which they previously did not.
269	- `dev sweep` reaps a task whose repository directory no longer exists. Such a record was unreachable by every command in the binary: `done`, `resume`, `park` and `retire` all resolve the repository first, the dead-branch rule excludes direct mode, and the stale-worktree rule requires a recorded worktree path. A live runtime session rules the suggestion out, and reaping removes only dev's record of intent.
270	- `dev sweep` reports a task-recorded checkout that exists but Git does not register and that holds nothing but agent artifact directories. Removal is offered only when every file inside is byte-identical to one already in the repository; anything else is reported as salvage work and is never removed, including under `--apply`.
271	- `dev sweep` acts on a cold task whose worktree is still on disk. Inventory has always computed that drift for `dev ls` and the dashboard, but sweep never consulted it, so it was displayed and not actionable.
272	- `dev retire <path>` reaps the matching task record. Only the by-task form set the task identity, so retiring the same checkout by path left the record behind; the DONE-state and identity checks are unchanged.
273	- `dev version` reports whether the running build is a published release, and `dev doctor` carries the same line plus the install owner, invoked/resolved executable path, and warnings for distinct `dev` copies on `PATH`. Nothing in the tool answered "am I current?" before, and `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so an untagged feature was invisible to anyone installing it.
274	- A release publishes platform archives and `SHA256SUMS` and takes its notes from `CHANGELOG.md`. Earlier releases published a GitHub release object and nothing else, so their assets are absent by construction.
275	- A release publishes Windows `.zip` archives alongside the Unix `.tar.gz` set, refreshes an in-repo Scoop manifest attached to the release (and pushed to the bucket when a token is configured), and publishes the matching source formula to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`. Homebrew publication is a required release step and fails visibly when its repository token is missing or rejected. A manual workflow can retry or backfill the formula for an existing stable release without creating or moving a tag.
276	- `dev upgrade` downloads the current release for this platform, verifies it against the release `SHA256SUMS`, and replaces the running binary with an atomic rename (Windows moves the live `.exe` aside and sweeps it on the next run). It detects and runs Homebrew, Scoop or `go install` when one of them owns the file; Homebrew users receive releases through the automatically advanced tap instead of an in-place Cellar overwrite.
277	- An interactive `dev` command prints one dim "newer release available" line at most once a day, read from the day-old release cache; it never blocks on the network. For the TUI, a stale-cache background refresh starts only after the initial view returns. `[update] check = false` or `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` disables it.
278

19	// listHeight budgets rows from what the current detail and footer actually
20	// render. REPOS has more detail and more key hints than TASKS; the old fixed
21	// chrome allowance let the complete view exceed terminal height, so Bubble
22	// Tea scrolled the first lines and the top tab bar appeared to disappear.
23	func (m Model) listHeight() int {
24		// Header + its blank line, per-view list preamble, blank before detail,
25		// blank before footer. Detail and footer can each wrap/change by view and
26		// terminal width.
27		fixed := 2 + m.listPreambleLines() + 1 + lineCount(m.renderDetail()) + 1 + lineCount(m.renderFooter())
28		h := m.height - fixed
29		if h < 3 {
30			return 3
31		}
32		// A long list adds the "… x–y of n" scroll note.
33		if m.count() > h && h > 3 {
34			h--
35		}
36		return h
37	}
38	
39	func (m Model) listPreambleLines() int {
40		lines := 1 // the table header, or the one-line empty/loading state
41		switch m.view {
42		case ViewRemote:
43			if m.viewLoad(ViewRemote).loading && len(m.visibleRemotes()) > 0 {

+func (m Model) toggleCapabilityScope() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
+	if m.capabilityScope == CapabilityAllRepositories {
+		m.capabilityScope = CapabilityStartupContext
+	} else {
+		m.capabilityScope = CapabilityAllRepositories
+	}
+	m.resetCapabilityView(ViewSkills)
+	m.resetCapabilityView(ViewMCP)
+	m.err, m.status = nil, ""
+
+	view := m.view
+	m.beginViewLoad(view, loadRefresh)
+	if err := m.dependentReposUnavailable(view); err != nil {
+		state := m.viewLoad(view)
+		m.applyViewResult(view, state.generation, false, "", "", 0, err, false)
+		return m, nil
+	}
+	if m.viewWaitsForRepos(view) {
+		m.setViewStatus(view, "waiting for local repositories…")
+		return m, nil
+	}
+	m.setViewStatus(view, dependentLoadingStatus(view))
+	return m, m.reloadDependentView(view)

570	- **TRY** — dated scratch experiments, including non-Git folders, with durable
571	  tags/notes and explicit active/deprecated/archived/graduated state.
572	- **REMOTE** — repositories visible through authenticated forge CLIs, including
573	  configured Azure DevOps projects, marked when a local repo or Try exists.
574	  What can I open or clone.
575	- **SKILLS** — native project/global agent-skill inventory for the exact startup
576	  checkout plus global sources, with local presence/integrity and an explicitly
577	  checked upstream freshness state. Outside Git it starts as a cross-repository
578	  inventory over accepted REPOS targets; `A` toggles either launch context to all
579	  accepted repositories for this TUI session.
580	- **MCP** — sanitized static MCP declarations for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
581	  Gemini CLI, and OpenCode, scoped to the same startup context by default and
582	  sharing the `A` context/all toggle. It resolves only Claude's documented
583	  project-approval settings; it does not claim connection health or a generally
584	  effective merged runtime configuration.
585	
586	The first view is constructed before runtime auto-detection, project-root lookup,
587	cache decoding, shell-based tool checks, or the optional release refresh can
588	finish. TASKS, REPOS, and TRY then publish independently from one shared local
589	load cycle; REMOTE, FLEET, SKILLS, and MCP remain lazy. A cached REMOTE/FLEET snapshot
590	is immediately usable but is tracked separately from a current live result.
591	Every requested view has its own generation, so `r` cancels the old read, a late
592	result cannot replace a newer one, a failed refresh keeps usable rows visible,
593	and a successful empty result clears obsolete rows. Warning-only SKILLS/MCP
594	source diagnostics keep a fresh partial snapshot, and a visible dependent view
595	resumes automatically after a failed REPOS generation is repaired and reloaded.
596	
597	TASKS, REPOS and TRY use the same services as their non-interactive commands.
598	Git-backed Tries appear in TRY rather than being duplicated in REPOS; REMOTE
599	still knows that local checkout exists. The repo list matters on day one: with
600	forty repositories and no tasks recorded yet, a task-only dashboard would just
601	be empty.
602	
603	Navigation is vim-style, arrows alongside:
604	
605	```
606	j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
607	g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
608	/          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit
609	```
610	
611	Mouse cell tracking is enabled alongside the keyboard model. Left-click selects a
612	visible row or tab, the wheel moves three rows, and right-click selects a row then
613	opens the same available actions used by keyboard shortcuts. Clicks act on press;
614	release/motion and modified clicks are ignored, and repeated clicks never imply
615	open. Terminals that reserve tracked mouse input may require Shift/Option while
616	selecting text.
617	
618	`enter` opens a selected row only when its checkout is currently valid. Inside Herdr/tmux/Zellij it
619	switches the current client; outside it exits the dashboard and attaches to
620	the target session. A COLD worktree task requires `dev resume`; a missing or
621	unregistered worktree requires `dev sweep` first so artifacts can be salvaged
622	before the task is resumed or reaped. A wide TASKS table includes `REPO`; its
623	compact layout keeps repository/path in the selected detail pane. In TASKS, `p`
624	parks and prompts for the next action and `c` edits it. In REPOS, `enter` is pure ad-hoc open,
625	`space` expands linked worktrees inline, `m` edits repository tags/summary,
626	`s` starts an isolated worktree task, and `d` starts a tracked direct task.
627	On TASKS and REPOS, `n` quick-adds a repository thought and `N` opens its notes
628	overlay. Expanded children carry their own Git/session/task state and can be
629	opened directly. In TRY, `n` creates or clones an experiment;
630	`space` opens mark/deprecate/archive/restore/graduate actions; `a` includes
631	retained history. Inside Git, SKILLS and MCP use only the exact startup worktree
632	plus global/user sources; outside Git they reuse every accepted REPOS target and
633	the ordinary startup directory. Uppercase `A` switches both views between that
634	startup context and all accepted repositories for this TUI session, clearing old
635	scope rows before a generation-guarded reload. In SKILLS, `a` opens the upstream
636	interactive installer, `c` performs the opt-in read-only network check after the
637	local snapshot has loaded, and `u` confirms before updating only the selected
638	lock-managed skill in that row's checkout. Source checks hash Git object bytes
639	without running checkout filters; non-ASCII provider folder hashes that cannot be
640	reproduced portably remain unverifiable. Mutations skip repository-local PATH
641	shims and are serialized across `dev` processes. `r` reloads local state without
642	checking the network. MCP only filters/reloads static declarations; it never
643	starts a server or helper. On either capability view, `e` opens the selected local
644	file in `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` and `y` offers file copy choices. `?` opens the complete
645	context-sensitive key map. That makes
646	the branch/worktree and lifecycle costs explicit rather than silently applying
647	them to every directory.
648	
649	For a one-run startup/readiness trace, name an absolute file that does not exist:
650	
651	```bash
652	DEV_TUI_TRACE=/tmp/dev-tui-trace.json dev
653	```
654	
655	The file is created with private permissions after the alternate screen is
656	restored and before a selected runtime is activated. It contains only a bounded,
657	versioned list of relative microsecond timings, aggregate row counts, and
658	categorical view/generation/outcome fields; it never includes project names,
659	paths, commands, key values,
660	URLs, runtime handles, or raw errors, and it is not written to `stats.db` or sent
661	anywhere. `tui.initial_view_returned` means the Bubble Tea view string was built,
662	not that a terminal rasterized it. Cache acceptance, live snapshot acceptance,
663	and load completion are separate events; there is no artificial “all tabs ready”
664	event because REMOTE, FLEET, SKILLS, and MCP may never be visited.
665	
666	REPOS also has an agent-handoff copy menu. Press `y`, then `y` for contextual
667	Markdown, `p` for the checkout path, `b` for the branch, `s` for runtime/agent
668	sessions, or `w` for every linked-worktree path. Parent `yy` includes the whole
669	repo; child `yy` includes only that worktree. SKILLS uses `yp` for the selected
670	`SKILL.md` (or lock-file) path, `ys` for a sanitized summary, `yu` for its

674	network access, but the system clipboard may then contain credentials and other
675	servers stored in that file. The same full repository context is pipe-friendly

679	dev repo context api

453	// WithTrace observes performance boundaries without controlling model state.
454	func (m Model) WithTrace(trace *perftrace.Recorder) Model {
455		m.trace = trace
456		return m
457	}
458	
459	// WithContext bounds asynchronous read/probe commands to one dashboard run.
460	func (m Model) WithContext(ctx context.Context) Model {
461		m.runContext = ctx
462		return m
463	}
464	
465	// WithRemotes seeds the lazy forge view from a fresh on-disk cache. The first
466	// switch is then instant; r still refreshes explicitly.
467	func (m Model) WithRemotes(rows []RemoteRow) Model {
468		m.replaceRemotes(rows)
469		m.seedViewSnapshot(ViewRemote, perftrace.SourceCache, perftrace.FreshnessFresh, true)
470		return m
471	}
472	
473	// WithFleet seeds cached fleet rows while the first live refresh remains lazy.
474	func (m Model) WithFleet(rows []FleetRow) Model {
475		m.fleet = rows
476		m.seedViewSnapshot(ViewFleet, perftrace.SourceCache, perftrace.FreshnessStale, true)
477		return m
478	}
479	
480	// WithRemotesStale marks seeded rows for background refresh on first visit.
481	func (m Model) WithRemotesStale(stale bool) Model {
482		if stale {
483			m.loads[int(ViewRemote)].freshness = perftrace.FreshnessStale
484		}
485		return m
486	}
487	
488	// WithTries seeds the Try view, primarily for tests and embedded callers. The
489	// production dashboard loads it with the other local inventories in Init.
490	func (m Model) WithTries(rows []TryRow) Model {
491		m.tries = rows
492		m.matchRemoteLocals()
493		m.seedViewSnapshot(ViewTries, perftrace.SourceLive, perftrace.FreshnessFresh, true)
494		return m
495	}
496	
497	// BeginLoading makes Init load task, repository, and Try data asynchronously. This lets
498	// the alternate screen appear immediately instead of blocking on dozens of Git
499	// probes before Bubble Tea starts.
500	func (m Model) BeginLoading() Model {
501		m.initialLoad = true
502		m.beginLocalLoads(loadInitial)
503		return m
504	}
505	
506	// Chosen reports a directory the caller should cd into after the program
507	// exits, or "" when there is none.
508	func (m Model) Chosen() string { return m.chosen }
509	
510	// Activation reports the runtime handle to switch/attach after the dashboard
511	// has restored the terminal, or "" when the user quit normally.
512	func (m Model) Activation() string { return m.activate }
513	
514	// CurrentView reports which list is showing.
515	func (m Model) CurrentView() View { return m.view }
516	
517	// CapabilityScope reports whether SKILLS and MCP are scoped to the startup
518	// context or all accepted repositories.
519	func (m Model) CapabilityScope() CapabilityScope { return m.capabilityScope }
520	
521	// Init implements tea.Model.
522	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
523		commands := []tea.Cmd{textinput.Blink}
524		if m.initialLoad {
525			commands = append(commands, m.reload())
526		}
527		if len(m.actions.Tools) > 0 {
528			commands = append(commands, m.probeTools())
529		}
530		if m.actions.LoadRemoteCache != nil {
531			commands = append(commands, m.loadRemoteCache())
532		}
533		if m.actions.LoadFleetCache != nil {
534			commands = append(commands, m.loadFleetCache())
535		}
536		if m.actions.AfterFirstView != nil {
537			commands = append(commands, m.runAfterFirstView())
538		}
539		return tea.Batch(commands...)
540	}

423	// New builds the dashboard.
424	func New(actions Actions, rows []inventory.Row, repos []RepoRow) Model {
425		in := textinput.New()
426		in.CharLimit = 200
427		cloneSpinner := spinner.MiniDot
428		cloneSpinner.FPS = 200 * time.Millisecond
429	
430		m := Model{
431			actions:            actions,
432			rows:               rows,
433			repos:              repos,
434			input:              in,
435			remoteCloneSpinner: spinner.New(spinner.WithSpinner(cloneSpinner)),
436			width:              100,
437			height:             30,
438			firstViewReady:     make(chan struct{}),
439			firstViewOnce:      &sync.Once{},
440		}
441		if len(actions.Tools) > 0 {
442			m.toolGeneration = 1
443		}
444		if rows != nil {
445			m.seedViewSnapshot(ViewTasks, perftrace.SourceLive, perftrace.FreshnessFresh, true)
446		}
447		if repos != nil {
448			m.seedViewSnapshot(ViewRepos, perftrace.SourceLive, perftrace.FreshnessFresh, true)
449		}
450		return m
451	}
452	
453	// WithTrace observes performance boundaries without controlling model state.
454	func (m Model) WithTrace(trace *perftrace.Recorder) Model {
455		m.trace = trace
456		return m
457	}
458	
459	// WithContext bounds asynchronous read/probe commands to one dashboard run.
460	func (m Model) WithContext(ctx context.Context) Model {
461		m.runContext = ctx
462		return m
463	}

+func (m *Model) resetCapabilityView(view View) {
+	m.invalidateView(view)
+	generation := m.loads[int(view)].generation
+	m.loads[int(view)] = viewLoadState{generation: generation}
+	m.viewErrors[int(view)] = nil
+	m.viewStatuses[int(view)] = ""

+	case ViewMCP:

+func (m Model) toggleCapabilityScope() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {

+		m.capabilityScope = CapabilityStartupContext
+	} else {
+		m.capabilityScope = CapabilityAllRepositories
+	}

+	m.resetCapabilityView(ViewMCP)
+	m.err, m.status = nil, ""
+
+	view := m.view

+	}
+	if m.viewWaitsForRepos(view) {

+		return m, nil
+	}
+	m.setViewStatus(view, dependentLoadingStatus(view))

12	func skillFilePath(row agentskill.Skill) (string, error) {
13		if row.Presence != agentskill.PresenceMissing && strings.TrimSpace(row.Path) != "" {
14			return filepath.Join(row.Path, "SKILL.md"), nil
15		}
16		if row.Lock != nil && strings.TrimSpace(row.Lock.File) != "" {
17			return row.Lock.File, nil
18		}
19		return "", fmt.Errorf("skill %s has no local skill or lock file", row.Name)
20	}
21	
22	func (m Model) capabilityFilePath() (string, error) {
23		if row, ok := m.currentSkill(); ok {
24			return skillFilePath(row)
25		}
26		if row, ok := m.currentMCP(); ok {
27			if strings.TrimSpace(row.ConfigPath) == "" {
28				return "", fmt.Errorf("MCP server %s has no local config path", row.Name)
29			}
30			return row.ConfigPath, nil
31		}
32		return "", fmt.Errorf("the selected row has no capability config file")
33	}

35	func formatSkillSummary(row agentskill.Skill) string {
36		lines := []string{
37			"name: " + row.Name,
38			"scope: " + string(row.Scope),
39		}
40		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "repository", row.Repository)
41		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "checkout", row.Checkout)
42		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "path", row.Path)
43		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "agents", strings.Join(row.Agents, ", "))
44		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "managed", string(row.ManagedBy))
45		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "presence", string(row.Presence))
46		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "integrity", string(row.Integrity))
47		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source", row.Source)
48		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source_url", row.SourceURL)
49		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "update", string(row.UpdateStatus))
50		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
51	}
52	
53	func formatMCPSummary(row agentmcp.Declaration) string {
54		lines := []string{
55			"server: " + row.Name,
56			"agent: " + string(row.Agent),
57			"scope: " + string(row.Scope),
58		}
59		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "repository", row.Repository)
60		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "checkout", row.Checkout)
61		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "config", row.ConfigPath)
62		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source", mcpSource(row))
63		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "state", mcpDeclarationState(row))
64		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "transport", string(row.Transport))
65		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "endpoint", row.Endpoint)
66		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "command", row.Command)
67		if row.ArgumentCount > 0 {
68			lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("arguments: %d value(s) redacted", row.ArgumentCount))
69		}
70		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "policies", mcpPolicySummary(row))
71		if len(row.Credentials) > 0 {
72			credentials := make([]string, 0, len(row.Credentials))
73			for _, credential := range row.Credentials {
74				value := string(credential.Kind)
75				if credential.Name != "" {
76					value += ":" + credential.Name
77				}
78				credentials = append(credentials, value)
79			}
80			lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "credentials", strings.Join(credentials, ", "))
81		}
82		if len(row.Redactions) > 0 {
83			redactions := make([]string, len(row.Redactions))
84			for i, redaction := range row.Redactions {
85				redactions[i] = string(redaction)
86			}
87			lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "redacted", strings.Join(redactions, ", "))
88		}
89		if len(row.Coverage) > 0 {
90			coverage := make([]string, len(row.Coverage))
91			for i, item := range row.Coverage {
92				coverage[i] = string(item.Code)
93			}
94			lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "coverage", strings.Join(coverage, ", "))
95		}
96		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
97	}
98	
99	func appendSummaryLine(lines []string, label, value string) []string {
100		if strings.TrimSpace(value) == "" {
101			return lines
102		}
103		return append(lines, label+": "+value)
104	}

294	exact Claude local project identity, bounded credential-reference summaries, and
295	redaction markers—never raw args, environment/header/OAuth values, indirect file
296	content, or connection health. That normalization still governs rows, safe
297	summaries, and JSON. Explicit `yf` instead reads the entire local source file (up
298	to 1 MiB) into the system clipboard; it performs no network access but may copy
299	credentials and other declarations from the same file.
300	
301	## Heatmap and editors
302	
303	```
304	H   open the selected repository's one-year activity heatmap
305	    b backfills only that repo; r rereads stats; H / esc returns
306	
307	e   edit effective dev config on ordinary views; edit the selected capability file on SKILLS/MCP
308	r   reparse config and reload local/remote data and tool bindings
309	```
310	
311	An empty heatmap is actionable: press `b` to derive only the selected repo's
312	history into stats.db and automatically redraw. `r` does not manufacture data;
313	it rereads what collectors/backfill have stored.
314	
315	Returning from an ordinary-view `e` live-reloads dev config; returning from a
316	SKILLS/MCP editor reloads only that capability inventory. Changes to scan roots, worktree
317	policy, forge cache settings and `[[tui.tools]]` take effect immediately. A
318	runtime backend change needs a restart because existing callbacks and sessions
319	belong to the backend the TUI opened with; the status line says so rather than
320	pretending to switch underneath a live workspace.
321	
322	## External tools are explicit configuration
323	
324	```bash
325	dev tui tools
326	```
```

```text
570	- **TRY** — dated scratch experiments, including non-Git folders, with durable
571	  tags/notes and explicit active/deprecated/archived/graduated state.
572	- **REMOTE** — repositories visible through authenticated forge CLIs, including
573	  configured Azure DevOps projects, marked when a local repo or Try exists.
574	  What can I open or clone.
575	- **SKILLS** — native project/global agent-skill inventory for the exact startup
576	  checkout plus global sources, with local presence/integrity and an explicitly
577	  checked upstream freshness state. Outside Git it starts as a cross-repository
578	  inventory over accepted REPOS targets; `A` toggles either launch context to all
579	  accepted repositories for this TUI session.
580	- **MCP** — sanitized static MCP declarations for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
581	  Gemini CLI, and OpenCode, scoped to the same startup context by default and
582	  sharing the `A` context/all toggle. It resolves only Claude's documented
583	  project-approval settings; it does not claim connection health or a generally
584	  effective merged runtime configuration.
585	
586	The first view is constructed before runtime auto-detection, project-root lookup,
587	cache decoding, shell-based tool checks, or the optional release refresh can
588	finish. TASKS, REPOS, and TRY then publish independently from one shared local
589	load cycle; REMOTE, FLEET, SKILLS, and MCP remain lazy. A cached REMOTE/FLEET snapshot
590	is immediately usable but is tracked separately from a current live result.
591	Every requested view has its own generation, so `r` cancels the old read, a late
592	result cannot replace a newer one, a failed refresh keeps usable rows visible,
593	and a successful empty result clears obsolete rows. Warning-only SKILLS/MCP
594	source diagnostics keep a fresh partial snapshot, and a visible dependent view
595	resumes automatically after a failed REPOS generation is repaired and reloaded.
596	
597	TASKS, REPOS and TRY use the same services as their non-interactive commands.
598	Git-backed Tries appear in TRY rather than being duplicated in REPOS; REMOTE
599	still knows that local checkout exists. The repo list matters on day one: with
600	forty repositories and no tasks recorded yet, a task-only dashboard would just
601	be empty.
602	
603	Navigation is vim-style, arrows alongside:
604	
605	```
606	j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
607	g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
608	/          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit
609	```
```

50		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-09-04 05:01:07Z)**_

Coverage is asymmetric: `TestEveryDashboardViewBuildsRowActionMenu` verifies token capture for every `Views` entry, but the only revalidation tests execute the task view. Therefore a new view can pass the all-view menu test after updating only the first switch, yet every menu action for that view will be rejected by the second switch as “selected row changed.” I’m checking cursor/filter semantics now to confirm that one shared keyed projection is actually valid for all views and would remove that failure mode.

580	- **MCP** — sanitized static MCP declarations for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
581	  Gemini CLI, and OpenCode, scoped to the same startup context by default and
582	  sharing the `A` context/all toggle. It resolves only Claude's documented
583	  project-approval settings; it does not claim connection health or a generally
584	  effective merged runtime configuration.
585	
586	The first view is constructed before runtime auto-detection, project-root lookup,
587	cache decoding, shell-based tool checks, or the optional release refresh can
588	finish. TASKS, REPOS, and TRY then publish independently from one shared local
589	load cycle; REMOTE, FLEET, SKILLS, and MCP remain lazy. A cached REMOTE/FLEET snapshot
590	is immediately usable but is tracked separately from a current live result.
591	Every requested view has its own generation, so `r` cancels the old read, a late
592	result cannot replace a newer one, a failed refresh keeps usable rows visible,
593	and a successful empty result clears obsolete rows. Warning-only SKILLS/MCP
594	source diagnostics keep a fresh partial snapshot, and a visible dependent view
595	resumes automatically after a failed REPOS generation is repaired and reloaded.
596	
597	TASKS, REPOS and TRY use the same services as their non-interactive commands.
598	Git-backed Tries appear in TRY rather than being duplicated in REPOS; REMOTE
599	still knows that local checkout exists. The repo list matters on day one: with
600	forty repositories and no tasks recorded yet, a task-only dashboard would just
601	be empty.
602	
603	Navigation is vim-style, arrows alongside:
604	
605	```
606	j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
607	g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
608	/          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit
609	```
610	
611	Mouse cell tracking is enabled alongside the keyboard model. Left-click selects a
612	visible row or tab, the wheel moves three rows, and right-click selects a row then
613	opens the same available actions used by keyboard shortcuts. Clicks act on press;
614	release/motion and modified clicks are ignored, and repeated clicks never imply

206	}
207	
208	// NewScanner creates a scanner for explicitly supplied host paths.
209	func NewScanner(options Options) *Scanner {
210		options = normalizeOptions(options)
211		s := &Scanner{options: options}
212		s.readSource = s.readSourceFromDisk
213		return s
214	}

216	// Scan uses documented host defaults.
217	func Scan(ctx context.Context, targets []Target) (Result, error) {
218		return NewScanner(DefaultOptions()).Scan(ctx, targets)
219	}
220	
221	// Scan returns all static declarations it can decode and fixed diagnostics for
222	// individual source failures. Cancellation is the only normal top-level scan
223	// failure and is returned as ctx.Err(), with any rows already collected.
224	func (s *Scanner) Scan(ctx context.Context, targets []Target) (Result, error) {
225		if ctx == nil {
226			ctx = context.Background()
227		}
228		targets = normalizeTargets(targets, s.options.WorkingDirectory)
229		result := Result{
230			Declarations: make([]Declaration, 0),
231			Diagnostics:  make([]Diagnostic, 0),
232			Coverage:     defaultCoverage(),
233		}
234		type cachedRead struct {
235			ready  chan struct{}
236			result readResult
237		}
238		var readMu sync.Mutex
239		reads := map[string]*cachedRead{}
240		readSource := func(ctx context.Context, spec sourceSpec) readResult {
241			key := spec.path + "\x00" + spec.projectRoot
242			readMu.Lock()
243			entry := reads[key]
244			if entry == nil {
245				entry = &cachedRead{ready: make(chan struct{})}
246				reads[key] = entry
247				readMu.Unlock()
248				entry.result = s.readSource(ctx, spec)
249				close(entry.ready)
250				return entry.result
251			}
252			readMu.Unlock()
253			select {
254			case <-ctx.Done():
255				return readResult{}
256			case <-entry.ready:
257				return entry.result
258			}
259		}
260	
261		for _, spec := range s.hostSources() {
262			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
263				finalizeResult(&result)
264				return result, err
265			}
266			rows, diagnostics := s.scanSource(ctx, spec, targets, readSource)
267			result.Declarations = append(result.Declarations, rows...)
268			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, diagnostics...)
269		}
270		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
271			finalizeResult(&result)
272			return result, err
273		}
274	
275		projectResults := make([]Result, len(targets))
276		jobs := make(chan int)
277		workers := s.options.Concurrency
278		if workers > len(targets) {
279			workers = len(targets)
280		}
281		var wg sync.WaitGroup
282		for range workers {
283			wg.Add(1)
284			go func() {
285				defer wg.Done()
286				for {
287					select {
288					case <-ctx.Done():
289						return
290					case index, ok := <-jobs:
291						if !ok {
292							return
293						}
294						for _, spec := range s.projectSources(targets[index]) {
295							if ctx.Err() != nil {
296								return
297							}
298							rows, diagnostics := s.scanSource(ctx, spec, nil, readSource)
299							projectResults[index].Declarations = append(projectResults[index].Declarations, rows...)
300							projectResults[index].Diagnostics = append(projectResults[index].Diagnostics, diagnostics...)
301						}
302					}
303				}
304			}()
305		}
306		for index := range targets {
307			select {
308			case jobs <- index:
309			case <-ctx.Done():
310				close(jobs)
311				wg.Wait()

314					result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, partial.Diagnostics...)
315				}
316				finalizeResult(&result)

261	func FilterDeclarations(rows []Declaration, f Filter) []Declaration {

266			}
267		}

101	## Versioning and changelog
102	
103	The current published baseline is `v0.2.4` (2026-09-01). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
104	
105	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
106	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
107	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
108	
109	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
110	
111	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
112	
113	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
114	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
115	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
116	
117	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
118	
119	For a release:
120	
121	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
122	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
123	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
124	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
125	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. Bubble Tea does invoke `model.Update` and then `model.View` for every accepted mouse message, but terminal writes are separately coalesced to at most 60 FPS and unchanged frames are skipped. The remaining concern is still material: this dashboard’s existing benchmarks show one unchanged-state `View` costs about 0.22–0.73 ms and allocates roughly 247 KB–1.71 MB depending on inventory size, so I’m validating that drag events are neither deduplicated nor dropped before reaching that loop.
