437	func safeDisplayValue(value string) bool {
438		if value == "" || !utf8.ValidString(value) {
439			return false
440		}
441		return !strings.ContainsFunc(value, func(r rune) bool {
442			return unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.In(r, unicode.Cf)
443		})
444	}
445	
446	func uniqueSorted(values []string) []string {
447		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(values))
448		out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
449		for _, value := range values {
450			if value == "" {
451				continue
452			}
453			if _, ok := seen[value]; ok {
454				continue
455			}
456			seen[value] = struct{}{}
457			out = append(out, value)
458		}
459		sort.Strings(out)
460		return out
461	}

466			return ""
467		}
468		return home

56		document := readGlobalLock(globalLockPath())
57		locations := globalScanLocations(definitions)
58		return scanScope(ctx, ScopeGlobal, home, agenttarget.Target{}, locations, document)

61	func projectScanLocations(root string, definitions []AgentDefinition, document lockDocument) []physicalScanLocation {
62		logical := make([]logicalScanLocation, 0, len(definitions))
63		for _, definition := range definitions {
64			if definition.ProjectSkillsDir == "" {
65				continue
66			}
67			logical = append(logical, logicalScanLocation{
68				Path: filepath.Join(root, definition.ProjectSkillsDir), AgentIDs: []string{definition.ID},
69			})
70		}
71		subagents := map[string]bool{}
72		for _, entry := range document.Entries {
73			for _, subagent := range entry.Subagents {
74				if safePathComponent(subagent) {
75					subagents[subagent] = true
76				}
77			}
78		}
79		subagentRoot := filepath.Join(root, "agent", "subagents")
80		if entries, err := os.ReadDir(subagentRoot); err == nil {
81			for _, entry := range entries {
82				if !safePathComponent(entry.Name()) {
83					continue
84				}
85				if info, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(subagentRoot, entry.Name())); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
86					subagents[entry.Name()] = true
87				}
88			}
89		}
90		for subagent := range subagents {
91			logical = append(logical, logicalScanLocation{
92				Path:     filepath.Join(subagentRoot, subagent, "skills"),
93				AgentIDs: []string{"eve"},
94			})
95		}
96		return dedupeScanLocations(logical)
97	}

99	func safePathComponent(value string) bool {
100		return pathx.ValidateComponent(value) == nil && safeDisplayValue(value)
101	}

103	func globalScanLocations(definitions []AgentDefinition) []physicalScanLocation {
104		logical := make([]logicalScanLocation, 0, len(definitions))
105		for _, definition := range definitions {
106			if definition.GlobalSkillsDir == "" {
107				continue
108			}
109			logical = append(logical, logicalScanLocation{
110				Path: definition.GlobalSkillsDir, AgentIDs: []string{definition.ID},
111			})
112		}
113		return dedupeScanLocations(logical)
114	}
115	
116	// dedupeScanLocations first coalesces identical registry paths, then aliases to
117	// the same physical directory. The latter retains every logical path and agent
118	// attribution while ensuring the directory is read only once.
119	func dedupeScanLocations(input []logicalScanLocation) []physicalScanLocation {
120		byLogical := map[string]*logicalScanLocation{}
121		for _, location := range input {
122			path := filepath.Clean(location.Path)
123			current := byLogical[path]
124			if current == nil {
125				copy := logicalScanLocation{Path: path}
126				byLogical[path] = &copy
127				current = &copy
128			}
129			current.AgentIDs = append(current.AgentIDs, location.AgentIDs...)
130		}
131		logicalPaths := make([]string, 0, len(byLogical))
132		for path := range byLogical {
133			logicalPaths = append(logicalPaths, path)
134		}
135		sort.Strings(logicalPaths)
136	
137		byPhysical := map[string]*physicalScanLocation{}
138		for _, path := range logicalPaths {
139			logical := *byLogical[path]
140			logical.AgentIDs = uniqueSorted(logical.AgentIDs)
141			physical := path
142			if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path); err == nil {
143				physical = filepath.Clean(resolved)
144			}
145			group := byPhysical[physical]
146			if group == nil {
147				group = &physicalScanLocation{Path: physical}
148				byPhysical[physical] = group
149			}
150			group.Logical = append(group.Logical, logical)
151		}
152		physicalPaths := make([]string, 0, len(byPhysical))
153		for path := range byPhysical {
154			physicalPaths = append(physicalPaths, path)
155		}
156		sort.Strings(physicalPaths)
157		result := make([]physicalScanLocation, 0, len(physicalPaths))
158		for _, path := range physicalPaths {
159			group := byPhysical[path]
160			sort.Slice(group.Logical, func(i, j int) bool { return group.Logical[i].Path < group.Logical[j].Path })
161			result = append(result, *group)
162		}
163		return result
164	}
165	
166	func scanScope(ctx context.Context, scope Scope, scopeRoot string, target agenttarget.Target, locations []physicalScanLocation, document lockDocument) ([]Skill, []Diagnostic) {
167		diagnostics := decorateDiagnostics(document.Diagnostics, target)
168		var scanned []scannedSkill
169		for _, location := range locations {
170			if ctx.Err() != nil {
171				break
172			}
173			found, foundDiagnostics := scanLocation(ctx, scope, target, location)
174			scanned = append(scanned, found...)
175			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, foundDiagnostics...)
176		}
177	
178		groups := map[string]*skillAggregate{}
179		normalizedInstalled := map[string][]string{}
180		for _, found := range scanned {
181			group := groups[found.Name]
182			if group == nil {
183				group = &skillAggregate{Installations: map[string]*Installation{}}
184				groups[found.Name] = group
185			}
186			group.Names = append(group.Names, found.Name)
187			normalized := normalizedName(found.Name)
188			normalizedInstalled[normalized] = append(normalizedInstalled[normalized], found.Name)
189			physical := found.Installation.RealPath
190			installation := group.Installations[physical]
191			if installation == nil {
192				copy := found.Installation
193				group.Installations[physical] = &copy
194				installation = &copy
195			} else {
196				installation.LogicalPaths = append(installation.LogicalPaths, found.Installation.LogicalPaths...)
197				installation.AgentIDs = append(installation.AgentIDs, found.Installation.AgentIDs...)
198			}
199			installation.LogicalPaths = uniqueSorted(installation.LogicalPaths)
200			installation.AgentIDs = uniqueSorted(installation.AgentIDs)
201			if len(installation.LogicalPaths) > 0 {
202				installation.Path = installation.LogicalPaths[0]
203			}
204			installation.Attribution = registryAttribution(installation.AgentIDs)
205		}
206	
207		for normalized, names := range normalizedInstalled {
208			names = uniqueSorted(names)
209			normalizedInstalled[normalized] = names
210			if len(names) > 1 {
211				diagnostics = append(diagnostics, decorateDiagnostic(Diagnostic{
212					Kind: DiagnosticNameCollision, Scope: scope, Name: normalized,
213					Message: fmt.Sprintf("installed skill names %s normalize to %q", strings.Join(names, ", "), normalized),
214				}, target))
215			}
216		}
217		exactNames := make([]string, 0, len(groups))
218		for name := range groups {
219			exactNames = append(exactNames, name)
220		}
221		sort.Strings(exactNames)
222		consumedLocks := map[string]bool{}
223		rows := make([]Skill, 0, len(groups)+len(document.Entries))
224		for _, name := range exactNames {
225			group := groups[name]
226			normalized := normalizedName(name)
227			var lock LockMetadata
228			candidates := document.candidates(normalized)
229			matched := false
230			if exact, ok := document.Entries[name]; ok {
231				lock, matched = exact, true
232			} else if len(normalizedInstalled[normalized]) == 1 && len(candidates) == 1 {
233				lock, matched = candidates[0], true
234			}
235			if matched {
236				consumedLocks[normalized] = true
237			}
238			rows = append(rows, buildPresentRow(scope, scopeRoot, target, name, group, lock, candidates, matched))
239		}
240	
241		lockGroups := document.namesByNormalized()
242		lockNormalized := make([]string, 0, len(lockGroups))
243		for normalized := range lockGroups {
244			lockNormalized = append(lockNormalized, normalized)
245		}
246		sort.Strings(lockNormalized)
247		for _, normalized := range lockNormalized {
248			if consumedLocks[normalized] {
249				continue
250			}
251			candidates := document.candidates(normalized)
252			if len(candidates) == 0 {
253				continue
254			}
255			selected := candidates[0]
256			rows = append(rows, buildMissingRow(scope, scopeRoot, target, selected, candidates))
257		}
258		return rows, diagnostics
259	}

261	func scanLocation(ctx context.Context, scope Scope, target agenttarget.Target, location physicalScanLocation) ([]scannedSkill, []Diagnostic) {
262		entries, err := os.ReadDir(location.Path)
263		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
264			return nil, nil
265		}
266		if err != nil {
267			return nil, []Diagnostic{decorateDiagnostic(Diagnostic{
268				Kind: DiagnosticSkillUnreadable, Scope: scope, Path: location.Path,
269				Message: fmt.Sprintf("could not read skills directory: %v", err),
270			}, target)}
271		}
272		sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool { return entries[i].Name() < entries[j].Name() })
273	
274		var skills []scannedSkill
275		var diagnostics []Diagnostic
276		for _, entry := range entries {
277			if ctx.Err() != nil {
278				break
279			}
280			child := filepath.Join(location.Path, entry.Name())
281			info, err := os.Stat(child)
282			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
283				continue
284			}
285			if err != nil {
286				diagnostics = append(diagnostics, decorateDiagnostic(Diagnostic{
287					Kind: DiagnosticSkillUnreadable, Scope: scope, Path: child,
288					Message: fmt.Sprintf("could not inspect skill directory: %v", err),
289				}, target))
290				continue
291			}
292			if !info.IsDir() {
293				continue
294			}
295			name, present, err := readSkillName(filepath.Join(child, "SKILL.md"))
296			if !present {
297				continue
298			}
299			if err != nil {
300				diagnostics = append(diagnostics, decorateDiagnostic(Diagnostic{
301					Kind: DiagnosticSkillFrontmatter, Scope: scope,
302					Path: filepath.Join(child, "SKILL.md"), Message: err.Error(),
303				}, target))
304				continue
305			}
306			physical := child
307			if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(child); err == nil {
308				physical = filepath.Clean(resolved)
309			}
310			var logicalPaths, agentIDs []string
311			for _, logical := range location.Logical {
312				logicalPaths = append(logicalPaths, filepath.Join(logical.Path, entry.Name()))
313				agentIDs = append(agentIDs, logical.AgentIDs...)
314			}
315			logicalPaths = uniqueSorted(logicalPaths)
316			agentIDs = uniqueSorted(agentIDs)
317			installation := Installation{
318				RealPath: physical, LogicalPaths: logicalPaths, AgentIDs: agentIDs,
319				Attribution: registryAttribution(agentIDs), Integrity: IntegrityUnknown,
320			}
321			if len(logicalPaths) > 0 {
322				installation.Path = logicalPaths[0]
323			}
324			skills = append(skills, scannedSkill{Name: name, Installation: installation})
325		}
326		return skills, diagnostics
327	}
328	
329	func readSkillName(filename string) (string, bool, error) {
330		file, _, err := safefile.OpenRegular(filename)
331		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
332			return "", false, nil
333		}
334		if errors.Is(err, safefile.ErrNotRegular) {
335			return "", true, errors.New("SKILL.md is not a regular file")
336		}
337		if err != nil {
338			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("could not read SKILL.md: %w", err)
339		}
340		defer file.Close()
341	
342		// Bound only the frontmatter, not the skill body. A valid skill may have a
343		// large reference body, and inventory never needs to read it.
344		reader := bufio.NewReader(io.LimitReader(file, maxFrontmatterBytes+1))
345		first, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
346		consumed := int64(len(first))
347		if readErr != nil && !errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
348			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("could not read SKILL.md: %w", readErr)
349		}
350		first = strings.TrimPrefix(first, string(rune(0xfeff)))
351		if strings.TrimSpace(first) != "---" {
352			return "", true, errors.New("SKILL.md must begin with YAML frontmatter")
353		}
354		var frontmatter strings.Builder
355		closed := false
356		for {
357			line, lineErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
358			consumed += int64(len(line))
359			if consumed > maxFrontmatterBytes {
360				return "", true, fmt.Errorf("SKILL.md frontmatter exceeds %d bytes", maxFrontmatterBytes)
361			}
362			if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "---" {
363				closed = true
364				break
365			}
366			frontmatter.WriteString(line)
367			if lineErr != nil {
368				if errors.Is(lineErr, io.EOF) {
369					break
370				}
371				return "", true, fmt.Errorf("could not read SKILL.md: %w", lineErr)
372			}
373		}
374		if !closed {
375			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("SKILL.md frontmatter is not closed within %d bytes", maxFrontmatterBytes)
376		}
377		var metadata struct {
378			Name        string `yaml:"name"`
379			Description string `yaml:"description"`
380		}
381		if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(frontmatter.String()), &metadata); err != nil {
382			return "", true, fmt.Errorf("invalid SKILL.md YAML frontmatter: %w", err)
383		}
384		metadata.Name = strings.TrimSpace(metadata.Name)
385		metadata.Description = strings.TrimSpace(metadata.Description)
386		if metadata.Name == "" || metadata.Description == "" {
387			return "", true, errors.New("SKILL.md frontmatter requires name and description")
388		}
389		if len(metadata.Name) > 256 || normalizedName(metadata.Name) == "" || !safeDisplayValue(metadata.Name) {
390			return "", true, errors.New("SKILL.md frontmatter name is invalid")
391		}
392		return metadata.Name, true, nil
393	}
394	
395	func buildPresentRow(scope Scope, scopeRoot string, target agenttarget.Target, name string, group *skillAggregate, lock LockMetadata, candidates []LockMetadata, matched bool) Skill {
396		installations := make([]Installation, 0, len(group.Installations))
397		for _, installation := range group.Installations {
398			installation.LogicalPaths = uniqueSorted(installation.LogicalPaths)
399			installation.AgentIDs = uniqueSorted(installation.AgentIDs)
400			installation.Attribution = registryAttribution(installation.AgentIDs)
401			installations = append(installations, *installation)
402		}
403		sort.Slice(installations, func(i, j int) bool {
404			if installations[i].RealPath != installations[j].RealPath {
405				return installations[i].RealPath < installations[j].RealPath
406			}
407			return installations[i].Path < installations[j].Path
408		})
409		var agents []string
410		for _, installation := range installations {
411			agents = append(agents, installation.AgentIDs...)
412		}
413		agentIDs := uniqueSorted(agents)
414		agents = agentDisplayNames(agentIDs)
415		row := Skill{
416			Name: name, Scope: scope, ScopeRoot: scopeRoot,
417			Agents: agents, Repository: target.RepoDisplay, RepositoryPath: target.RepoPath,
418			Checkout: target.CheckoutRoot, Installations: installations, Presence: PresencePresent,
419			Integrity: IntegrityUnknown, Attribution: registryAttribution(agentIDs),
420			RegistryVersion: RegistryVersion, LockCandidates: append([]LockMetadata(nil), candidates...),
421			ManagedBy: ManagedByExternal, UpdateStatus: UpdateUnknown,
422			UpdateDetail: "not tracked by the skills CLI",
423		}
424		if len(installations) > 0 {
425			row.Path = installations[0].Path
426		}
427		if directManagedSkillName(name) {
428			if name == skill.Name {
429				row.ManagedBy = ManagedByDev
430				row.Source = "dev binary"
431				applyBundledIntegrity(&row)
432				row.UpdateStatus, row.UpdateDetail = bundledStatus(row.Integrity, row.IntegrityDetail)
433			} else {
434				row.UpdateDetail = "name is reserved for the binary-managed dev-cli skill"
435			}
436			return row
437		}
438		if matched {
439			copy := lock
440			row.Lock = &copy
441			row.ManagedBy = ManagedBySkills
442			row.UpdateStatus = UpdateUnchecked
443			row.UpdateDetail = ""
444			row.Source, row.SourceURL = sourceDisplay(lock.Source), sourceDisplay(lock.SourceURL)
445			row.SourceType = safeSourceType(lock.SourceType)
446			return row
447		}
448		if len(candidates) > 1 {
449			row.UpdateDetail = "ambiguous normalized lock names; no lock entry selected"
450		}
451		return row
452	}
453	
454	func buildMissingRow(scope Scope, scopeRoot string, target agenttarget.Target, lock LockMetadata, candidates []LockMetadata) Skill {
455		copy := lock
456		row := Skill{
457			Name: lock.Name, Scope: scope, ScopeRoot: scopeRoot, Agents: []string{},
458			Source: sourceDisplay(lock.Source), SourceURL: sourceDisplay(lock.SourceURL),
459			SourceType: safeSourceType(lock.SourceType),
460			ManagedBy:  ManagedBySkills, UpdateStatus: UpdateUnchecked,
461			Repository: target.RepoDisplay, RepositoryPath: target.RepoPath,
462			Checkout: target.CheckoutRoot, Presence: PresenceMissing, Integrity: IntegrityUnknown,
463			Attribution: registryAttribution(nil), RegistryVersion: RegistryVersion,
464			Lock: &copy, LockCandidates: append([]LockMetadata(nil), candidates...),
465		}
466		if directManagedSkillName(lock.Name) {
467			row.Lock = nil
468			if lock.Name == skill.Name {
469				row.ManagedBy = ManagedByDev
470				row.Source, row.SourceURL, row.SourceType = "dev binary", "", ""
471				row.UpdateStatus = UpdateAvailable
472				row.UpdateDetail = "bundled skill is missing; run `dev skill install`"
473			} else {
474				row.ManagedBy = ManagedByExternal
475				row.UpdateStatus = UpdateUnknown
476				row.UpdateDetail = "name is reserved for the binary-managed dev-cli skill"
477			}
478		}
479		return row
480	}
481	
482	func applyBundledIntegrity(row *Skill) {
483		files, err := skill.Files()
484		if err != nil {
485			row.Integrity = IntegrityUnknown
486			row.IntegrityDetail = err.Error()
487			return
488		}
489		row.Integrity = IntegrityVerified
490		row.IntegrityDetail = "all embedded files match this dev binary"
491		for index := range row.Installations {
492			status, detail := bundledIntegrity(row.Installations[index].RealPath, files)
493			row.Installations[index].Integrity = status
494			row.Installations[index].IntegrityDetail = detail
495			if status == IntegrityDrifted {
496				row.Integrity = IntegrityDrifted
497				row.IntegrityDetail = detail
498			} else if status == IntegrityUnknown && row.Integrity != IntegrityDrifted {
499				row.Integrity = IntegrityUnknown
500				row.IntegrityDetail = detail
501			}
502		}
503	}
504	
505	func bundledIntegrity(directory string, files map[string][]byte) (Integrity, string) {
506		for relative, want := range files {
507			got, err := safefile.ReadRegular(context.Background(), filepath.Join(directory, relative), int64(len(want))+1)
508			if err != nil || !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
509				return IntegrityDrifted, "bundled skill differs; run `dev skill install`"
510			}
511		}
512		return IntegrityVerified, "all embedded files match this dev binary"
513	}
514	
515	// bundledStatus preserves the legacy update-status contract while deriving it
516	// from the already-computed aggregate integrity across every installation.
517	func bundledStatus(integrity Integrity, detail string) (UpdateStatus, string) {
518		if integrity == IntegrityVerified {
519			return UpdateCurrent, detail
520		}
521		if integrity == IntegrityDrifted {
522			return UpdateAvailable, detail
523		}
524		return UpdateFailed, detail
525	}
526	
527	func sourceDisplay(value string) string {
528		if value == "" {
529			return ""
530		}
531		if !safeDisplayValue(value) {
532			return "[redacted]"
533		}
534		value = repo.RedactCloneRef(value)
535		parsed, err := url.Parse(value)
536		if err == nil && parsed.Scheme != "" && parsed.Host != "" {
537			parsed.User = nil
538			parsed.RawQuery = ""
539			parsed.ForceQuery = false
540			parsed.Fragment = ""
541			return parsed.String()
542		}
543		return value
544	}
545	
546	func safeSourceType(value string) string {
547		if value == "" || safeDisplayValue(value) {
548			return value
549		}
550		return "[redacted]"
551	}
552	
553	func registryAttribution(agentIDs []string) Attribution {
554		return Attribution{Registry: RegistrySource, RegistryVersion: RegistryVersion, AgentIDs: uniqueSorted(agentIDs)}
555	}
556	
557	func decorateDiagnostics(input []Diagnostic, target agenttarget.Target) []Diagnostic {
558		result := make([]Diagnostic, len(input))
559		for index, diagnostic := range input {
560			result[index] = decorateDiagnostic(diagnostic, target)
561		}
562		return result
563	}
564	
565	func decorateDiagnostic(diagnostic Diagnostic, target agenttarget.Target) Diagnostic {
566		diagnostic.Repository = target.RepoDisplay
567		diagnostic.RepositoryPath = target.RepoPath
568		diagnostic.Checkout = target.CheckoutRoot
569		return diagnostic
570	}

226	// Filter selects declarations for CLI or TUI consumers. Empty fields are
227	// wildcards; Enabled and HasCredentials distinguish an omitted filter from false.
228	type Filter struct {
229		Agent          Agent
230		Scope          Scope
231		Source         DeclarationSource
232		Transport      Transport
233		Repository     string
234		NameContains   string
235		Enabled        *bool
236		HasCredentials *bool
237	}
238	
239	// Match reports whether a declaration satisfies f.
240	func (f Filter) Match(d Declaration) bool {
241		if f.Agent != "" && d.Agent != f.Agent ||
242			f.Scope != "" && d.Scope != f.Scope ||
243			f.Source != "" && d.Source != f.Source ||
244			f.Transport != "" && d.Transport != f.Transport ||
245			f.Repository != "" && d.Repository != f.Repository {
246			return false
247		}
248		if f.NameContains != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(d.Name), strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(f.NameContains))) {
249			return false
250		}
251		if f.Enabled != nil && (d.Enabled == nil || *d.Enabled != *f.Enabled) {
252			return false
253		}
254		if f.HasCredentials != nil && (len(d.Credentials) > 0) != *f.HasCredentials {
255			return false
256		}
257		return true
258	}
259	
260	// FilterDeclarations returns matching rows without changing their order.
261	func FilterDeclarations(rows []Declaration, f Filter) []Declaration {
262		out := make([]Declaration, 0, len(rows))
263		for _, row := range rows {
264			if f.Match(row) {
265				out = append(out, row)
266			}
267		}
268		return out
269	}
270	
271	// SortDeclarations establishes the stable order used by Scan.
272	func SortDeclarations(rows []Declaration) {
273		sort.SliceStable(rows, func(i, j int) bool {
274			a, b := rows[i], rows[j]
275			ak := []string{string(a.Agent), scopeSortKey(a.Scope), strings.ToLower(a.Repository), a.RepositoryPath, a.Checkout, a.LocalProjectPath, a.ConfigPath, string(a.Source), strings.ToLower(a.Plugin), a.Plugin, strings.ToLower(a.Name), a.Name}
276			bk := []string{string(b.Agent), scopeSortKey(b.Scope), strings.ToLower(b.Repository), b.RepositoryPath, b.Checkout, b.LocalProjectPath, b.ConfigPath, string(b.Source), strings.ToLower(b.Plugin), b.Plugin, strings.ToLower(b.Name), b.Name}
277			for n := range ak {
278				if ak[n] != bk[n] {
279					return ak[n] < bk[n]
280				}
281			}
282			return false
283		})
284	}
285	
286	func scopeSortKey(scope Scope) string {
287		switch scope {
288		case ScopeProject:
289			return "0-project"
290		case ScopeLocal:
291			return "1-local"
292		case ScopeUser:
293			return "2-user"
294		case ScopeCustom:
295			return "3-custom"
296		case ScopeSystemDefaults:
297			return "4-system-defaults"
298		case ScopeSystemOverride:
299			return "5-system-override"
300		case ScopeManaged:
301			return "6-managed"
302		default:
303			return "9-" + string(scope)
304		}
305	}
306	
307	func diagnosticMessage(code DiagnosticCode) string {
308		switch code {
309		case DiagnosticUnreadable:
310			return "configuration file could not be read"
311		case DiagnosticTooLarge:
312			return "configuration file exceeds the scan size limit"
313		case DiagnosticNotRegular:
314			return "configuration source is not a regular file"
315		case DiagnosticSymlinkLimit:
316			return "configuration symlink chain exceeds the scan limit"
317		case DiagnosticProjectSymlinkEscape:
318			return "project configuration resolves outside the checkout"
319		case DiagnosticMalformed:
320			return "configuration file could not be decoded"
321		case DiagnosticControlCharacter:
322			return "configuration contains an unsupported control character"
323		case DiagnosticInvalidDeclaration:
324			return "server declaration has an invalid field"
325		case DiagnosticInvalidName:
326			return "server declaration has an invalid name"
327		case DiagnosticUnknownTransport:
328			return "server transport cannot be determined statically"
329		case DiagnosticConflictingTransport:
330			return "server declaration contains conflicting transport fields"
331		case DiagnosticInvalidEndpoint:
332			return "server endpoint could not be represented safely"
333		case DiagnosticInvalidReference:
334			return "credential reference name is invalid"
335		case DiagnosticPluginDefinitionAbsent:
336			return "plugin override does not include the plugin server definition"
337		case DiagnosticTransportPrecedence:
338			return "lower-precedence transport fields were ignored"
339		default:
340			return "configuration could not be fully represented"
341		}
342	}
343	
344	func coverage(code DiagnosticCode) CoverageDiagnostic {
345		return CoverageDiagnostic{Code: code, Message: diagnosticMessage(code)}
346	}

197		projectRoot := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.ProjectRoot)
198		destination, err := pathx.JoinChild(projectRoot, name)
199		if err != nil {
200			return "", fmt.Errorf("remote repository name %q is not a safe clone destination: %w", name, err)
201		}

205	func cloneRemoteFromTUI(ctx context.Context, app *App, row tui.RemoteRow) (string, error) {
206		destination, err := tuiRemoteCloneDestination(app, row.Repo.Name)
207		if err != nil {
208			return "", err
209		}
210		discoverable, err := repositoryPathDiscoverable(app.Cfg, destination)
211		if err != nil {
212			return "", fmt.Errorf("verify REMOTE clone destination %s: %w", config.Contract(destination), err)
213		}
214		if !discoverable {
215			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s is outside paths.scan_roots/repo_paths; add paths.project_root to scan_roots before cloning from REMOTE",
216				config.Contract(destination))
217		}
218		if _, err := os.Lstat(destination); err == nil {
219			return destination, fmt.Errorf("%s already exists; add it to scan_roots/repo_paths or move it before cloning", config.Contract(destination))
220		} else if !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
221			return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect clone destination %s: %w", config.Contract(destination), err)
222		}
223		acquired, err := repo.Acquire(ctx, repo.AcquireRequest{
224			Kind: repo.AcquireClone, Name: row.Repo.Name,
225			CloneRef: row.Repo.CloneURL, Destination: destination,
226		})
227		if err != nil {
228			if _, statErr := os.Lstat(destination); statErr == nil {
229				return destination, fmt.Errorf("%w; inspect the destination now present at %s before retrying", err, config.Contract(destination))
230			}
231			return "", err
232		}
233		return acquired.Path, nil
234	}

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-09-04 05:06:08Z)**_

The scanner semantics confirm the cost scales with the selected scope: SKILLS launches one project scan per deduplicated target plus one global scan, while MCP schedules every target and reads each target’s supported project-source set. A content fingerprint around the one selected path can safely suppress this work when bytes are unchanged; a changed file still requires refresh, and narrower rescanning must account for checkout-wide skill locks and MCP global files that can describe multiple projects.

REFUTED

**Governing rule:** “`tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.” (`/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-mouse-mode-and-more/AGENTS.md:63`) and “Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages” (`AGENTS.md:51`).

**Evidence:**

- The TUI remains filesystem-agnostic: `Actions.ReadFile` is an injected callback for a bounded raw-copy action (`internal/tui/model.go:171-176`), invoked at `internal/tui/model.go:3497-3521`.
- The CLI adapter wires that callback (`internal/cli/tui.go:513-514`) and configures a 1 MiB presentation/clipboard bound (`internal/cli/tui.go:43,759-765`).
- Actual safety mechanics live in generic `safefile`: it rejects non-regular files and performs caller-bounded reads (`internal/safefile/read.go:1-3,18-34,37-75`).
- The bound is explicitly TUI behavior: raw `yf` copies a local source file “up to 1 MiB” to the clipboard (`internal/help/topics/tui.md:293-299`). No equivalent non-TUI raw-file action exists; `dev mcp list` only emits sanitized inventory (`internal/cli/mcp.go:28-88`), and `dev skill list` only emits inventory/table JSON (`internal/cli/skill.go:43-103`).
- `agentmcp.DefaultMaxFileBytes` is separately domain-owned scan/parser policy (`internal/agentmcp/scanner.go:16-23,43-45,151-152,363-367`); skill scanning has different bounds—64 KiB frontmatter and 4 MiB locks (`internal/agentskill/scan.go:25`, `internal/agentskill/lock.go:17,58-70`). Therefore the equal 1 MiB value does not establish a shared cross-frontend policy.

This is reasonable adapter configuration around a generic domain safety API, not duplicated capability-domain policy.

- `/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-mouse-mode-and-more/internal/tui/list_actions.go:518-536` retains only the originating view and editor error; it records neither the selected path nor a pre-edit fingerprint.
- Therefore every successful editor exit reaches `/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-mouse-mode-and-more/internal/tui/model.go:2577-2594` and unconditionally reloads the originating SKILLS or MCP view. The behavior is explicitly asserted by `/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-mouse-mode-and-more/internal/tui/capability_internal_test.go:11-44`.
- Reloading passes the complete cached repository inventory and current scope through `reloadSkills`/`reloadMCP` at `model.go:952-1003`. In explicit all-repositories scope, `/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-mouse-mode-and-more/internal/cli/tui.go:770-785` produces targets for every accepted repository.

115	
116	TRY handles low-cost experiments, reversible archive/restore, marking, and graduation. Archive is organization, not deletion or disk reclamation.

118	REMOTE loads lazily so startup does not wait for the network. Its private XDG
119	cache is decoded after the first view and holds the complete paginated inventory.
120	Fresh rows require no network; stale rows stay searchable while background
121	refresh runs. Oversized/malformed payloads and caches fingerprinted for another
122	configured GH/GL host or Azure target are ignored. GitLab uses explicit

12	// AgentSkillOptions selects native scopes and the explicit remote freshness

14	type AgentSkillOptions struct {
15		Project bool
16		Global  bool
17		Check   bool
18		Limiter *Limiter
19	}
20	
21	// CollectAgentSkills scans each repository target through the shared local
22	// process limiter, scans global paths once, and only then groups remote source
23	// checks across the complete result.
24	func CollectAgentSkills(ctx context.Context, targets []agenttarget.Target, options AgentSkillOptions) (agentskill.Result, error) {
25		if ctx == nil {
26			ctx = context.Background()
27		}
28		project, global := options.Project, options.Global
29		if !project && !global {
30			project, global = true, true
31		}
32		targets = agenttarget.Dedupe(targets)
33		partCount := 0
34		if project {
35			partCount += len(targets)
36		}
37		globalIndex := -1
38		if global {
39			globalIndex = partCount
40			partCount++
41		}
42		parts := make([]agentskill.Result, partCount)
43		errs := make([]error, partCount)
44		limiter := options.Limiter
45		if limiter == nil {
46			limiter = NewLimiter(8)
47		}
48	
49		var wait sync.WaitGroup
50		launch := func(index int, scan func() (agentskill.Result, error)) {
51			wait.Go(func() {
52				release, ok := limiter.Acquire(ctx)
53				if !ok {
54					errs[index] = ctx.Err()
55					return
56				}
57				defer release()
58				parts[index], errs[index] = scan()
59			})
60		}
61		if project {
62			for index, target := range targets {
63				target := target
64				launch(index, func() (agentskill.Result, error) {
65					return agentskill.Scan(ctx, []agenttarget.Target{target}, agentskill.ListOptions{Project: true})
66				})
67			}
68		}
69		if global {
70			launch(globalIndex, func() (agentskill.Result, error) {
71				return agentskill.Scan(ctx, nil, agentskill.ListOptions{Global: true})
72			})
73		}
74		wait.Wait()
75	
76		result := agentskill.MergeResults(parts...)
77		if options.Check && ctx.Err() == nil {
78			result.Skills = agentskill.CheckUpdates(ctx, result.Skills)
79		}
80		joined := errors.Join(errs...)
81		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
82			joined = errors.Join(joined, ctxErr)
83		}
84		return result, joined
85	}

219	func Scan(ctx context.Context, targets []agenttarget.Target, options ListOptions) (Result, error) {
220		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
221			return Result{}, err

223		project, global := options.Project, options.Global

260		return result, nil
261	}

14	func fleetEditorCommand(editor, path string) (*exec.Cmd, error) {
15		arguments, err := windows.DecomposeCommandLine(editor)
16		if err != nil {
17			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse Windows editor command: %w", err)
18		}
19		if len(arguments) == 0 || arguments[0] == "" {
20			return nil, errors.New("Windows editor command is empty")
21		}
22		return exec.Command(arguments[0], append(arguments[1:], path)...), nil
23	}

25	// replaceProcessWithShell starts an interactive shell in the current working
26	// directory. Windows has no exec(2), so dev runs the shell as a child that
27	// inherits the console and then exits with the shell's status when it returns.
28	func replaceProcessWithShell() error {
29		shell := os.Getenv("COMSPEC")
30		if shell == "" {
31			shell = "cmd.exe"
32		}
33		cmd := exec.Command(shell)
34		cmd.Stdin, cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = os.Stdin, os.Stdout, os.Stderr
35		err := cmd.Run()
36		var exit *exec.ExitError
37		if errors.As(err, &exit) {
38			os.Exit(exit.ExitCode())
39		}
40		if err != nil {
41			return err
42		}
43		os.Exit(0)
44		return nil
45	}

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Evaluating copy command synchronization**

I'm considering how commands might race when copying. If the first copy is slow, the second might trigger afterward, causing side effects. We could make the copy happen synchronously during updates, but that could create bad blocks. Another option is to use a shared mutex and a generation check in the command before writing, using an atomic request pointer.  

The model could include a `copyGate` as a shared pointer, with an atomic generation created in the New function. It’s worth reconsidering the value semantics principle.
</details></think>

`medium effort → 3+5 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify → ≤8 findings`

You are reviewing for **precision** at medium effort: every finding you surface
should be one a maintainer would act on.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`. If the Agent tool is not available in your current tool set, do not error — perform each angle (and each verification) yourself, sequentially, in this context.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, 3-state)

Dedup candidates that point at the same line/mechanism, keeping the one with
the most concrete failure scenario. For each remaining candidate, run **one
verifier** via the Agent tool: give it the diff, the relevant
file(s), and the candidate, and have it return exactly one of:

- **CONFIRMED** — can name the inputs/state that trigger it and the wrong
  output or crash. Quote the line.
- **PLAUSIBLE** — mechanism is real, trigger is uncertain (timing, env,
  config). State what would confirm it.
- **REFUTED** — factually wrong (code doesn't say that) or guarded elsewhere.
  Quote the line that proves it.

Keep candidates where the vote is CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 8 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 8 survive, keep the 8 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	`AGENTS.md` is the canonical repository guidance file. `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to it; edit this file rather than replacing the symlink.
6	
7	## Toolchain and commands
8	
9	- Go 1.26.4 (from `go.mod`) builds the CLI. Python 3.11+ and `uv` are used only for the documentation site.
10	- `make` / `make all` runs `fmt -> vet -> test -> build`. `make fmt` runs `gofmt -w .` and therefore modifies files.
11	- There is no working `make lint` recipe even though `lint` appears in `.PHONY`. The repository's static gates are formatting and `go vet`.
12	
13	```bash
14	make build                         # build ./dev with git-derived version metadata
15	make test                          # go test ./...
16	go test -race ./...                # CI test command
17	go test ./internal/gitx -run '^TestAddWorktreeUsesExplicitBase$'  # one test
18	go test ./internal/cli -run '^TestName/Subtest$'                  # one subtest
19	make vet                           # go vet ./...
20	files="$(gofmt -l .)" && test -z "$files"  # format check that preserves gofmt failures
21	make e2e                           # real CLI lifecycle in an isolated temporary HOME
22	make skill-sync                    # regenerate command docs, then rebuild embedded skill
23	make skill-check                   # fail when command tree and generated skill reference drift
24	make install                       # binary under PREFIX; skill in user agent directories
25	```
26	
27	Documentation uses the same sequence as CI:
28	
29	```bash
30	uv sync --frozen --extra docs
31	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source
32	uv run mkdocs build --strict
33	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --site site
34	```
35	
36	If generated `docs/llms*.txt` files drift, regenerate them with `uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source --generate-llms` and then rerun the documentation checks.
37	
38	## Architecture
39	
40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:
41	
42	```text
43	cmd/dev/main.go
44	  -> cli.Execute()
45	  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
46	  -> App.Load()
47	  -> Cobra command handler
48	  -> domain package(s)
49	```
50	
51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:
52	
53	- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints. Lifecycle callers use exact-record revisions and locked compare-and-update/delete transactions rather than treating a previously read task as current.
56	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
57	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
58	- `taskflow` is the UI-agnostic lifecycle authority: it separates recorded intent, typed live observations, immutable guarded plans, approvals, and partial result ledgers. Apply locks and reloads task/Git/worktree/runtime/artifact/remote identity, then rejects stale authority before mutation.
59	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, all registered worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and UI projections consume this joined view.
60	- `flowtui` is an independent Bubble Tea model for the preview `dev flow` repository state-machine UI. It receives repository reads and taskflow Plan/Apply callbacks; do not embed it in or add a mode to the dashboard's `tui` model.
61	- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
62	- `note` stores multiple repository thoughts as durable Markdown keyed by catalog ID and maintains a rebuildable SQLite FTS index. It is distinct from task context and the catalog's single metadata summary.
63	- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.
64	- `stats` is durable SQLite data; `diskusage`, note FTS, and forge/gitignore data are regenerable caches. Do not treat stats as cache.
65	- `forge` wraps optional `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI integrations and must degrade to local Git behavior when they are unavailable.
66	- `sshhost` owns bounded static discovery of the active user OpenSSH Include closure, canonical files under `~/.ssh/dev.d`, public-key selection/generation/bootstrap, fresh authentication proofs, and the explicit handoff into dev fleet. OpenSSH and plain `ssh -G` remain semantic authority; dev reads foreign host definitions but never rewrites them, copies private keys, weakens host-key policy, or treats every alias as a fleet member.
67	- `fleet` merges the user-authored primary `remotes.toml` with strict dev-owned `remotes.d/ssh-<alias>.toml` registrations. Remote `dev` state remains host-local. `remote_os` selects target semantics: POSIX uses the shell launcher, while Windows uses an encoded PowerShell launcher that accepts only hidden fleet helpers, preserves sync stdin, and never applies controller path rules to remote paths.
68	
69	The principal task start flow spans `internal/cli/start.go`, `start_flow.go`, `gitx`/`wt`, `runtime`, and `task`: resolve the canonical repository and explicit base, create or select the checkout, provision/open it, then persist and annotate the task. Task-backed park/resume/completion/retirement and exact unmanaged Adopt/Remove policy belong in `taskflow`; CLI commands, the dashboard, `sweep`, and `flowtui` are adapters. Preserve report-before-apply and no-data-loss ordering, including the isolated compatibility paths that have not migrated to taskflow.
70	
71	State is split intentionally:
72	
73	- Git remotes/branches are durable code truth.
74	- Worktrees are disposable local checkouts.
75	- Runtime sessions are per-host and re-derivable.
76	- Task TOML and catalog assets hold only intent/identity that Git cannot answer.
77	- Repository quick-note Markdown is durable sidecar data; `notes.db` is only its disposable search index.
78	- `stats.db` is durable observation data; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/*` is disposable.
79	- The user's OpenSSH configuration is durable connection truth. Dev owns only its exact top-level `Include ~/.ssh/dev.d/*.conf` and structurally valid fragments in `~/.ssh/dev.d`; key bootstrap sends public material only and has no private-key transfer or remote-key revocation lifecycle.
80	- Fleet intent is the merged primary `remotes.toml` plus generated sibling `remotes.d` fragments. A generated fragment exists only after explicit `dev ssh setup --fleet` and a fresh ordinary alias login; controller caches and each remote machine's paths/tasks/runtime remain re-derivable or host-local.
81	
82	## Behavioral contracts
83	
84	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
85	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
86	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
87	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
88	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
89	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
90	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
91	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
92	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
93	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
94	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
95	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
96	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output.
97	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
98	- SSH initialization is report-before-apply; managed host changes are confined to canonical dev-owned fragments. Full bootstrap requires an explicit existing key or explicit generation, registers fleet only behind `--fleet`, and reports interrupted remote installation as unknown rather than pretending to roll it back.
99	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.
100	
101	## Versioning and changelog
102	
103	The current published baseline is `v0.2.4` (2026-09-01). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
104	
105	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
106	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
107	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
108	
109	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
110	
111	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
112	
113	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
114	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
115	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
116	
117	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
118	
119	For a release:
120	
121	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
122	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
123	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
124	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
125	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
126	
127	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
128	
129	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
130	
131	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
132	
133	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
134	
135	| Change | Required synchronization |
136	|---|---|
137	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
138	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
139	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
140	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
141	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
142	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
143	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
144	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
145	
146	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
147	
148	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
149

+package tui

+func skillFilePath(row agentskill.Skill) (string, error) {
+	if row.Presence != agentskill.PresenceMissing && strings.TrimSpace(row.Path) != "" {
+		return filepath.Join(row.Path, "SKILL.md"), nil
+	}
+	if row.Lock != nil && strings.TrimSpace(row.Lock.File) != "" {
+		return row.Lock.File, nil
+	}
+	return "", fmt.Errorf("skill %s has no local skill or lock file", row.Name)
+}
+
+func (m Model) capabilityFilePath() (string, error) {
+	if row, ok := m.currentSkill(); ok {
+		return skillFilePath(row)
+	}
+	if row, ok := m.currentMCP(); ok {
+		if strings.TrimSpace(row.ConfigPath) == "" {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("MCP server %s has no local config path", row.Name)
+		}
+		return row.ConfigPath, nil
+	}
+	return "", fmt.Errorf("the selected row has no capability config file")
+}
+
+func formatSkillSummary(row agentskill.Skill) string {
+	lines := []string{
+		"name: " + row.Name,
+		"scope: " + string(row.Scope),
+	}
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "repository", row.Repository)
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "checkout", row.Checkout)
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "path", row.Path)
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "agents", strings.Join(row.Agents, ", "))
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "managed", string(row.ManagedBy))
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "presence", string(row.Presence))
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "integrity", string(row.Integrity))
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source", row.Source)

+func prepareTUICapabilityEdit(path string) (tui.CapabilityEdit, error) {
+	logical := filepath.Clean(path)
+	resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(logical)
+	if err != nil {
+		return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve capability file %s: %w", config.Contract(logical), err)
+	}
+	source, observed, err := safefile.OpenRegular(resolved)
+	if err != nil {
+		return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, fmt.Errorf("open capability file %s: %w", config.Contract(logical), err)
+	}
+	original, readErr := safefile.ReadAll(context.Background(), source, safefile.CompiledMaxFileBytes)
+	closeErr := source.Close()
+	if readErr != nil {
+		return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, fmt.Errorf("read capability file %s: %w", config.Contract(logical), readErr)
+	}
+	if closeErr != nil {
+		return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, fmt.Errorf("close capability file %s: %w", config.Contract(logical), closeErr)
+	}
+
+	working, err := os.CreateTemp("", "dev-capability-edit-*")
+	if err != nil {
+		return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
+	}
+	workingPath := working.Name()
+	cleanup := true
+	defer func() {
+		if cleanup {
+			_ = os.Remove(workingPath)
+		}
+	}()
+	if _, err := working.Write(original); err != nil {
+		_ = working.Close()
+		return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
+	}
+	if err := working.Sync(); err != nil {
+		_ = working.Close()
+		return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
+	}
+	if err := working.Close(); err != nil {
+		return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
+	}
+	process, _, err := editorProcess(workingPath, "")
+	if err != nil {
+		return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
+	}
+	cleanup = false
+
+	return tui.CapabilityEdit{
+		Command: process,
+		Complete: func(runErr error) error {
+			if runErr != nil {
+				_ = os.Remove(workingPath)
+				return runErr
+			}
+			edited, err := safefile.ReadRegular(context.Background(), workingPath, safefile.CompiledMaxFileBytes)
+			if err != nil {
+				return fmt.Errorf("read edited capability file; working copy preserved at %s: %w", config.Contract(workingPath), err)
+			}
+			if bytes.Equal(edited, original) {
+				return os.Remove(workingPath)
+			}
+			root, err := os.OpenRoot(filepath.Dir(resolved))
+			if err != nil {
+				return fmt.Errorf("open capability file directory; working copy preserved at %s: %w", config.Contract(workingPath), err)
+			}
+			defer root.Close()
+			if _, err := safefile.AtomicReplace(
+				context.Background(), root, filepath.Base(resolved), observed, edited, observed.Mode().Perm(),
+			); err != nil {
+				return fmt.Errorf("replace changed capability file; working copy preserved at %s: %w", config.Contract(workingPath), err)
+			}
+			return os.Remove(workingPath)
+		},
+	}, nil
+}

12	func skillFilePath(row agentskill.Skill) (string, error) {
13		if row.Presence != agentskill.PresenceMissing && strings.TrimSpace(row.Path) != "" {
14			return filepath.Join(row.Path, "SKILL.md"), nil
15		}
16		if row.Lock != nil && strings.TrimSpace(row.Lock.File) != "" {
17			return row.Lock.File, nil
18		}
19		return "", fmt.Errorf("skill %s has no local skill or lock file", row.Name)
20	}
21	
22	func (m Model) capabilityFilePath() (string, error) {
23		if row, ok := m.currentSkill(); ok {
24			return skillFilePath(row)
25		}
26		if row, ok := m.currentMCP(); ok {
27			if strings.TrimSpace(row.ConfigPath) == "" {
28				return "", fmt.Errorf("MCP server %s has no local config path", row.Name)
29			}
30			return row.ConfigPath, nil
31		}
32		return "", fmt.Errorf("the selected row has no capability config file")
33	}
34	
35	func formatSkillSummary(row agentskill.Skill) string {
36		lines := []string{
37			"name: " + row.Name,
38			"scope: " + string(row.Scope),
39		}
40		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "repository", row.Repository)
41		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "checkout", row.Checkout)
42		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "path", row.Path)
43		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "agents", strings.Join(row.Agents, ", "))
44		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "managed", string(row.ManagedBy))
45		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "presence", string(row.Presence))
46		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "integrity", string(row.Integrity))
47		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source", row.Source)
48		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source_url", row.SourceURL)
49		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "update", string(row.UpdateStatus))
50		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
51	}
52	
53	func formatMCPSummary(row agentmcp.Declaration) string {
54		lines := []string{
55			"server: " + row.Name,
56			"agent: " + string(row.Agent),
57			"scope: " + string(row.Scope),
58		}
59		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "repository", row.Repository)
60		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "checkout", row.Checkout)
61		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "config", row.ConfigPath)
62		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source", mcpSource(row))
63		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "state", mcpDeclarationState(row))
64		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "transport", string(row.Transport))
65		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "endpoint", row.Endpoint)
66		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "command", row.Command)
67		if row.ArgumentCount > 0 {
68			lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("arguments: %d value(s) redacted", row.ArgumentCount))
69		}
70		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "policies", mcpPolicySummary(row))
71		if len(row.Credentials) > 0 {
72			credentials := make([]string, 0, len(row.Credentials))
73			for _, credential := range row.Credentials {
74				value := string(credential.Kind)
75				if credential.Name != "" {
76					value += ":" + credential.Name
77				}
78				credentials = append(credentials, value)
79			}
80			lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "credentials", strings.Join(credentials, ", "))
81		}
82		if len(row.Redactions) > 0 {
83			redactions := make([]string, len(row.Redactions))
84			for i, redaction := range row.Redactions {
85				redactions[i] = string(redaction)
86			}
87			lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "redacted", strings.Join(redactions, ", "))
88		}
89		if len(row.Coverage) > 0 {
90			coverage := make([]string, len(row.Coverage))
91			for i, item := range row.Coverage {
92				coverage[i] = string(item.Code)
93			}
94			lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "coverage", strings.Join(coverage, ", "))
95		}
96		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
97	}
98	
99	func (m Model) copyBindingHelp() string {
100		if m.view == ViewRepos {
101			return "y context · p path · b branch · s sessions · w worktree paths"
102		}
103		parts := make([]string, 0, 4)
104		if _, err := m.capabilityFilePath(); err == nil {
105			parts = append(parts, "p file path")
106		}
107		parts = append(parts, "s safe summary")
108		if row, ok := m.currentSkill(); ok && row.SourceURL != "" {
109			parts = append(parts, "u source URL")
110		}
111		if _, err := m.capabilityFilePath(); err == nil && m.actions.ReadFile != nil {
112			parts = append(parts, "f raw file")
113		}
114		return strings.Join(parts, " · ")
115	}
116	
117	func appendSummaryLine(lines []string, label, value string) []string {
118		if strings.TrimSpace(value) == "" {
119			return lines
120		}
121		return append(lines, label+": "+value)
122	}

375		if m.overlay.optionCount == 0 || m.overlay.optionIndex >= m.overlay.optionCount {
376			return m, nil
377		}
378		action := m.overlay.options[m.overlay.optionIndex]
379		token := m.overlay.selection

381			m.overlay = overlayState{}
382			m.err = fmt.Errorf("selected row changed while its action menu was open")

384		}

5	const mouseWheelRows = 3

7	// mouseFrameFits fails closed when Bubble Tea would drop top lines from an
8	// over-height frame. Screen-relative mouse coordinates cannot safely target
9	// logical header/list rows once that clipping occurs.
10	func (m Model) mouseFrameFits() bool {
11		if m.height <= 0 {
12			return false
13		}
14		if m.overlay.kind == overlayActionMenu {
15			return lineCount(m.renderOverlay()) <= m.height
16		}
17	
18		n := m.count()
19		listLines := m.listPreambleLines()
20		if n > 0 {
21			visible := min(n, m.listHeight())
22			listLines += visible
23			if visible < n {
24				listLines++
25			}
26		}
27		total := 2 + listLines + 1 + lineCount(m.renderDetail()) + 1 + lineCount(m.renderFooter())
28		return total <= m.height
29	}

31	func (m Model) updateMouse(message tea.MouseMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
32		event := tea.MouseEvent(message)
33		if event.Shift || event.Alt || event.Ctrl {
34			return m, nil
35		}
36		if m.overlay.kind == overlayActionMenu {
37			if !m.mouseFrameFits() {
38				return m, nil
39			}
40			return m.updateActionMenuMouse(event)
41		}
42		if m.noteMode() || m.overlay.kind != overlayNone || m.mode != modeList {
43			return m, nil
44		}
45		if !m.mouseFrameFits() {
46			return m, nil
47		}
48	
49		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
50			if !m.mouseOverList(event.X, event.Y) {
51				return m, nil
52			}
53			delta := mouseWheelRows
54			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
55				delta = -delta
56			}
57			m.setAt(m.at() + delta)
58			return m, nil
59		}
60		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress {
61			return m, nil
62		}
63	
64		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonLeft && event.Y == 0 {
65			for _, hit := range m.buildHeaderLayout().tabs {
66				if event.X < hit.from || event.X >= hit.to {
67					continue
68				}
69				if m.view == hit.view {
70					return m, nil
71				}
72				m.view = hit.view
73				return m.afterViewSwitch()
74			}
75			return m, nil
76		}
77	
78		row, ok := m.mouseRow(event.X, event.Y)
79		if !ok {
80			return m, nil
81		}
82		switch event.Button {
83		case tea.MouseButtonLeft:
84			m.setAt(row)
85		case tea.MouseButtonRight:
86			m.setAt(row)
87			if !m.remoteClone.active() {
88				m = m.openActionMenu()
89			}
90		}
91		return m, nil
92	}

94	func (m Model) mouseRow(x, y int) (int, bool) {
95		if x < 0 || x >= m.width {
96			return 0, false
97		}
98		count := m.count()
99		from, to := m.window(count)
100		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
101		if y < first || y >= first+(to-from) {
102			return 0, false
103		}
104		return from + y - first, true
105	}
106	
107	func (m Model) mouseOverList(x, y int) bool {
108		if x < 0 || x >= m.width || m.count() == 0 {
109			return false
110		}
111		from, to := m.window(m.count())
112		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
113		return y >= 2 && y < first+(to-from)
114	}

116	func (m Model) updateActionMenuMouse(event tea.MouseEvent) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
117		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
118			if m.overlay.optionCount == 0 {
119				return m, nil
120			}
121			delta := 1
122			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
123				delta = -1
124			}
125			m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + delta + m.overlay.optionCount) % m.overlay.optionCount
126			return m, nil
127		}

+package tui
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/agentmcp"
+	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/agentskill"
+)
+
+func skillFilePath(row agentskill.Skill) (string, error) {
+	if row.Presence != agentskill.PresenceMissing && strings.TrimSpace(row.Path) != "" {
+		return filepath.Join(row.Path, "SKILL.md"), nil
+	}
+	if row.Lock != nil && strings.TrimSpace(row.Lock.File) != "" {
+		return row.Lock.File, nil
+	}
+	return "", fmt.Errorf("skill %s has no local skill or lock file", row.Name)
+}
+
+func (m Model) capabilityFilePath() (string, error) {
+	if row, ok := m.currentSkill(); ok {
+		return skillFilePath(row)
+	}
+	if row, ok := m.currentMCP(); ok {
+		if strings.TrimSpace(row.ConfigPath) == "" {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("MCP server %s has no local config path", row.Name)
+		}
+		return row.ConfigPath, nil
+	}
+	return "", fmt.Errorf("the selected row has no capability config file")
+}
+
+func formatSkillSummary(row agentskill.Skill) string {
+	lines := []string{
+		"name: " + row.Name,
+		"scope: " + string(row.Scope),
+	}
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "repository", row.Repository)
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "checkout", row.Checkout)
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "path", row.Path)
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "agents", strings.Join(row.Agents, ", "))
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "managed", string(row.ManagedBy))
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "presence", string(row.Presence))
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "integrity", string(row.Integrity))
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source", row.Source)
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source_url", row.SourceURL)
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "update", string(row.UpdateStatus))
+	return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
+}
+
+func formatMCPSummary(row agentmcp.Declaration) string {
+	lines := []string{
+		"server: " + row.Name,
+		"agent: " + string(row.Agent),
+		"scope: " + string(row.Scope),
+	}
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "repository", row.Repository)
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "checkout", row.Checkout)
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "config", row.ConfigPath)
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source", mcpSource(row))
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "state", mcpDeclarationState(row))
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "transport", string(row.Transport))
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "endpoint", row.Endpoint)
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "command", row.Command)
+	if row.ArgumentCount > 0 {
+		lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("arguments: %d value(s) redacted", row.ArgumentCount))
+	}
+	lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "policies", mcpPolicySummary(row))
+	if len(row.Credentials) > 0 {
+		credentials := make([]string, 0, len(row.Credentials))
+		for _, credential := range row.Credentials {
+			value := string(credential.Kind)
+			if credential.Name != "" {
+				value += ":" + credential.Name
+			}
+			credentials = append(credentials, value)
+		}
+		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "credentials", strings.Join(credentials, ", "))
+	}
+	if len(row.Redactions) > 0 {
+		redactions := make([]string, len(row.Redactions))
+		for i, redaction := range row.Redactions {
+			redactions[i] = string(redaction)
+		}
+		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "redacted", strings.Join(redactions, ", "))
+	}
+	if len(row.Coverage) > 0 {
+		coverage := make([]string, len(row.Coverage))
+		for i, item := range row.Coverage {
+			coverage[i] = string(item.Code)
+		}
+		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "coverage", strings.Join(coverage, ", "))
+	}
+	return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
+}
+
+func (m Model) copyBindingHelp() string {
+	if m.view == ViewRepos {
+		return "y context · p path · b branch · s sessions · w worktree paths"
+	}
+	parts := make([]string, 0, 4)
+	if _, err := m.capabilityFilePath(); err == nil {
+		parts = append(parts, "p file path")
+	}
+	parts = append(parts, "s safe summary")
+	if row, ok := m.currentSkill(); ok && row.SourceURL != "" {
+		parts = append(parts, "u source URL")
+	}
+	if _, err := m.capabilityFilePath(); err == nil && m.actions.ReadFile != nil {
+		parts = append(parts, "f raw file")
+	}
+	return strings.Join(parts, " · ")
+}
+
+func appendSummaryLine(lines []string, label, value string) []string {
+	if strings.TrimSpace(value) == "" {
+		return lines
+	}
+	return append(lines, label+": "+value)
+}
