6	# dev-cli
7	
8	The `dev` command is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent
9	runtimes. It exists to stop four different things collapsing into one:
10	
11	```
12	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
13	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
14	herdr / tmux / zellij
15	                a per-host live runtime
16	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
17	```
18	
19	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
20	human/task facts such as identity, checkout mode, **state**, **owner** and **next
21	action** in one TOML file per task under configured `paths.state_dir/tasks`
22	(default `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks`); transient pane data is not persisted.
23	Machine connection intent has separate owners: OpenSSH remains authoritative,
24	while dev owns only canonical `~/.ssh/dev.d` fragments and explicit generated
25	fleet registrations beside user-authored `remotes.toml`.
26	
27	**The problem it solves:** when a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only
28	record of what you are working on, nothing can ever be closed. `dev` gives that
29	record a home outside the runtime, so closing a session stops meaning
30	abandoning a task.
31	
32	## Check it is there first
33	
34	`dev` is not installed everywhere. Before using it:
35	
36	```bash
37	command -v dev || echo "not installed"
38	dev doctor          # version/install owner/path, PATH collisions, and capabilities
39	```
40	
41	Only **git** is required. System `ssh` enables SSH evaluation/probing/bootstrap
42	and fleet transport; `ssh-keygen` enables key derivation/generation; Windows
43	OpenSSH targets need PowerShell. `herdr`, `tmux`, `zellij`, `gh`, `glab` and
44	Azure CLI enable other capabilities and degrade cleanly when absent — never make
45	a step hard-depend on one unless the requested operation crosses that boundary.
46	
47	## Worktree ownership — read this before creating any worktree
48	
49	There are three mechanisms that create git worktrees, and picking the wrong one
50	is the most common source of confusion. The rule:
51	
52	| Kind of worktree | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
53	|---|---|---|---|
54	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff — anything you might return to | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path`, default `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>` | until external `dev retire` |
55	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation (`isolation: worktree`, `/batch`, `EnterWorktree`) | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (keep gitignored) | owned by that harness; not a transcript-relocation guarantee |
56	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add` itself, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
57	
58	**Rule of thumb: if code/history/plan must remain reviewable or a human may
59	return tomorrow, use `dev`. Use native isolation only when the harness owns the
60	entire turn-scoped lifecycle.**
61	
62	Why `dev` does not delegate to `herdr worktree create`: the path policy has to
63	hold on machines where herdr is not installed. `dev` creates the checkout with
64	plain git and asks herdr only to *open* it — which still makes it appear in the
65	sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
66	
67	Never nest a `dev` worktree inside a repository. A checkout inside another
68	checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second copy of
69	the tree. `dev` refuses to do it.
70	
71	Full detail: `references/worktree-ownership.md`.
72	
73	## The task lifecycle
74	
75	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
76	|---|---|---|---|
77	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
78	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | normally closed | back within days |
79	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
80	| ✅ `done` | merged | may remain open | MERGED; external retirement pending |
81	
82	```bash
83	dev repo open api                                  # ad hoc; no task/worktree
84	dev start api --task "typo" --direct                # track current/main directly
85	dev start api --task "small" --branch-only --base main
86	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # isolated worktree → hot
87	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
88	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
89	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
90	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid>                # arm final transcript handoff
91	dev done                                           # TTY wizard: inspect dirty state, then FF/PR/merged
92	dev done --ff                                      # → done/MERGED; resources kept
93	dev retire "token refresh"                         # external-only cleanup → RETIRED
94	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --json              # strict V1 report only
95	```

97	For stale Claude Workflow isolation, run `dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees` only
98	from the canonical non-bare checkout. The bounded metadata adapter never emits
99	prompt/script/log/result/transcript content. A candidate must have one exact
100	mapping, terminal workflow, done agent, journal start/result, no same-ID resume,
101	sufficient provider inactivity, clean Git including no ignored or recursive
102	submodule content, no task/unsafe artifact/runtime/caller claim, and unchanged

105	2.1.259 does not expose that non-replayable Git identity, so current Claude claims

107	is TTY-only, rejects bypass
108	flags, confirms each item, and revalidates the fingerprint under a common-dir
109	lock before non-force removal. It never prunes, closes runtimes, changes Claude
110	metadata, or repairs dirty work. Branches are retained unless separately safe
111	`--delete-branches --base <ref>` was requested.
112	
113	**Parking is the move that matters.** `dev park --next "…"` is what makes it
114	safe to close a session, and the `--next` text is what makes resuming cheap.
115	Always suggest a `--next` when parking.

120	### Repository flow preview
121	
122	`dev flow [repo]` is a preview-labelled, full-screen, TTY-only repository
123	state-machine UI independent of the six-view dashboard. From any canonical or
124	linked checkout it opens the canonical repository and focuses that exact
125	surface; outside Git it opens a picker. It lists every registered worktree plus
126	task-only records, including COLD/DONE tasks without a checkout.
127	
128	Rows are `canonical`, `managed`, `unmanaged`, `harness`, `task-only`, or
129	`conflict`. Managed bindings receive legal mode/state lifecycle actions.
130	Eligible unmanaged linked rows receive metadata-only Adopt and clean, non-force,
131	branch-preserving Remove Checkout. Canonical checkout removal, harness cleanup,
132	and destructive conflict resolution fail closed.
133	
134	Enter always builds a plan first. The plan separates persisted HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE
135	intent from live facts, shows conditions/remediation/effects/retained resources/
136	fallback, and applies only after `y` or its displayed typed token. Apply locks and
137	revalidates the task revision plus exact repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact
138	identity; partial effects remain in a result ledger with recovery.
139	
140	`r` reloads local facts without network access. `R` offers explicit fetch,
141	review query, or both; review evidence is run-local and only portable existence,
142	state, draft, URL, provider, and observation time—not decisions or checks.
143	Runtime `none` leaves occupancy unobserved without invalidating otherwise fresh
144	local Git/task facts. The preview omits dirty commit/discard, WIP, shared-writer,
145	takeover, and unknown-runtime overrides; use the displayed CLI fallback when an
146	expert compatibility flag is actually required.

148	## Pick the task's checkout mode
149	
150	A task does not imply a worktree. Use the lightest explicit boundary:
151	
152	- `dev repo open <repo>` / REPOS Enter — ad-hoc open, no task at all.
153	- `dev start … --direct` / REPOS `d` — track current branch (usually main),
154	  create no branch/worktree. HOT ↔ WARM only; `dev done` needs no merge mode.
155	- `dev start … --branch-only` — create and switch a branch in the canonical
156	  checkout. No concurrent branch there.
157	- `dev start …` / REPOS `s` — default isolated branch + worktree. Use once work
158	  may be interrupted, experimental, or parallel.
159	
160	Do not create isolation before it has a job, but do not carry dirty main changes
161	into a parallel task implicitly either: a worktree starts from committed HEAD.
162	Checkpoint first when the new task depends on that work.

165	
166	Read `references/parallel-agents.md` before spawning an independent agent while
167	another remains live. The fail-closed workflow uses `dev start --json`, requires
168	a newly created first-class Herdr worktree and its exact returned root pane,
169	then launches an explicit SpecStory/profile command there. Reused, fallback,

172	For a human one-liner, `dev start --run '<shell command>'` uses the same exact

177	`dev` guards writer-claiming direct/branch starts and resume when another

181	owner, not writer authorization. Never add `--allow-shared-checkout` unless
182	agents already have coordinated disjoint file ownership.

184	A new external agent does not inherit the parent permission mode, and a resumed

287	```
288	
289	OpenSSH is authority. Dev reads foreign definitions but never edits them; only
290	canonical portable aliases under `~/.ssh/dev.d` are mutable. Full setup needs an
291	explicit `--key` or `--generate-key`. It sends only one public record to a fixed
292	remote installer, preserves host-key policy, disables connection sharing for
293	proofs, and never copies/reads private key bytes for transfer. A working
294	ProxyJump is skipped unless `--install-on-working-jump` is explicit. Windows
295	administrator authorized_keys needs the separate
296	`--windows-admin-authorized-keys` consent and may still need manual elevation.
297	
298	`--fleet` is never inferred. It writes a strict generated `remotes.d` fragment
299	only after a second fresh ordinary alias login succeeds. The primary
300	`remotes.toml` remains user-authored and is edited through
301	`dev fleet config edit`; `fleet config show` displays the merged config and identifies generated
302	origins. `remote_os` selects POSIX shell or encoded Windows PowerShell transport.
303	
304	Treat partial and unknown results literally. If a remote installer started, the
305	key may have arrived; do not "clean up" `authorized_keys`. Local config and
306	generated keys are retained so a rerun can converge. `ssh remove` never revokes a
307	remote key, deletes local keys/known_hosts, or removes the shared Include.
308	
309	Read `references/prompt-handoffs.md` before using `dev prompt`, configuring a
310	launcher, or interpreting session/workspace closeout advice. Discover profiles
311	with `dev prompt agents`; its output is intentionally redacted. Profile selection
312	is global before recipe collection, requested modes never fall back across
313	profiles, and prompt recipes remain read-only context handoffs rather than
314	mutation or permission authority.
315	
316	## Bootstrapping and adopting an existing machine
317	
318	Read `references/bootstrap.md` before recursively scanning paths, creating a
319	symlink index, moving physical repositories, or generating layout config. Move
320	is destructive and must follow its report → review → apply procedure.
321	
322	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use. `dev` discovers repositories through
323	`paths.scan_roots` plus exact `paths.repo_paths` and never moves, renames or deletes anything.
324	
325	```bash
326	dev config init     # detects this machine's roots; every value stays editable
327	dev adopt           # report existing worktrees, sessions and unmerged branches
328	dev adopt --apply   # record them as tasks (nothing on disk changes)
329	```
330	
331	Do not assume the user's layout is `~/Documents/Program`. Run `dev config show`
332	or `dev repo list` to see what this machine is actually configured for.
333	
334	## Creating and setting up repositories
335	
336	Read `references/repository-bootstrap.md` before creating a published repo,
337	running project-owned hooks, or installing setup-capable skills. A bare
338	`dev repo new` is interactive; `dev repo new NAME` deliberately retains the
339	minimal README + initial-commit contract. A clear Git URL, local Git path, or
340	`owner/name` argument to `new` or `create` automatically clones and preserves
341	its remote; template and upstream-creation flags cannot accompany that route.
342	Explicit `repo clone` remains available when scripts should state acquisition
343	directly. On a TTY, bare `repo clone` selects an exact clone URL from the
344	existing private forge cache and retains a manual URL/path/owner-name option;
345	it never refreshes providers implicitly. Outside a checkout, bare `start`
346	selects a local repository with fast live discovery; inside one it keeps the
347	immediate current-repository default. The configured line selector defaults to `fzf` and
348	falls back to dev's built-in Bubble Tea picker when missing; non-TTY input stays
349	line-oriented.
350	`repo new --template` snapshots a local directory or Git tree into a fresh
351	history; it is not a clone. `--template-ref` and `--template-subdir` select the
352	exact source tree.
353	
354	Use `--check-in=commit|stage|none` to choose whether generated changes are
355	committed, staged for human review, or left unstaged (`auto` follows a new
356	repository's preset and otherwise defaults to none). `repo setup --commit`
357	remains the compatibility spelling for commit.
358	Stage mode cannot create an upstream and cannot hand dirty setup directly to
359	`start`.
360	
361	On a TTY, wizard fields are real inline editors: arrows, Home/End,
362	Backspace and Delete edit typed text rather than inserting escape sequences.
363	Esc or Ctrl-C cancels; piped input remains line-oriented.
364	
365	The create/setup wizard asks one customization-gate question after preset
366	selection. Declining uses resolved defaults and skips detailed template,
367	README/gitignore/license/agent/skill questions; explicit customization flags or
368	a required input without a default make yes the suggested answer.
369	
370	Global recipes live in `scaffolds.toml`. Repositories may commit the allowlisted
371	`.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`, but executable project
372	configuration in those files must be trusted by its exact content hash before
373	it runs. Legacy `.dev.toml` retains its compatibility behavior.
374	
375	## Dashboard and forge inventory
376	
377	Bare `dev` / `dev tui` is the seven-view dashboard described here. It is separate
378	from the plan-first `dev flow [repo]` repository lifecycle preview above.
379	
380	The dashboard has TASKS, REPOS, FLEET, TRY, REMOTE, SKILLS and MCP views, switched
381	with tab, vim-style h/l, or a left click on a visible tab. Left-click selects a
382	row without opening it, the wheel moves three rows, and right-click selects a row
383	and opens the same legal actions used by keyboard shortcuts. Repeated clicks do
384	not imply open. Wide TASKS tables show `REPO`; compact layouts keep it in detail.
385	TRY `n` creates an experiment; `space` opens metadata/lifecycle actions; `a`
386	includes retained history. Archive is a reversible same-filesystem move, not
387	deletion or disk reclamation. `?` opens the full key map.
388	
389	The initial view never waits for runtime/project-root resolution, cache decoding,
390	or shell tool probes. TASKS/REPOS/TRY publish independently from one shared local
391	cycle; optional tabs remain lazy. Refreshes are generation-scoped: late results
392	are ignored, failed refreshes keep usable rows, warning-only capability results
393	stay fresh, visible tabs resume after REPOS recovery, and valid empty results
394	clear obsolete rows. For a one-run diagnostic, set `DEV_TUI_TRACE` to an absolute new
395	file. The private bounded trace is written after TUI teardown with relative
396	startup/view timings and aggregate row counts only; it excludes names, paths,
397	commands, key values, URLs, handles and raw errors, and never enters `stats.db`
398	or a network sink. SKILLS and MCP are startup-context-first: inside Git they
399	scan only the exact current checkout plus global/user sources; outside Git they
400	reuse every accepted REPOS target and the ordinary startup directory. Uppercase
401	`A` toggles both views to all accepted repositories for the current TUI run.
402	Skill listing uses the native versioned 77-agent path registry and never runs
403	Node/`npx`; `c` hashes remote Git objects without checkout filters, while
404	mutations require a trusted direct provider and are serialized. MCP inventories
405	only sanitized static declarations for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and
406	OpenCode; only Claude's documented project approvals are resolved. It never
407	starts or health-checks a server. In either capability view, `e` opens the selected
408	local source and `y` copies its path, safe summary, or explicit raw file; raw reads
409	are regular-file-only, capped at 1 MiB, and may put credentials into the system
410	clipboard without changing sanitized inventory output. Full detail:
411	`references/agent-capabilities.md`.
412	
413	REMOTE queries authenticated `gh` and `glab` plus configured Azure DevOps
414	organization/project targets lazily and fully paginates every repository the
415	account can access. A private cache is decoded after the first view; stale rows
416	stay searchable while refresh runs. Malformed/oversized payloads and caches
417	fingerprinted for another configured GH/GL host or Azure target are ignored.
418	GitLab uses explicit `GITLAB_HOST`/`GLAB_HOST` (default `gitlab.com`) instead of
419	cwd inference; a successful empty refresh clears obsolete rows. `/` filters
420	provider, owner/name, visibility and description, with `vis:private` for an exact
421	visibility match. Enter opens an existing local clone. For an absent remote, `c`
422	confirms; `enter` clones and stays in the dashboard, while `o` clones and opens
423	after a spinner-backed, local-only REPOS refresh. A `project_root` outside the
424	configured REPOS discovery roots/depth is rejected before mutation. `q`/Ctrl-C
425	requests cancellation without abandoning the in-flight result. Once accepted,
426	REMOTE shows `repo` and REPOS can search the clone immediately. If Git leaves a
427	destination after failure, REMOTE marks the exact path `inspect` and does not
428	delete it automatically. Use `dev repo remote [query] --json` for the non-interactive form; `--cached` avoids
429	a network query and `--refresh` forces a complete synchronization.
430	
431	`dev journal` derives calendar-day reports from Git rather than storing a
432	second history database. The default current-user report adds existing
433	session/WakaTime observations, matching task intent and recent dirty-worktree
434	snapshots, clearly separated from committed history. `auto` expands at most 100
435	commit details while retaining complete aggregates; `--max-commits 0` is
436	unlimited. Use `--author <email>` or `--all-authors` for commit-only team views,
437	and `--json` for a stable structured report. dev generates the context only; it
438	does not launch the receiving agent.
439	
440	`dev summary` is the complementary current-state view across this machine. It
441	combines durable repositories and present active/deprecated Tries with live Git,
442	worktree, task, runtime, recovery and catalog facts. The default `auto` Markdown
443	expands active work and leaves quiet projects in a compact index; `--attention`
444	selects both active work and recovery hazards, while `--json` always emits the
445	complete selected snapshot. Use journal for time ranges and `repo context` for
446	one repository.
447	
448	Azure DevOps inventory is opt-in and cloud-only:
449	
450	```toml
451	[[forge.azure_devops]]
452	organization = "https://dev.azure.com/acme"
453	project = "Platform"
454	```
455	
456	Install Azure CLI's `azure-devops` extension separately. `dev` never installs
457	the extension, logs in, changes Azure defaults, or stores a PAT.
458	
459	FLEET merges user-authored primary `remotes.toml` with strict dev-owned sibling
460	`remotes.d/ssh-<alias>.toml` fragments, then reuses the accepted REPOS snapshot
461	for the local host and calls each configured host's own `dev` over SSH. Generated
462	entries are owned by explicit `dev ssh setup/remove --fleet`; FLEET `e` and
463	`fleet config edit` open only the primary file, while `fleet config show` marks
464	generated origins. `remote_os` selects POSIX shell or allowlisted encoded
465	PowerShell transport and participates in endpoint cache identity with the SSH
466	port and optional `machine_id` pin. If REPOS is still loading, FLEET waits while keeping cached rows instead
467	of rescanning. The TUI hides this machine by default because REPOS is richer;
468	`a` includes local rows. `dev fleet list` remains local plus remote. Enter
469	prefers Herdr remote navigation and falls back to an SSH login shell.
470	`dev fleet sync` is explicit and strict: it only fast-forwards a clean checkout
471	of the same behind-only branch; dirty/ahead/diverged clones are never rewritten.
472	
473	`dev fleet files [repo-or-path] --to <host>` is a separate one-shot channel for
474	explicitly exported ignored files. It is report-only unless `--apply` is passed;
475	`--yes` never implies `--replace`. Both clones must already match by fetch
476	identity, attached branch and exact commit, and each exact path must be untracked
477	and ignored on both sides. Only bounded regular files are accepted. Apply also
478	requires a `machine_id` pin obtained with the read-only `dev fleet machine-id
479	<host>` command and verified independently. The operation never clones, switches
480	branches, runs provisioning, transfers task/catalog/note state, deletes source
481	files, or evicts a repository; native Windows payloads are disabled.
482	
483	REPOS has LIVE, LATEST and asynchronous SIZE. SIZE is logical
484	checkout+private-Git bytes; shared Git is separate and marked `+S`. Detail also
485	shows no-remote/local-only/multi-upstream recovery topology. Press space to
486	expand linked worktrees; children
487	show their own Git/session/task state and mark harness-owned or untracked
488	checkouts `(ephemeral)` / `(external)`. Press `y` followed by `y/p/b/s/w` to
489	copy contextual Markdown, path, branch, runtime/agent sessions, or every
490	worktree path. `dev repo context [repo]` prints the full Markdown without a TUI.
491	`[tui.repos]` chooses columns and default sort; `O` cycles sort and `R` reverses
492	it.
493	
494	`H` opens the selected repo's heatmap. On an empty panel, `b` backfills only
495	that repo and redraws; `r` rereads existing stats. Stats live in
496	`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and are durable observations, not cache — use
497	`dev stats clear` with an explicit scope. `dev cache clear` only removes
498	regenerable forge/size/gitignore/note-FTS data under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev`.
499	
500	On ordinary views, `e` edits dev config and returning live-reloads data/tool
501	bindings; on SKILLS/MCP it opens the selected capability file and reloads only
502	that inventory. `r` reloads explicitly. Runtime backend changes require restarting
503	the TUI.
504	
505	External tools are explicit `[[tui.tools]]` config. Run `dev tui tools` before
506	recommending a binding; it shows the exact command and whether it is available.
507	Commands run through `$SHELL` in the selected checkout. For an alias/function
508	that exists only in shell rc, set `interactive = true`; dev uses `$SHELL -lic`
509	and evaluates the command after rc loading. Prefer an executable on PATH when
510	the binding should be portable across machines.
511	
512	## Repository quick notes
513	
514	Read `references/notes.md` before adding/searching/editing/deleting notes or
515	when deciding whether content belongs in dev vs td/beads.
516	
517	Quick notes are multiple timestamped Markdown files under configured
518	`paths.state_dir/notes/<catalog-id>/` (default `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`); the
519	catalog ID attaches them to the canonical clone across worktrees, symlinks and
520	moves. `dev` does not synchronize notes or catalog state, so cross-host
521	attachment requires syncing both. SQLite FTS at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db`
522	is disposable: clearing it removes no thoughts and the next search rebuilds it.
523	
524	TUI context keys: `n` quick-adds on TASKS/REPOS; `N` browses with `/` search,
525	Enter expand, `a` add, `e` editor, and confirmed `d` delete. In TRY, `n` remains
526	“new Try.” REMOTE needs a local clone.
527	
528	## Editing configuration
529	
530	Use `dev edit` (or `dev config edit`) rather than guessing the XDG path. It
531	opens the file selected by `--config`, generating the machine-detected starter
532	when absent, and resolves `--editor` → `$VISUAL` → `$EDITOR` → nvim/vim/vi.
533	
534	## Rules for agents
535	
536	1. **Do not equate task with worktree.** Ad-hoc opening needs no task; `--direct`
537	   tracks current/main; `--branch-only` is lightweight isolation; default
538	   worktree is for interruption/experimentation/parallelism.
539	
540	2. **Always pass `--base` for branch/worktree tasks.** Without it a new branch starts from the current
541	   HEAD, so starting a task while standing on `feature/A` silently builds on
542	   `feature/A`. This is the single most common way to produce a confusing
543	   history unattended.
544	
545	3. **Never `--force` a worktree removal on your own.** `dev wt rm` refuses a
546	   checkout with uncommitted changes; that refusal is the feature. Ask the
547	   user before overriding it.
548	
549	4. **Report drift, do not fix it silently.** `dev sweep` without `--apply`
550	   changes nothing. Show the user its output rather than running `--apply --yes`
551	   for them. For merged worktree cleanup, run `dev sweep --merged-worktrees`
552	   from the canonical main checkout, present every candidate and blocker as a
553	   QA question, and use `--apply --yes` only after the user explicitly approves
554	   that exact set. Branch deletion remains a separate `--delete-branches` opt-in.
555	   `dev pr list --scope local --state merged` finds candidates, but a merged
556	   pull request is never on its own grounds to remove a checkout: a squash
557	   merge leaves no local ancestor, so containment still has to be proven
558	   locally. See `references/pull-requests.md`. If an explanation is useful, use
559	   the generic `workspace-closeout` recipe only after reading
560	   `references/prompt-handoffs.md`; its audit is advisory and never an approval.
561	
562	5. **Prefer a checkpoint commit over `git stash`.** A stash is invisible in the
563	   log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
564	   machine. `dev park --wip` makes a `wip:` commit instead.
565	
566	6. **One writer per branch at a time.** `dev resume` refuses a task owned by
567	   another host without `--force`. Before overriding, confirm that machine has
568	   pushed.
569	
570	7. **Check `dev wt plan` before blaming a worktree.** A worktree that comes up
571	   broken is nearly always a provisioning gap, not a git problem. The plan
572	   shows the detected project types, which tools are missing, and exactly what
573	   would be copied or run. Dependencies arrive by a per-ecosystem strategy —
574	   `reinstall` (default), `copy`, `link` or `skip` — and dev refuses an unsound
575	   one rather than producing a broken checkout: a virtualenv cannot be copied,
576	   because it bakes its own absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg`.
577	
578	8. **Do not create a worktree per agent.** Worktrees isolate *change streams*;
579	   panes isolate *agents*. A writer claim in one checkout needs explicit
580	   disjoint ownership; pure open/focus may navigate to the existing owner.
581	
582	9. **Parallel launch is exact-pane and fail-closed.** Accept only a new
583	   first-class Herdr worktree/root pane from `dev start --json` or the same
584	   internal proof used by explicit `dev start --run`. Never infer from
585	   focus/sidebar order, relocate SpecStory with mid-session `EnterWorktree`, or
586	   treat any recognized agent state as a free pane. Never add
587	   `--allow-shared-checkout` without coordinated ownership.
588	
589	10. **Launcher profile and effective permissions are explicit.** Standard
590	    Claude/Codex put the complete native command inside SpecStory `-c`; verified
591	    `*-copilot-once` wrappers already wrap SpecStory but inherit effective
592	    provider permissions, which may be dangerous. Never append a conflicting
593	    safer mode to an elevated command. Read `parallel-agents.md`.
594	
595	11. **Cleanup is external, never self-triggered by agent state.** Herdr `done`
596	    means a turn settled. Arm and finalize exact artifacts first; `dev done`
597	    integrates only, and `dev retire` must run outside the target workspace.
598	    Never run raw `git worktree remove --force` against the caller's checkout.
599	
600	12. **Prefer `dev bootstrap --index` over `--move`.** If the problem is
601	   navigation, a symlink catalog solves it without changing the authoritative
602	   paths. For a physical move, never add `--apply --yes` on the user's behalf;
603	   blocked rows are preconditions to resolve, not checks to bypass.
604	
605	13. **`dev adopt` without `--apply` changes nothing.** Show the user its report
606	   rather than applying it for them — which branches count as work in flight is
607	   their judgement, not yours.
608	
609	14. **Treat Markdown notes as durable and notes.db as cache.** Never delete
610	   configured `paths.state_dir/notes` to fix search; use `dev cache clear notes`
611	   and reindex. Note deletion itself requires explicit confirmation, and `dev`
612	   does not synchronize note/catalog state between hosts.
613	
614	15. **Do not call stats.db a cache.** Session/WakaTime observations may not be
615	   reconstructible. Use `dev stats clear --repo/--source/--all`; use
616	   `dev cache clear` only for regenerable remote/fleet/size/gitignore/license/note-FTS caches.
617	
618	16. **Archive is not eviction.** `dev tries archive` is a reversible hidden move
619	   on the same filesystem; it does not free space. Phase 1 has no project-data
620	   delete command. Never substitute `rm -rf` merely because a remote exists —
621	   no-remote, local-only refs, ignored files and stash are independent risks.
622	
623	17. **Read Git state as counts, not a dirty boolean.** `⇡`/`⇣` are upstream
624	   divergence; `=` conflicts, `+` staged, `!` unstaged, `?` untracked. Use
625	   `dev status` or JSON for the unique-path and type breakdown before cleanup.
626	
627	18. **OpenSSH is authority; foreign SSH config is read-only.** Run `ssh init`
628	   without `--apply` first, never hand-edit a dev-owned fragment, and never turn
629	   alias discovery into implicit `--fleet`. Full setup must name/generate a key,
630	   but only its public record may reach the remote. Do not copy private keys,
631	   weaken host-key policy, delete remote authorized_keys after an unknown
632	   result, or promise that `ssh remove` performs revocation.
633	
634	19. **Portable export is separately authorized.** Never treat `[worktree].include`
635	   as permission to send a file off-machine. Use only `[local_files].include` or
636	   explicit `--file`, show the report first, independently verify and pin the
637	   target UUID before apply, and never infer `--replace` from `--yes`.
638	
639	20. **Commit messages stay English** and follow Conventional Commits, even when
640	   the conversation is in another language — see the companion `git-workflow`
641	   skill, which owns commit conventions, SemVer and branch naming. This skill
642	   does not duplicate them.
643	
644	21. **Never bypass `.dev-cli` project-config trust.** Inspect the rendered hooks
645	    and skill entrypoints, then use `dev config trust <repo> --yes`. A changed
646	    executable hash is a new decision. Pre-commit/gitleaks inspect generated
647	    content; they do not make an untrusted command safe to execute. Legacy
648	    `.dev.toml` remains a compatibility surface rather than acquiring this trust
649	    contract retroactively.
650	
651	## When to use this skill
652	
653	- "What am I working on?" / "我在做什麼" / too many terminal workspaces open.
654	- Starting, parking or resuming a piece of work.
655	- Spawning independent background agents without disturbing a live checkout.
656	- "Where should this worktree go?" / "should I use `claude --worktree` or herdr?"
657	- A new worktree is missing `node_modules`, `.venv` or `.env`.
658	- Cleaning up stale branches, worktrees and sessions.
659	- Rendering or handing off pull-request/session/workspace operational context.
660	- Cloning, creating or auditing repositories across a machine.
661	- Discovering, inspecting, configuring, probing, or removing an OpenSSH alias.
662	- Installing a public key through ProxyJump or registering a verified dev fleet host.
663	- Promoting an experiment into a real project.
664	- "Which repo do I spend my time in?"
665	- Setting up a `.gitignore`, or a harness worktree showing as untracked.
666	- Adopting a machine that already has repos, worktrees and sessions.
667	- Recursively scanning, indexing, or physically reorganising existing repos.
668	- Configuring a flat repo/worktree layout or generating config for one.
669	
670	## When NOT to use it
671	
672	- **Commit messages, SemVer, branch naming, PR-vs-main tiering** — that is the
673	  `git-workflow` skill. This one links to it rather than restating it.
674	- **Standalone Herdr pane/agent control** — that is the `herdr` skill. The
675	  `dev start --json` and explicit `--run` cross-tool launch paths remain here.
676	- A single `git add` + `git commit` needs no tooling at all.
677	
678	## Reference files
679	
680	- `references/ssh-hosts.md` — read before SSH discovery, managed-fragment
681	  changes, public-key bootstrap, probing, or generated fleet registration/removal.
682	- `references/notes.md` — read before repository quick-note operations or
683	  choosing the boundary with td/beads.
684	- `references/bootstrap.md` — read before scanning or organising an existing
685	  machine; includes the non-destructive index default and move safety gates.
686	- `references/worktree-ownership.md` — who owns which worktree, and how a
687	  worktree gets a working environment. Read before creating one.
688	- `references/task-lifecycle.md` — HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE, when to park, and how
689	  work moves between machines.
690	- `references/agent-retirement.md` — prepare/finalize/integrate/retire, caller
691	  safety, exact transcript handling and orphaned-runtime recovery.
692	- `references/runtime-herdr.md` — how `dev` and herdr divide responsibility,
693	  including native worktree grouping, collisions and cleanup semantics.
694	- `references/parallel-agents.md` — read before launching parallel background
695	  work; exact JSON/pane validation, SpecStory profiles and permissions.
696	- `references/commands.md` — the full command reference, generated from the
697	  binary by `dev skill sync` so it cannot drift.
698	- `references/repository-bootstrap.md` — new/clone/setup presets, project
699	  overrides, skill initialization, upstream publishing, trust and handoff.
700	- `references/pull-requests.md` — read before using `dev pr` or advising on a
701	  pull request; covers effective scope, local checkout health, why a field can
702	  be missing, and why a merged request cannot authorize retirement.
703	- `references/prompt-handoffs.md` — read before rendering/running/opening a
704	  generic recipe or configuring a launcher; covers transports, current-terminal
705	  behavior, permissions, closeout audits, and rebase-conflict safety.
706	
707	## Gotchas
708	
709	- **`dev` may be a shell wrapper around the binary.** The trusted `shell-init`
710	  output defines a wrapper that gives navigation commands a private side channel
711	  (a child-only file descriptor for POSIX shells, a `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` temp
712	  file for `shell-init powershell`), reads one NUL-terminated path and calls
713	  `builtin cd` / `Set-Location` without evaluating command output. Without the
714	  wrapper, the binary's printable legacy directive cannot change the parent
715	  shell — that is not a bug.
716	- **Windows runs SSH natively but without a multiplexer.** SSH discovery,
717	  protected managed fragments, ssh-keygen, public-key bootstrap, and Windows
718	  fleet transport are supported. There is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr on Windows,
719	  so the runtime backend is always `none`; `dev fleet open` starts a child shell
720	  instead of replacing the process. Windows remote helpers use only the encoded
721	  allowlisted PowerShell launcher; `remote_os` must match the target. `dev upgrade` self-replaces only
722	  a standalone install and otherwise delegates to the detected Homebrew/Scoop/
723	  `go install` command. Stable releases advance the Homebrew tap; never overwrite its Cellar
724	  binary manually.
725	- **A worktree is a clean checkout.** It has no `node_modules`, no `.venv` and
726	  none of the gitignored env files. `dev` provisions it; `--no-provision`
727	  skips that and leaves you to it.
728	- **Only explicitly included, gitignored stable regular files are copied.**
729	  Source swaps and symlinked destination parents are refused; existing targets
730	  are reported skipped, not copied. Do not universally include
731	  `.claude/settings.local.json`: only sticky/plain-Claude profiles opt in.
732	- **Worktree provisioning and fleet export use different allowlists.**
733	  `[worktree].include` is local-only. `fleet files` reads `[local_files].include`
734	  plus explicit `--file`, expands patterns before transport, and defaults to a
735	  content-free plan. It is not task transfer, backup, restore, or eviction.
736	- **A repository template is a snapshot, not a clone.** Source Git metadata,
737	  remotes and history are excluded. A local Git worktree without a ref includes
738	  tracked plus nonignored untracked files; a non-Git directory includes its
739	  complete current tree. Human plans preview paths and warn about live unpinned
740	  sources. URL userinfo is redacted, while held root/directory/file handles
741	  confine traversal. Symlinks, special files, traversal and source changes fail
742	  closed, and the snapshot applies only to an otherwise-empty new repo.
743	- **Lazygit commit drafts are a best-effort adapter.** `--check-in=stage` writes
744	  `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` in that worktree's Git directory so lowercase `c`
745	  can preload the proposed message. This is not `commit.template` or
746	  `COMMIT_EDITMSG`, uppercase `C` and other clients need not read it, and an
747	  existing different draft is preserved. Draft write/sync failure is a warning,
748	  not rollback: the successfully staged index remains ready for manual commit.
749	- **Agent-ready guidance is honest about unknowns.** Its canonical `AGENTS.md`
750	  starter labels bootstrap status incomplete, supplies safe working/handoff
751	  rules, and leaves project purpose, commands, architecture, and invariants as
752	  TODOs rather than fabricating facts.
753	- **Agent history remains reviewable.** The common managed ignore excludes only
754	  `.specstory/statistics.json`; histories, project identity, and config remain
755	  visible. Built-in `agent-history-hygiene` additionally seeds
756	  `.specstory/.gitignore` only for machine-local `.project.json` and generated
757	  `statistics.json`; it does not ignore `.specstory/history/*.md`. An existing
758	  nested ignore keeps its custom content and mode while missing required rules
759	  are appended. Correct any broader parent `.specstory/` rule explicitly.
760	- **Removing a worktree never deletes the branch.** Those are separate
761	  decisions; conflating them is how work gets lost.
762	- **Bare `dev done` is interactive only on a TTY.** It reports branch relation
763	  and dirty-content equivalence, then offers commit/discard and FF/PR/merged
764	  handling. It records DONE without closing/removing resources; Retire is
765	  separate. Non-interactive use remains report-only without `--ff`/`--pr`. Unique discard
766	  requires `DROP` or explicit `--dirty=discard --yes`.
767	- **The stats sampler must be scheduled.** `dev stats` is empty until
768	  `dev stats backfill` runs once and `dev stats sample` runs periodically.

diff --git a/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-mouse-mode-and-more/internal/tui/mouse.go b/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-mouse-mode-and-more/internal/tui/mouse.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f5046fc
--- /dev/null
+++ b/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-mouse-mode-and-more/internal/tui/mouse.go
@@ -0,0 +1,138 @@
+package tui
+
+import tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
+
+const mouseWheelRows = 3
+
+// mouseFrameFits fails closed when Bubble Tea would drop top lines from an
+// over-height frame. Screen-relative mouse coordinates cannot safely target
+// logical header/list rows once that clipping occurs.
+func (m Model) mouseFrameFits() bool {
+	if m.height <= 0 {
+		return false
+	}
+	if m.overlay.kind == overlayActionMenu {
+		return lineCount(m.renderOverlay()) <= m.height
+	}
+
+	n := m.count()
+	listLines := m.listPreambleLines()
+	if n > 0 {
+		visible := min(n, m.listHeight())
+		listLines += visible
+		if visible < n {
+			listLines++
+		}
+	}
+	total := 2 + listLines + 1 + lineCount(m.renderDetail()) + 1 + lineCount(m.renderFooter())
+	return total <= m.height
+}
+
+func (m Model) updateMouse(message tea.MouseMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
+	event := tea.MouseEvent(message)
+	if event.Shift || event.Alt || event.Ctrl {
+		return m, nil
+	}
+	if m.overlay.kind == overlayActionMenu {
+		if !m.mouseFrameFits() {
+			return m, nil
+		}
+		return m.updateActionMenuMouse(event)
+	}
+	if m.noteMode() || m.overlay.kind != overlayNone || m.mode != modeList {
+		return m, nil
+	}
+	if !m.mouseFrameFits() {
+		return m, nil
+	}
+
+	if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
+		if !m.mouseOverList(event.X, event.Y) {
+			return m, nil
+		}
+		delta := mouseWheelRows
+		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
+			delta = -delta
+		}
+		m.setAt(m.at() + delta)
+		return m, nil
+	}
+	if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress {
+		return m, nil
+	}
+
+	if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonLeft && event.Y == 0 {
+		for _, hit := range m.buildHeaderLayout().tabs {
+			if event.X < hit.from || event.X >= hit.to {
+				continue
+			}
+			if m.view == hit.view {
+				return m, nil
+			}
+			m.view = hit.view
+			return m.afterViewSwitch()
+		}
+		return m, nil
+	}
+
+	row, ok := m.mouseRow(event.X, event.Y)
+	if !ok {
+		return m, nil
+	}
+	switch event.Button {
+	case tea.MouseButtonLeft:
+		m.setAt(row)
+	case tea.MouseButtonRight:
+		m.setAt(row)
+		if !m.remoteClone.active() {
+			m = m.openActionMenu()
+		}
+	}
+	return m, nil
+}
+
+func (m Model) mouseRow(x, y int) (int, bool) {
+	if x < 0 || x >= m.width {
+		return 0, false
+	}
+	count := m.count()
+	from, to := m.window(count)
+	first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
+	if y < first || y >= first+(to-from) {
+		return 0, false
+	}
+	return from + y - first, true
+}
+
+func (m Model) mouseOverList(x, y int) bool {
+	if x < 0 || x >= m.width || m.count() == 0 {
+		return false
+	}
+	from, to := m.window(m.count())
+	first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
+	return y >= 2 && y < first+(to-from)
+}
+
+func (m Model) updateActionMenuMouse(event tea.MouseEvent) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
+	if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
+		if m.overlay.optionCount == 0 {
+			return m, nil
+		}
+		delta := 1
+		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
+			delta = -1
+		}
+		m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + delta + m.overlay.optionCount) % m.overlay.optionCount
+		return m, nil
+	}
+	if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress || event.Button != tea.MouseButtonLeft {
+		return m, nil
+	}
+	first := m.buildActionMenuLayout().firstOptionY
+	if event.Y < first || event.Y >= first+m.overlay.optionCount {
+		m.overlay = overlayState{}
+		return m, nil
+	}
+	m.overlay.optionIndex = event.Y - first
+	return m.runOverlayAction()
+}

+func (m *Model) resetCapabilityView(view View) {
+	m.invalidateView(view)
+	generation := m.loads[int(view)].generation
+	m.loads[int(view)] = viewLoadState{generation: generation}
+	m.viewErrors[int(view)] = nil
+	m.viewStatuses[int(view)] = ""

+	case ViewMCP:

+		m.mcpCursor = 0
+	}
+}

+	} else {

+	}
+	m.setViewStatus(view, dependentLoadingStatus(view))
+	return m, m.reloadDependentView(view)

12	func skillFilePath(row agentskill.Skill) (string, error) {
13		if row.Presence != agentskill.PresenceMissing && strings.TrimSpace(row.Path) != "" {
14			return filepath.Join(row.Path, "SKILL.md"), nil
15		}
16		if row.Lock != nil && strings.TrimSpace(row.Lock.File) != "" {
17			return row.Lock.File, nil
18		}
19		return "", fmt.Errorf("skill %s has no local skill or lock file", row.Name)
20	}
21	
22	func (m Model) capabilityFilePath() (string, error) {
23		if row, ok := m.currentSkill(); ok {
24			return skillFilePath(row)
25		}
26		if row, ok := m.currentMCP(); ok {
27			if strings.TrimSpace(row.ConfigPath) == "" {
28				return "", fmt.Errorf("MCP server %s has no local config path", row.Name)
29			}
30			return row.ConfigPath, nil
31		}
32		return "", fmt.Errorf("the selected row has no capability config file")
33	}

35	func formatSkillSummary(row agentskill.Skill) string {
36		lines := []string{
37			"name: " + row.Name,
38			"scope: " + string(row.Scope),
39		}
40		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "repository", row.Repository)
41		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "checkout", row.Checkout)
42		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "path", row.Path)
43		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "agents", strings.Join(row.Agents, ", "))
44		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "managed", string(row.ManagedBy))
45		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "presence", string(row.Presence))
46		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "integrity", string(row.Integrity))
47		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source", row.Source)
48		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source_url", row.SourceURL)
49		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "update", string(row.UpdateStatus))
50		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
51	}
52	
53	func formatMCPSummary(row agentmcp.Declaration) string {
54		lines := []string{
55			"server: " + row.Name,
56			"agent: " + string(row.Agent),
57			"scope: " + string(row.Scope),
58		}
59		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "repository", row.Repository)
60		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "checkout", row.Checkout)
61		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "config", row.ConfigPath)
62		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source", mcpSource(row))
63		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "state", mcpDeclarationState(row))
64		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "transport", string(row.Transport))
65		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "endpoint", row.Endpoint)
66		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "command", row.Command)
67		if row.ArgumentCount > 0 {
68			lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("arguments: %d value(s) redacted", row.ArgumentCount))
69		}
70		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "policies", mcpPolicySummary(row))
71		if len(row.Credentials) > 0 {
72			credentials := make([]string, 0, len(row.Credentials))
73			for _, credential := range row.Credentials {
74				value := string(credential.Kind)
75				if credential.Name != "" {
76					value += ":" + credential.Name
77				}
78				credentials = append(credentials, value)
79			}
80			lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "credentials", strings.Join(credentials, ", "))
81		}
82		if len(row.Redactions) > 0 {
83			redactions := make([]string, len(row.Redactions))
84			for i, redaction := range row.Redactions {
85				redactions[i] = string(redaction)
86			}
87			lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "redacted", strings.Join(redactions, ", "))
88		}
89		if len(row.Coverage) > 0 {
90			coverage := make([]string, len(row.Coverage))
91			for i, item := range row.Coverage {
92				coverage[i] = string(item.Code)
93			}
94			lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "coverage", strings.Join(coverage, ", "))
95		}
96		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
97	}

99	func (m Model) copyBindingHelp() string {
100		if m.view == ViewRepos {
101			return "y context · p path · b branch · s sessions · w worktree paths"
102		}
103		parts := make([]string, 0, 4)
104		if _, err := m.capabilityFilePath(); err == nil {
105			parts = append(parts, "p file path")
106		}
107		parts = append(parts, "s safe summary")
108		if row, ok := m.currentSkill(); ok && row.SourceURL != "" {
109			parts = append(parts, "u source URL")
110		}
111		if _, err := m.capabilityFilePath(); err == nil && m.actions.ReadFile != nil {
112			parts = append(parts, "f raw file")
113		}
114		return strings.Join(parts, " · ")
115	}

117	func appendSummaryLine(lines []string, label, value string) []string {
118		if strings.TrimSpace(value) == "" {
119			return lines
120		}
121		return append(lines, label+": "+value)
122	}

5	const mouseWheelRows = 3
6	
7	// mouseFrameFits fails closed when Bubble Tea would drop top lines from an
8	// over-height frame. Screen-relative mouse coordinates cannot safely target
9	// logical header/list rows once that clipping occurs.
10	func (m Model) mouseFrameFits() bool {
11		if m.height <= 0 {
12			return false
13		}
14		if m.overlay.kind == overlayActionMenu {
15			return lineCount(m.renderOverlay()) <= m.height
16		}
17	
18		n := m.count()
19		listLines := m.listPreambleLines()
20		if n > 0 {
21			visible := min(n, m.listHeight())
22			listLines += visible
23			if visible < n {
24				listLines++
25			}
26		}
27		total := 2 + listLines + 1 + lineCount(m.renderDetail()) + 1 + lineCount(m.renderFooter())
28		return total <= m.height
29	}
30	
31	func (m Model) updateMouse(message tea.MouseMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
32		event := tea.MouseEvent(message)
33		if event.Shift || event.Alt || event.Ctrl {
34			return m, nil
35		}
36		if m.overlay.kind == overlayActionMenu {
37			if !m.mouseFrameFits() {
38				return m, nil
39			}
40			return m.updateActionMenuMouse(event)
41		}
42		if m.noteMode() || m.overlay.kind != overlayNone || m.mode != modeList {
43			return m, nil
44		}
45		if !m.mouseFrameFits() {
46			return m, nil
47		}
48	
49		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
50			if !m.mouseOverList(event.X, event.Y) {
51				return m, nil
52			}
53			delta := mouseWheelRows
54			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
55				delta = -delta
56			}
57			m.setAt(m.at() + delta)
58			return m, nil
59		}
60		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress {
61			return m, nil
62		}
63	
64		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonLeft && event.Y == 0 {
65			for _, hit := range m.buildHeaderLayout().tabs {
66				if event.X < hit.from || event.X >= hit.to {
67					continue
68				}
69				if m.view == hit.view {
70					return m, nil
71				}
72				m.view = hit.view
73				return m.afterViewSwitch()
74			}
75			return m, nil
76		}
77	
78		row, ok := m.mouseRow(event.X, event.Y)
79		if !ok {
80			return m, nil
81		}
82		switch event.Button {
83		case tea.MouseButtonLeft:
84			m.setAt(row)
85		case tea.MouseButtonRight:
86			m.setAt(row)
87			if !m.remoteClone.active() {
88				m = m.openActionMenu()
89			}
90		}
91		return m, nil
92	}
93	
94	func (m Model) mouseRow(x, y int) (int, bool) {
95		if x < 0 || x >= m.width {
96			return 0, false
97		}
98		count := m.count()
99		from, to := m.window(count)
100		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
101		if y < first || y >= first+(to-from) {
102			return 0, false
103		}
104		return from + y - first, true
105	}
106	
107	func (m Model) mouseOverList(x, y int) bool {
108		if x < 0 || x >= m.width || m.count() == 0 {
109			return false
110		}
111		from, to := m.window(m.count())
112		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
113		return y >= 2 && y < first+(to-from)
114	}
115	
116	func (m Model) updateActionMenuMouse(event tea.MouseEvent) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
117		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
118			if m.overlay.optionCount == 0 {
119				return m, nil
120			}
121			delta := 1
122			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
123				delta = -1
124			}
125			m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + delta + m.overlay.optionCount) % m.overlay.optionCount
126			return m, nil
127		}
128		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress || event.Button != tea.MouseButtonLeft {
129			return m, nil
130		}
131		first := m.buildActionMenuLayout().firstOptionY
132		if event.Y < first || event.Y >= first+m.overlay.optionCount {
133			m.overlay = overlayState{}
134			return m, nil
135		}
136		m.overlay.optionIndex = event.Y - first
137		return m.runOverlayAction()
138	}

115	func prepareTUICapabilityEdit(path string) (tui.CapabilityEdit, error) {
116		logical := filepath.Clean(path)
117		resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(logical)
118		if err != nil {
119			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve capability file %s: %w", config.Contract(logical), err)
120		}
121		source, observed, err := safefile.OpenRegular(resolved)
122		if err != nil {
123			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, fmt.Errorf("open capability file %s: %w", config.Contract(logical), err)
124		}
125		original, readErr := safefile.ReadAll(context.Background(), source, safefile.CompiledMaxFileBytes)
126		closeErr := source.Close()
127		if readErr != nil {
128			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, fmt.Errorf("read capability file %s: %w", config.Contract(logical), readErr)
129		}
130		if closeErr != nil {
131			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, fmt.Errorf("close capability file %s: %w", config.Contract(logical), closeErr)
132		}
133	
134		working, err := os.CreateTemp("", "dev-capability-edit-*")
135		if err != nil {
136			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
137		}
138		workingPath := working.Name()
139		cleanup := true
140		defer func() {
141			if cleanup {
142				_ = os.Remove(workingPath)
143			}
144		}()
145		if _, err := working.Write(original); err != nil {
146			_ = working.Close()
147			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
148		}
149		if err := working.Sync(); err != nil {
150			_ = working.Close()
151			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
152		}
153		if err := working.Close(); err != nil {
154			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
155		}
156		process, _, err := editorProcess(workingPath, "")
157		if err != nil {
158			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
159		}
160		cleanup = false
161	
162		return tui.CapabilityEdit{
163			Command: process,
164			Complete: func(runErr error) error {
165				if runErr != nil {
166					_ = os.Remove(workingPath)
167					return runErr
168				}
169				edited, err := safefile.ReadRegular(context.Background(), workingPath, safefile.CompiledMaxFileBytes)
170				if err != nil {
171					return fmt.Errorf("read edited capability file; working copy preserved at %s: %w", config.Contract(workingPath), err)
172				}
173				if bytes.Equal(edited, original) {
174					return os.Remove(workingPath)
175				}
176				root, err := os.OpenRoot(filepath.Dir(resolved))
177				if err != nil {
178					return fmt.Errorf("open capability file directory; working copy preserved at %s: %w", config.Contract(workingPath), err)
179				}
180				defer root.Close()
181				if _, err := safefile.AtomicReplace(
182					context.Background(), root, filepath.Base(resolved), observed, edited, observed.Mode().Perm(),
183				); err != nil {
184					return fmt.Errorf("replace changed capability file; working copy preserved at %s: %w", config.Contract(workingPath), err)
185				}
186				return os.Remove(workingPath)
187			},
188		}, nil
189	}

191	// ensureConfigForEdit generates a usable config before opening an absent path.
192	// Editing an empty file would hide every default the user is trying to change.
193	func ensureConfigForEdit(path string) (bool, error) {
194		info, err := os.Stat(path)
195		switch {
196		case err == nil && info.IsDir():
197			return false, fmt.Errorf("%s is a directory, not a config file", config.Contract(path))
198		case err == nil:
199			return false, nil
200		case !os.IsNotExist(err):
201			return false, err
202		}
203		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
204			return false, err
205		}
206		body := renderStarterConfig(config.DetectLayout().Fallbacks())
207		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o644); err != nil {
208			return false, err
209		}
210		return true, nil
211	}
212	
213	func editorProcess(path, override string) (*exec.Cmd, string, error) {
214		chosen, err := resolveEditor(override)
215		if err != nil {
216			return nil, "", err
217		}
218		command, err := fleetEditorCommand(chosen, path)
219		return command, chosen, err
220	}
221	
222	func resolveEditor(override string) (string, error) {
223		for _, candidate := range []string{override, os.Getenv("VISUAL"), os.Getenv("EDITOR")} {
224			if strings.TrimSpace(candidate) != "" {
225				return candidate, nil
226			}
227		}
228		for _, candidate := range []string{"nvim", "vim", "vi"} {
229			if _, err := exec.LookPath(candidate); err == nil {
230				return candidate, nil
231			}
232		}
233		return "", fmt.Errorf("no editor found; set $VISUAL or $EDITOR, or pass --editor")
234	}

154	// buildHeaderLayout renders the tab strip and records the exact cell spans it
155	// used, so mouse hit testing cannot drift from responsive labels or styles.
156	func (m Model) buildHeaderLayout() headerLayout {
157		build := func(compact, summary bool) headerLayout {
158			short := map[View]string{
159				ViewTasks: "TSK", ViewRepos: "REP", ViewFleet: "FLT", ViewTries: "TRY",
160				ViewRemote: "REM", ViewSkills: "SKL", ViewMCP: "MCP",

164			builder.WriteString(prefix)
165			x := lipgloss.Width(prefix)
166			hits := make([]tabHit, 0, len(Views))
167			for index, view := range Views {
168				if index > 0 {
169					separator := styleDim.Render("│")
170					builder.WriteString(separator)
171					x += lipgloss.Width(separator)
172				}
173				name := strings.ToUpper(view.String())
174				if compact {
175					name = short[view]
176				}
177				label := name
178				if !compact {
179					label = " " + name + " "
180				}
181				rendered := styleDim.Render(label)
182				if view == m.view {
183					rendered = styleSelected.Render(label)
184				}
185				from := x
186				builder.WriteString(rendered)
187				x += lipgloss.Width(rendered)
188				hits = append(hits, tabHit{view: view, from: from, to: x})
189			}
190			if summary {
191				builder.WriteString("   " + styleDim.Render(m.Summary()))
192			}
193			if m.filter != "" {
194				builder.WriteString("   " + styleWarm.Render("/"+m.filter))
195			}
196			return headerLayout{line: builder.String(), tabs: hits}
197		}
198	
199		layout := build(false, true)
200		if lipgloss.Width(layout.line) > m.width {
201			layout = build(false, false)
202		}
203		if lipgloss.Width(layout.line) > m.width {
204			layout = build(true, false)
205		}
206		if lipgloss.Width(layout.line) <= m.width {
207			return layout
208		}
209	
210		prefix := styleTitle.Render("dev") + "  "
211		name := strings.ToUpper(m.view.String())
212		line := prefix + styleSelected.Render(name)
213		layout = headerLayout{

217		if m.filter != "" {

219			if available > 1 {
220				layout.line += "   " + styleWarm.Render("/"+pad(m.filter, available-1))
221			}
222		}
223		return layout
224	}

230	// window returns the slice of a list visible around the cursor, and the offset
231	// it starts at, so a long inventory scrolls instead of overflowing.
232	func (m Model) window(n int) (from, to int) {
233		h := m.listHeight()
234		if n <= h {
235			return 0, n
236		}
237		from = m.at() - h/2
238		if from < 0 {
239			from = 0
240		}
241		if from+h > n {
242			from = n - h
243		}
244		return from, from + h
245	}

1466	func (m Model) renderFooter() string {
1467		viewErr, viewStatus := m.viewError(m.view), m.viewStatus(m.view)
1468		var status string
1469		switch {
1470		case m.err != nil:
1471			status = styleErr.Render("✗ " + m.err.Error())
1472		case m.remoteClone.active():
1473			status = styleLive.Render(m.remoteCloneSpinner.View() + " " + m.remoteCloneStatus())
1474		case viewErr != nil:
1475			status = styleErr.Render("✗ " + viewErr.Error())
1476		case m.status != "":
1477			status = styleOK.Render("✓ " + m.status)
1478		case viewStatus != "":
1479			status = styleOK.Render("✓ " + viewStatus)
1480		}
1481	
1482		var bindings []string
1483		if m.remoteClone.active() {
1484			bindings = []string{"q cancel clone", "tab view", "/ filter", "j/k move"}
1485			var b strings.Builder
1486			if status != "" {
1487				b.WriteString("  " + status + "\n")
1488			}
1489			b.WriteString("  " + styleHelp.Render(wrapBindings(bindings, m.width-4)))
1490			return b.String()
1491		}
1492		switch m.view {
1493		case ViewRepos:
1494			sortBy := m.actions.RepoSort
1495			if sortBy == "" {
1496				sortBy = "activity"
1497			}
1498			if m.actions.RepoReverse {
1499				sortBy += "↑"
1500			}
1501			if item, ok := m.currentRepoItem(); ok && item.child() {
1502				bindings = append(bindings, "enter open worktree", "space collapse")
1503			} else {
1504				bindings = append(bindings, "enter ad hoc", "space worktrees", "m metadata", "n add note", "N notes", "s worktree task", "d direct task")
1505			}
1506			bindings = append(bindings, "O sort:"+sortBy, "R reverse")
1507		case ViewFleet:

19	// listHeight budgets rows from what the current detail and footer actually
20	// render. REPOS has more detail and more key hints than TASKS; the old fixed
21	// chrome allowance let the complete view exceed terminal height, so Bubble
22	// Tea scrolled the first lines and the top tab bar appeared to disappear.
23	func (m Model) listHeight() int {
24		// Header + its blank line, per-view list preamble, blank before detail,
25		// blank before footer. Detail and footer can each wrap/change by view and
26		// terminal width.
27		fixed := 2 + m.listPreambleLines() + 1 + lineCount(m.renderDetail()) + 1 + lineCount(m.renderFooter())
28		h := m.height - fixed
29		if h < 3 {
30			return 3
31		}
32		// A long list adds the "… x–y of n" scroll note.
33		if m.count() > h && h > 3 {
34			h--
35		}
36		return h
37	}

39	func (m Model) listPreambleLines() int {
40		lines := 1 // the table header, or the one-line empty/loading state
41		switch m.view {
42		case ViewRemote:
43			if m.viewLoad(ViewRemote).loading && len(m.visibleRemotes()) > 0 {
44				lines++
45			}
46		case ViewSkills:
47			if m.viewLoad(ViewSkills).loading && len(m.visibleSkills()) > 0 {
48				lines++
49			}
50		case ViewMCP:
51			if m.viewLoad(ViewMCP).loading && len(m.visibleMCP()) > 0 {
52				lines++
53			}
54		}
55		return lines
56	}

58	func lineCount(s string) int {
59		s = strings.TrimRight(s, "\n")

62		}

64	}

1499			case x < y:

1517			}
1518			if a.LastActivity.After(b.LastActivity) {
1519				return -1
1520			}
1521			return 1
1522		}
1523	
1524		switch sortBy {
1525		case "name":
1526			return nameCmp
1527		case "latest":
1528			if c := latest(); c != 0 {
1529				return c
1530			}
1531		case "git":
1532			if c := descBool(a.Status.Dirty(), b.Status.Dirty()); c != 0 {
1533				return c
1534			}
1535			if c := descInt(a.Status.Changed, b.Status.Changed); c != 0 {

1538		case "size":
1539			switch {
1540			case a.Usage != nil && b.Usage == nil:
1541				return -1
1542			case a.Usage == nil && b.Usage != nil:
1543				return 1
1544			case a.Usage != nil && b.Usage != nil && a.Usage.OwnedBytes > b.Usage.OwnedBytes:
1545				return -1
1546			case a.Usage != nil && b.Usage != nil && a.Usage.OwnedBytes < b.Usage.OwnedBytes:
1547				return 1
1548			}
1549		case "tasks":

1551				return c
1552			}
1553			if c := descInt(len(a.Tasks), len(b.Tasks)); c != 0 {

3743			if !m.viewUsesRepos(view) {
3744				continue
3745			}

3748				m.beginViewLoad(view, loadRefresh)
3749				if fresh {
3750					m.setViewStatus(view, dependentLoadingStatus(view))
3751					commands = append(commands, m.reloadDependentView(view))
3752					continue
3753				}
3754				dependencyErr := err

3761			}
3762			if state.hasSnapshot {
3763				m.invalidateView(view)
3764			}
3765		}
3766		return batchCommands(commands...)
3767	}

4046	func (m Model) launchTool(key string) tea.Cmd {
4047		for _, t := range m.actions.Tools {
4048			if t.Key != key {
4049				continue
4050			}
4051			if t.Probe != nil && t.Availability != ToolAvailable {
4052				detail := "availability is still being checked"

4062				return func() tea.Msg {
4063					return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("nothing selected with a checkout on disk")}
4064				}
4065			}
4066			c := exec.Command(t.Command[0], t.Command[1:]...)

4069				if err != nil {
4070					return afterExec(actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", t.Name, err)})
4071				}
4072				return afterExec(actionMsg{status: "back from " + t.Name, forceSizes: true})
4073			})
4074		}
4075		return nil
4076	}

1	package tui
2	
3	import tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
4	
5	const mouseWheelRows = 3
6	
7	// mouseFrameFits fails closed when Bubble Tea would drop top lines from an
8	// over-height frame. Screen-relative mouse coordinates cannot safely target
9	// logical header/list rows once that clipping occurs.
10	func (m Model) mouseFrameFits() bool {
11		if m.height <= 0 {
12			return false
13		}
14		if m.overlay.kind == overlayActionMenu {
15			return lineCount(m.renderOverlay()) <= m.height
16		}
17	
18		n := m.count()
19		listLines := m.listPreambleLines()
20		if n > 0 {
21			visible := min(n, m.listHeight())
22			listLines += visible
23			if visible < n {
24				listLines++
25			}
26		}
27		total := 2 + listLines + 1 + lineCount(m.renderDetail()) + 1 + lineCount(m.renderFooter())
28		return total <= m.height
29	}
30	
31	func (m Model) updateMouse(message tea.MouseMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
32		event := tea.MouseEvent(message)
33		if event.Shift || event.Alt || event.Ctrl {
34			return m, nil
35		}
36		if m.overlay.kind == overlayActionMenu {
37			if !m.mouseFrameFits() {
38				return m, nil
39			}
40			return m.updateActionMenuMouse(event)
41		}
42		if m.noteMode() || m.overlay.kind != overlayNone || m.mode != modeList {
43			return m, nil
44		}
45		if !m.mouseFrameFits() {
46			return m, nil
47		}
48	
49		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
50			if !m.mouseOverList(event.X, event.Y) {
51				return m, nil
52			}
53			delta := mouseWheelRows
54			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
55				delta = -delta
56			}
57			m.setAt(m.at() + delta)
58			return m, nil
59		}
60		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress {
61			return m, nil
62		}
63	
64		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonLeft && event.Y == 0 {
65			for _, hit := range m.buildHeaderLayout().tabs {
66				if event.X < hit.from || event.X >= hit.to {
67					continue
68				}
69				if m.view == hit.view {
70					return m, nil
71				}
72				m.view = hit.view
73				return m.afterViewSwitch()
74			}
75			return m, nil
76		}
77	
78		row, ok := m.mouseRow(event.X, event.Y)
79		if !ok {
80			return m, nil
81		}
82		switch event.Button {
83		case tea.MouseButtonLeft:
84			m.setAt(row)
85		case tea.MouseButtonRight:
86			m.setAt(row)
87			if !m.remoteClone.active() {
88				m = m.openActionMenu()
89			}
90		}
91		return m, nil
92	}
93	
94	func (m Model) mouseRow(x, y int) (int, bool) {
95		if x < 0 || x >= m.width {
96			return 0, false
97		}
98		count := m.count()
99		from, to := m.window(count)
100		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
101		if y < first || y >= first+(to-from) {
102			return 0, false
103		}
104		return from + y - first, true
105	}
106	
107	func (m Model) mouseOverList(x, y int) bool {
108		if x < 0 || x >= m.width || m.count() == 0 {
109			return false
110		}
111		from, to := m.window(m.count())
112		first := 2 + m.listPreambleLines()
113		return y >= 2 && y < first+(to-from)
114	}
115	
116	func (m Model) updateActionMenuMouse(event tea.MouseEvent) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
117		if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
118			if m.overlay.optionCount == 0 {
119				return m, nil
120			}
121			delta := 1
122			if event.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp {
123				delta = -1
124			}
125			m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + delta + m.overlay.optionCount) % m.overlay.optionCount
126			return m, nil
127		}
128		if event.Action != tea.MouseActionPress || event.Button != tea.MouseButtonLeft {
129			return m, nil
130		}
131		first := m.buildActionMenuLayout().firstOptionY
132		if event.Y < first || event.Y >= first+m.overlay.optionCount {
133			m.overlay = overlayState{}
134			return m, nil
135		}
136		m.overlay.optionIndex = event.Y - first
137		return m.runOverlayAction()
138	}

41		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "checkout", row.Checkout)

48		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "source_url", row.SourceURL)
49		lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "update", string(row.UpdateStatus))
50		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")

53	func formatMCPSummary(row agentmcp.Declaration) string {

87			lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "redacted", strings.Join(redactions, ", "))
88		}
89		if len(row.Coverage) > 0 {
90			coverage := make([]string, len(row.Coverage))
91			for i, item := range row.Coverage {
92				coverage[i] = string(item.Code)
93			}
94			lines = appendSummaryLine(lines, "coverage", strings.Join(coverage, ", "))
95		}
96		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
97	}
98	
99	func (m Model) copyBindingHelp() string {
100		if m.view == ViewRepos {
101			return "y context · p path · b branch · s sessions · w worktree paths"
102		}
103		parts := make([]string, 0, 4)
104		if _, err := m.capabilityFilePath(); err == nil {
105			parts = append(parts, "p file path")
106		}
107		parts = append(parts, "s safe summary")
108		if row, ok := m.currentSkill(); ok && row.SourceURL != "" {
109			parts = append(parts, "u source URL")
110		}
111		if _, err := m.capabilityFilePath(); err == nil && m.actions.ReadFile != nil {
112			parts = append(parts, "f raw file")
113		}
114		return strings.Join(parts, " · ")
115	}
116	
117	func appendSummaryLine(lines []string, label, value string) []string {
118		if strings.TrimSpace(value) == "" {
119			return lines
120		}
121		return append(lines, label+": "+value)
122	}

98	// configEditorProcess resolves the effective config and editor without running
99	// it. The CLI runs the process directly; the TUI passes it to tea.ExecProcess,
100	// which suspends the alternate screen and redraws after the editor exits.
101	func configEditorProcess(app *App, editor string) (*exec.Cmd, string, bool, error) {
102		path := app.configPath
103		if path == "" {
104			path = config.ConfigFile()
105		}
106		path = config.Expand(path)
107		created, err := ensureConfigForEdit(path)
108		if err != nil {
109			return nil, "", false, err
110		}
111		proc, chosen, err := editorProcess(path, editor)
112		return proc, chosen, created, err
113	}

115	func prepareTUICapabilityEdit(path string) (tui.CapabilityEdit, error) {
116		logical := filepath.Clean(path)
117		resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(logical)
118		if err != nil {
119			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve capability file %s: %w", config.Contract(logical), err)
120		}
121		source, observed, err := safefile.OpenRegular(resolved)
122		if err != nil {
123			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, fmt.Errorf("open capability file %s: %w", config.Contract(logical), err)
124		}
125		original, readErr := safefile.ReadAll(context.Background(), source, safefile.CompiledMaxFileBytes)
126		closeErr := source.Close()
127		if readErr != nil {
128			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, fmt.Errorf("read capability file %s: %w", config.Contract(logical), readErr)
129		}
130		if closeErr != nil {
131			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, fmt.Errorf("close capability file %s: %w", config.Contract(logical), closeErr)
132		}
133	
134		working, err := os.CreateTemp("", "dev-capability-edit-*")
135		if err != nil {
136			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
137		}
138		workingPath := working.Name()
139		cleanup := true
140		defer func() {
141			if cleanup {
142				_ = os.Remove(workingPath)
143			}
144		}()
145		if _, err := working.Write(original); err != nil {
146			_ = working.Close()
147			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
148		}
149		if err := working.Sync(); err != nil {
150			_ = working.Close()
151			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
152		}
153		if err := working.Close(); err != nil {
154			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
155		}
156		process, _, err := editorProcess(workingPath, "")
157		if err != nil {
158			return tui.CapabilityEdit{}, err
159		}
160		cleanup = false
161	
162		return tui.CapabilityEdit{
163			Command: process,
164			Complete: func(runErr error) error {
165				if runErr != nil {
166					_ = os.Remove(workingPath)
167					return runErr
168				}
169				edited, err := safefile.ReadRegular(context.Background(), workingPath, safefile.CompiledMaxFileBytes)
170				if err != nil {
171					return fmt.Errorf("read edited capability file; working copy preserved at %s: %w", config.Contract(workingPath), err)
172				}
173				if bytes.Equal(edited, original) {
174					return os.Remove(workingPath)
175				}
176				root, err := os.OpenRoot(filepath.Dir(resolved))
177				if err != nil {
178					return fmt.Errorf("open capability file directory; working copy preserved at %s: %w", config.Contract(workingPath), err)
179				}
180				defer root.Close()
181				if _, err := safefile.AtomicReplace(
182					context.Background(), root, filepath.Base(resolved), observed, edited, observed.Mode().Perm(),
183				); err != nil {
184					return fmt.Errorf("replace changed capability file; working copy preserved at %s: %w", config.Contract(workingPath), err)
185				}
186				return os.Remove(workingPath)
187			},
188		}, nil
189	}

191	// ensureConfigForEdit generates a usable config before opening an absent path.
192	// Editing an empty file would hide every default the user is trying to change.
193	func ensureConfigForEdit(path string) (bool, error) {
194		info, err := os.Stat(path)
195		switch {
196		case err == nil && info.IsDir():
197			return false, fmt.Errorf("%s is a directory, not a config file", config.Contract(path))
198		case err == nil:
199			return false, nil
200		case !os.IsNotExist(err):
201			return false, err
202		}
203		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
204			return false, err
205		}
206		body := renderStarterConfig(config.DetectLayout().Fallbacks())
207		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o644); err != nil {
208			return false, err
209		}
210		return true, nil
211	}
212	
213	func editorProcess(path, override string) (*exec.Cmd, string, error) {
214		chosen, err := resolveEditor(override)
215		if err != nil {
216			return nil, "", err
217		}
218		command, err := fleetEditorCommand(chosen, path)
219		return command, chosen, err
220	}
221	
222	func resolveEditor(override string) (string, error) {
223		for _, candidate := range []string{override, os.Getenv("VISUAL"), os.Getenv("EDITOR")} {
224			if strings.TrimSpace(candidate) != "" {
225				return candidate, nil
226			}
227		}
228		for _, candidate := range []string{"nvim", "vim", "vi"} {
229			if _, err := exec.LookPath(candidate); err == nil {
230				return candidate, nil
231			}
232		}
233		return "", fmt.Errorf("no editor found; set $VISUAL or $EDITOR, or pass --editor")
234	}

659				for _, value := range totals {
660					seconds += value
661					if value > 0 {
662						days++
663					}
664				}
665				return tui.StatsPanel{
666					Repo: repoName, Seconds: seconds, ActiveDays: days,
667					Since: since, Until: until,
668					Heatmap: stats.Heatmap(totals, stats.HeatmapOptions{
669						Since: since, Until: until, Legend: true, WeekdayLabels: true,
670					}),
671				}, nil
672			},

674			BackfillStats: func(ctx context.Context, repoName string) error {
675				active := appState.Current()
676				r, _, err := repo.Resolve(ctx, active.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repoName)
677				if err != nil {
678					return err
679				}
680				store, err := stats.Open(stats.Path(active.Cfg.StateDir()))
681				if err != nil {
682					return err
683				}
684				defer store.Close()
685				_, err = stats.BackfillGit(ctx, store, []repo.Repo{r}, time.Now().AddDate(-1, 0, 0), "")
686				return err
687			},
688	
689			EditConfig: func() (*exec.Cmd, error) {
690				proc, _, _, err := configEditorProcess(appState.Current(), "")
691				return proc, err
692			},
693	
694			EditFleetConfig: func() (*exec.Cmd, error) {
695				return fleetConfigEditorProcess(appState.Current(), "")
696			},
697	
698			// loadFleetConfig applies defaults and re-runs the private-mode check,
699			// so an edit that loosens remotes.toml's permissions while it holds a
700			// plaintext password is caught here rather than at the next fan-out.
701			ValidateFleetConfig: func() error {
702				_, err := loadFleetConfig(appState.Current())

706			ReloadConfig: func(ctx context.Context) (tui.ConfigUpdate, string, error) {
707				currentRuntime, err := runtimeResolver.Resolve(ctx)
708				if err != nil {
709					return tui.ConfigUpdate{}, "", err
710				}
711				oldRuntime := currentRuntime.Name()
712				next, err := appState.Prepare(ctx)
713				if err != nil {
714					return tui.ConfigUpdate{}, "", err
715				}
716				status := "config + data reloaded"
717				if nextRuntime := next.Runtime().Name(); nextRuntime != oldRuntime {
718					status += fmt.Sprintf("; restart TUI to switch runtime %s → %s", oldRuntime, nextRuntime)
719				}
720				return tui.ConfigUpdate{
721					Apply:       func() { appState.Commit(next) },
722					Tools:       externalTools(next),
723					RepoColumns: next.Cfg.EffectiveRepoColumns(),
724					RepoSort:    next.Cfg.EffectiveRepoSort(),
725					RepoReverse: next.Cfg.TUI.Repos.Reverse,
726				}, status, nil
727			},
728		}
729	
730		// Enter the alternate screen immediately. Local inventory is loaded by
731		// Init in the background rather than making the terminal appear frozen
732		// while dozens of repos are probed.
733		model := tui.New(actions, nil, nil).WithTrace(app.trace).WithContext(runCtx).BeginLoading()
734		finishSetup(perftrace.OutcomeSuccess)
735		app.trace.Mark(perftrace.TUIProgramRunBegin, perftrace.Fields{})
736		final, err := tea.NewProgram(model, tea.WithAltScreen(), tea.WithMouseCellMotion()).Run()
737		cancelRun()
738		app.finishTrace()
739		if err != nil {
740			return err
741		}
742		// A directory choice can only be honoured once the alternate screen is
743		// torn down, and only by the shell wrapper.
744		if m, ok := final.(tui.Model); ok {
745			if dir := m.Chosen(); dir != "" {
746				return app.cdDirective(dir)
747			}
748			if handle := m.Activation(); handle != "" {
749				rt, resolveErr := runtimeResolver.Resolve(ctxOf())
750				if resolveErr != nil {
751					return resolveErr
752				}
753				return activateRuntime(ctxOf(), rt, handle)
754			}
755		}
756		return nil
757	}
